entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Id
entries.docstring:
An identifier of a row of kind `k`: the textual UUID the database minted, tagged with its
kind. The model never inspects the text beyond equality; `Uuid.isCanonical` states its shape.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.IdKind
entries.docstring:
The kinds of row an identifier can name: one per table whose primary key is `id uuid`.
`connector` is the `mcp_servers` table; `principal` is `workspace_principals`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.JValue
entries.docstring:
A JSON value: `null`, a boolean, an exact decimal number `mantissa · 10⁻ᵉˣᵖᵒⁿᵉⁿᵗ`, a string, an
array, or an object as an ordered list of fields.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.ProjectConnectorKey
entries.docstring: `project_mcp_servers` is keyed by `(project_id, mcp_server_id)`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.ProjectFileKey
entries.docstring: `project_files` is keyed by `(project_id, file_id)`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.RunEventKey
entries.docstring: `run_events` is keyed by `(run_id, sequence)` (`run_events_pkey`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.SessionMessageKey
entries.docstring: `session_messages` adds the message `sequence` to its transcript's key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.SessionTranscriptKey
entries.docstring:
`session_transcripts` is keyed by `(workspace_id, project_key, session_id, subpath)`; the
empty `subpath` is the main transcript.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunStatus
entries.docstring:
The run lifecycle as the API reports it: `queued` and `running` are live, the other three are
terminal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.failAccounting
entries.docstring: The repository writes `failed` only while accounting is pending.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.priceFirstResponse
entries.docstring:
A late price for the first, previously unpriced response updates that ledger row without
inserting another response or adding its token counters again.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.priceVersionConflict
entries.docstring:
Two different priced catalogue versions conflict; an unpriced arrival has no version
opinion and cannot conflict with an earlier priced response.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.recordAccounting
entries.docstring:
A successful record insert or duplicate response: only a new response appends to the ledger.
`priced` is whether that response has a price table version.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.runAction
entries.docstring:
One store/control-plane operation. An append is allowed until `finish` closes the log.
The repository revokes gateway run tokens in the same transaction as terminal `finish`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.runStep
entries.docstring: One operation on a run whose current status is `current`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Text.isJsWhitespace
entries.docstring:
The ECMAScript *WhiteSpace* and *LineTerminator* code points: what `trim` removes and what
`\s` matches.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Text.utf16Length
entries.docstring: `String.prototype.length`: the number of UTF-16 code units.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Uuid.isCanonical
entries.docstring:
`isUuid`: the RFC 9562 canonical textual form, any version, either case
(`UUID_PATTERN = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-…-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Decision
entries.docstring:
`Decision`: `allow` and `deny` are decisions; `refuse` is the absence of one. A `deny` whose
`scopeDenial` is set carries the code `token_out_of_scope`; otherwise the renderer's default
`forbidden`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership
entries.docstring: `Ownership`: whose row is being acted on, as far as the handler could tell.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Query
entries.docstring:
`AuthorisationQuery`. The role is the raw runtime value; `scope` is `null` for every
credential but a browser token.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.applyGrant
entries.docstring: `applyGrant`: whether a grant of this width admits a row of this ownership.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideAuth
entries.docstring: `decide`: a dedicated revoke capability precedes the ordinary operation table.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.declaredRoutes
entries.docstring: The declared route union (155 routes).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.matrixIdentityOnlyRoutes
entries.docstring: `IDENTITY_ONLY_ROUTES`: the identity-proof route the matrix exempts.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.matrixPublicRoutes
entries.docstring: `PUBLIC_ROUTES`: the pre-authentication routes the matrix exempts.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.methods
entries.docstring: `METHODS`: the methods a Next.js route handler may export, in `decide.ts` order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.parseOperation
entries.docstring: `parseOperation`: a method and a sub-resource, as an operation.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.parsePath
entries.docstring: `parsePath`: `/api/<resource>`, `/api/<resource>/:id`, `/api/<resource>/:id/<sub>`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.revokeTokensRoleGate
entries.docstring:
The role predicate of the dedicated revoke decision: after the scope refusal, only `owner`
and `admin` pass (`403 run_token_revoke_forbidden` otherwise).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grant
entries.docstring: `Grant`: how wide a permission is.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grants
entries.docstring: `Grants`: the three operations' grants for one (role, resource) pair.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Operation
entries.docstring: `Operation`: what a caller is trying to do to a resource.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.docRow
entries.docstring:
§3.3's rows: the (Owner, Admin, Builder, Viewer) phrases for each resource the table names;
`none` for the four resources it does not name (`endpoint-clients`, `me`, `setup`,
`tool-bundles`). The "audit" of
"metrics, audit" is `audit-events`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.grantsFor
entries.docstring: `grantsFor`: the override for the resource if the role names it, else the fallback.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.grantsForW9Auth165
entries.docstring: `POLICY` as ADR W9-AUTH-165's decision text describes it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.policy
entries.docstring: `POLICY`, role by role, in the order and with the constants `permissions.ts` uses.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.Resource
entries.docstring: `RESOURCES`: the 29 top-level resources, in the `as const` order of `resources.ts`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.composeSubResources
entries.docstring:
`composeSubResources`: the base table plus the declarations; `error d` is the throw naming
the first duplicate declaration.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.declaredSubResources
entries.docstring:
`DECLARED_SUB_RESOURCES`: every declaration, in the import order of
`declared-sub-resources.ts` and, within a file, the file's order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.parseResource
entries.docstring: `parseResource`: a resource, or `none` for any segment that is not exactly one spelling.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.parseSub
entries.docstring: `parseSub`: the segment, when it is one `subResources` classifies under `resource`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.spec34SubResources
entries.docstring: `SPEC_34_SUB_RESOURCES`: the three pairs spec §34 prints.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.subResources
entries.docstring:
`SUB_RESOURCES`, as `permissions.ts` composes it (the empty table if the composition threw,
which the theorems show it does not).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Roles.parseRoleInput
entries.docstring: `parseRole` at `decide()`'s first step: the role, or `none` (then `decide()` refuses).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Roles.roles
entries.docstring: `ROLES`, in the order `roles.ts` lists them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.Surface
entries.docstring: `Surface`: the three surfaces of spec §34.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.candidateForms
entries.docstring: `candidateForms`: every reading of the pathname, or `none` when it cannot be read.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.classifyPath
entries.docstring: `classifyPath`: the surface of a pathname.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.decodeURIComponent
entries.docstring: `decodeURIComponent`: `none` where JavaScript throws `URIError`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.isUnder
entries.docstring: `isUnder`: the prefix itself, or anything below it (`/apiary` is not under `/api`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.maxDecodeRounds
entries.docstring: `MAX_DECODE_ROUNDS`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.removeDotSegments
entries.docstring: `removeDotSegments`: RFC 3986 §5.2.4 plus duplicate-slash collapse and trailing-slash removal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.KeyRule
entries.docstring:
`key-safety.ts`'s named rules. `percentEncoded` stands for every rejection of a key that
contains `%`: such a key is never accepted (it either fails to decode, `malformed-encoding`, or is
not its own decoding, `non-canonical`, unless its decoded form trips an earlier rule first); the
model does not decode, so it names only that the key is refused.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.RequestPrincipal
entries.docstring:
The request principal (`apps/web/server/rbac/principal.ts#Principal`): who acts, in which
one workspace, with which role, and the browser-token attenuation if any.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ResolverOutcome
entries.docstring: An `OwnershipOutcome`: the ownership `decide()` should see, or a refusal to return as is.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ScopeValue
entries.docstring:
A value handed to `requireWorkspaceScope(value: unknown)`: a scope a resolver minted, or one
of the two forgeries the compiler admits (`{ workspaceId } as WorkspaceScope`, and
`Object.create(WorkspaceScope.prototype)` with a `workspaceId`), or not an object at all. A
minted scope is frozen, so it cannot be tampered with in place (`Object.assign` throws).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.Via
entries.docstring: How a principal was authenticated (`Via`, in `principal.ts` order).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.WorkspaceScope
entries.docstring: A `WorkspaceScope`: the `workspaces.id` every repository `where` clause is built from.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.apiKeyNotPermitted
entries.docstring: `apiKeyRefusal`: `403 api_key_not_permitted`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.authenticateApiKey
entries.docstring:
`authenticateApiKeyHash`: the key with that hash joined to its principal
(`workspace_principals.(workspace_id, api_key_id) = api_keys.(workspace_id, id)`), neither revoked,
the key unexpired.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.authoriseFlow
entries.docstring:
`authorise(request, ownership, run)` with a resolver: unconfigured is 503, no principal 401,
a refusing resolver's result is returned **without calling `decide()`**, then `decide()`'s allow,
deny (403, `decision.code ?? 'forbidden'`) or refuse (500).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.containsReservedMarker
entries.docstring: `containsReservedMarker(segment)`: the marker occurs in the folded segment.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.dbStoreGet
entries.docstring: The database store's `get`: resolve the workspace, then read through the scoped repository.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.findRunForPrincipal
entries.docstring:
`findRunForPrincipal`: the run, only if it belongs to the principal's workspace; `null` for
"no such run" and "not yours" alike.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.findRunWorkspace
entries.docstring:
`findRunWorkspace(db, runId)`: the one query keyed by run id alone; a workspace id and no row
content.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.forWorkspaceId
entries.docstring:
`WorkspaceScope.databaseResolver(db).forWorkspaceId`: the first `workspaces` row with that id,
or `null`. The scope carries the row's id, never the caller's argument.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.forWorkspaceSlug
entries.docstring: `databaseResolver(db).forWorkspaceSlug`: the workspace a session token's slug names.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.fromApiKey
entries.docstring: `Principal.fromApiKey`: the key's workspace, fixed.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.fromBrowserToken
entries.docstring: `Principal.fromBrowserToken`: the minter's identity and workspace, with the token's scope.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.fromDirectoryRecord
entries.docstring: `Principal.fromDirectoryRecord`: the minter's current identity, unattenuated.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.fromSession
entries.docstring:
`Principal.fromSession`: refuse a workspace whose slug is not the verified session's, refuse
a blank identity, otherwise a `session` principal of that workspace's id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.getForMember
entries.docstring:
`getForMember(id, userId)`: the caller's role there, `null` for a missing workspace and for
one the caller does not belong to, indistinguishably.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.identifySessionCurrent
entries.docstring:
The session branch of `resolveActor` (`session-rbac.ts`), after the cookie verified: resolve
the membership by `(claims.sub, claims.ws)`, then build the principal with the slug **copied from
the claims** (`{ id: member.workspaceId, slug: verified.claims.ws }`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.inMemoryForId
entries.docstring: `inMemoryResolver(known).forWorkspaceId`: `byId.set(row.id, row.id)`, so any known id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.inMemoryForSlug
entries.docstring:
`inMemoryResolver(known).forWorkspaceSlug`: `bySlug.set(row.slug, row.id)`, where a later row
with the same slug overwrites an earlier one (`Map.set`), so the last match wins.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.isWorkspaceScope
entries.docstring:
`WorkspaceScope.isWorkspaceScope`: the `#private` brand is present (only the class's own
constructor adds it) and the frozen instance is unchanged.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.keyGuard
entries.docstring:
`evaluateRelativePath(raw, allowRoot)`: the input itself (the guard filters, it never
rewrites) or the first rule it trips. Exact for keys without `%`; a key with `%` is refused.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.leadingIndexedColumns
entries.docstring:
`leadingIndexedColumns(table)`: every column that leads an index (unique or not) or a unique
constraint, as a set, transcribed from the Drizzle schema (the latest snapshot, `Er.Snapshot.file`);
`tests/formal/authz-tenancy.test.ts` recomputes it from the live table objects. This is the one
fact rule 1 needs that `Er.Core.TableSpec` does not carry (it models unique keys only).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.memberResolver
entries.docstring: `memberOwnershipResolver`: `own` for any current membership, the concealed 404 otherwise.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.metadataMarker
entries.docstring: `OBJECT_METADATA_MARKER`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.objectWorkspaceIdCurrent
entries.docstring: The workspace ids `createScopedObjectStore` accepts today: any non-blank string.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.objectWorkspaceIdTarget
entries.docstring:
The intended acceptance: a non-blank id that is one key segment, so the prefix names one
workspace (the module's header: "every key it sees is prefixed to one workspace").

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ownerResolver
entries.docstring: `ownerOwnershipResolver`: `own` only for an Owner, `other` for a lesser member.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.principalById
entries.docstring:
`principalById(workspaceId, principalId)`: an unrevoked principal of that workspace, with the
role and label of its membership (and user) or of its live API key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.requireWorkspaceScope
entries.docstring: `requireWorkspaceScope`: the scope, or `ForgedWorkspaceScopeError` (`none`) before any query.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.resolveBrowserToken
entries.docstring:
`resolveBrowserTokenActor` (`session-rbac.ts`): the active token by hash, its workspace's
scope, the scoped run (not terminal) or session (not archived), and the minter re-read from the
directory in the token's workspace, attenuated by the token's scope.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.resolveMemberUserId
entries.docstring:
`resolveMemberUserId(memberships, actor)`: the first member whose normalised email is the
actor's, never a fallback.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.resolveMembership
entries.docstring:
`root.resolveMembership(email, workspaceSlug)`: the workspace named by the slug, the user named
by the email, their membership, and its unrevoked membership principal; `null` unless all four
rows exist.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.resolveMembershipView
entries.docstring:
`resolveMembershipView`: malformed id, API-key caller, vanished membership, not a member.
Returns the caller's role in workspace `id` or the outcome to return at once.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.runNotFound
entries.docstring: The one 404 every run route answers for a missing or foreign run.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.runPreflight
entries.docstring:
What each run route answers before it reads the store (the environment is installed and the
caller authenticated): `revokeRunTokens` refuses a scope, then a role other than owner and admin,
then a malformed id; the other three refuse a malformed id (no resume cursor is sent).

entries.statement: {α : Type} → AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.RunRoute → AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State → AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.RunCaller → String → (AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row → Except AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.RunProblem α) → Except AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.RunProblem α
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.runRoute
entries.docstring:
A run route, up to and including the lookup: the preflight, then `findRunForPrincipal`'s 404,
then the rest of the handler `k`, which only ever sees a run of the caller's workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedObjectOp
entries.docstring:
`createScopedObjectStore(backend, ws)` followed by one call, under a workspace-id acceptance
rule: `objectWorkspaceIdCurrent` is today's, `objectWorkspaceIdTarget` the intended one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedSelect
entries.docstring: `SELECT … WHERE workspace_id = scope.workspaceId AND p`: a repository's read.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.sdkProjectDirName
entries.docstring: `SDK_PROJECT_DIR_NAME = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.sdkWindowsDeviceName
entries.docstring: `SDK_WINDOWS_DEVICE_NAME = /^(?:con|prn|aux|nul|com[0-9]|lpt[0-9])$/i`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.stmtInWorkspace
entries.docstring:
A write statement stays inside workspace `ws`: it touches a tenant-scoped table, and every row
it inserts, deletes or replaces (old and new) belongs to `ws`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.storeGet
entries.docstring: `RunStore.get(runId)` (the in-memory store keys by id alone): the run row with that id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.testRule1
entries.docstring:
Rule 1 of `tenancy.test.ts` ("the table is scoped"), as the test states it: an exempt table
(the root or a global table, `TENANT_EXEMPT`) has no `workspace_id`; any other has a `NOT NULL`
`workspace_id`, exactly one foreign key whose whole column list is `workspace_id`, that key
references `workspaces(id)`, and `workspace_id` leads an index.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.validateTenantSessionScope
entries.docstring:
`validateTenantSessionScope(input)`: an object with a non-blank string `configDir` and a
string `projectKey` the SDK's own validator accepts and that names no Windows device.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.workspaceKeyPrefix
entries.docstring: `workspaceKeyPrefix(workspaceId)`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.workspaceNotFound
entries.docstring: `workspaceNotFound()`: the one 404 of the workspace routes.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.Scope → AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.Resource → AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Operation → Option String → Option String → Option AgentWorkspace.Authz.TokenScope.ScopeDenial
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.TokenScope.checkTokenScope
entries.docstring: `checkTokenScope`: `some d` denies with `token_out_of_scope`; `none` defers to §21's table.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.TokenScope.documentedScopeRoutes
entries.docstring:
§3.1.1's grammar table as the document prints it, route by route: (scope, method, path).
Transcribed independently of `grammar`; `Normative.AuthzDecide` proves the two agree.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.TokenScope.grammar
entries.docstring:
`TOKEN_SCOPE_GRAMMAR`: the route shapes, as `(resource, operation, sub-resource)` cells, a kind
may reach. A `none` sub-resource matches any sub-resource (see `inGrammar`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.mintAfterOpen
entries.docstring:
`createSurfaceSession`'s open → mint step: `mayOpenSession` first, then the route's other
refusals (`admitted`: the mode it serves and the rate limit), then `runtime.open`, which names the
session it opened or none (gone, not offered, not resumable, refused). A token is minted, scoped to
that one session, only when every step lets it through.

entries.statement: Bool → Bool → List String → Option String → AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.OpenMode → AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.OpenVerdict
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.openVerdict
entries.docstring:
`mayOpenSession`: the loopback branch first (its same-origin condition only for `session`),
then the allowed-origin branch, where a cross-origin `Origin` must equal a listed one exactly.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.sessionScopeMatch
entries.docstring:
`requireSessionScopeMatch`: `true` when the request may go on. Any principal without a session
scope passes; a session scope passes only for the session it names (`none`: a turn's body named no
session, which is refused like a different one).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.visitorDecision
entries.docstring: The scope grammar, then the session match: either refusal is `403 token_out_of_scope`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.EngineImageMap
entries.docstring: The configured map, as an association list from engine id to image reference.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.catalogue
entries.docstring: `registeredEngines`: every registered engine, with `installed` read from the map.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.controlPlane
entries.docstring:
`readConfiguredEngineImages`: the control plane checks each value's shape and **never its
digest**, in production or out — it never starts a container and reads the map only to answer
`installed` and the `422` (ADR-0073 D5). Outside production an environment that configures no
engine at all gets {@link developmentImages}.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.create
entries.docstring:
`create()` of every image-taking driver: resolve the image of the run's engine first, and
create nothing when there is none. The driver does not change the decision — all three call
`requireEngineImage` before their first side effect.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.createInPool
entries.docstring: `create()` of the ACA session pool, which holds exactly one image for one engine.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.envName
entries.docstring: `engineImageEnvName`: `AGENT_WORKSPACE_RUNTIME_IMAGE_` and the id upper-cased, `-` as `_`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.installed
entries.docstring: ENG-02's `installed`, since ENG-07: the map holds an image for the engine.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.parse
entries.docstring: `parseEngineImageMap`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.readEnv
entries.docstring: `readEngineImageMap`: read only the published engines' variables, then parse.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.runnerManager
entries.docstring:
`engineImagesFor`: the runner manager, which starts sandboxes from the map, is where the digest
rule lives — digests are required in production — and a manager with no image at all refuses to
start, with a refusal that names no key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.startRun
entries.docstring:
`startRun`, after the session's engine is pinned: refuse an engine with no image before
`store.create`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.AssignmentCapabilities
entries.docstring:
What one engine can honour of the three demandable resources: the `mcp`, `skills` and
`subagents` fields of `EngineCapabilitiesSchema`, and nothing else from it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.AssignmentDemand
entries.docstring:
What one agent would make its engine honour: whether it is assigned a connector, whether a run
of it would materialise a skill, and whether its version body names a subagent.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict
entries.docstring: What `PUT /api/agents/:id/policy` and the one-call create answer about the engine.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchState
entries.docstring: The state a run-create decision reads and writes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict
entries.docstring: What `startRun` answers about the engine.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict
entries.docstring:
What `parsePolicyBody` answers. Every arm is a `400`; they are told apart because each names a
different thing the client can fix.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.RunRow
entries.docstring: One `runs` row, in the cell this decision writes: the engine that executed the run.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.claudeAssignmentCapabilities
entries.docstring:
`claude-agent-sdk`'s three demandable capabilities, as `apps/web/server/engines/registry.ts`
states them: connectors and skills are honoured; subagents are not yet, like every engine in the
catalogue, which declares `subagents: false` until a run can delegate to one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.enginePaired
entries.docstring:
The release invariant, as a predicate on one row: a session that has an engine session id
names the engine that produced it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migratePolicy
entries.docstring:
The jsonb rewrite of migration 0025, per document.

`(policy - 'provider') || jsonb_build_object('engine', policy ->> 'provider')`, and its `WHERE`:
a document that already states `engine` is left alone, which is what makes the migration
re-runnable, and a document stating neither key is left for a reader to find rather than given an
invented engine.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migrateSession
entries.docstring:
The backfill of migration 0025: every session that already has an identity names the engine
that reported it; a session with no identity is left unpinned.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy
entries.docstring:
`parsePolicyBody`: the three named refusals, then the union.

`accept` stands for the Zod union's own verdict on a body that has cleared the two engine checks;
the replay suite supplies the real `AgentPolicySchema` for it, so this function is the *order* of
the decisions and not a second copy of the schema.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.recordIdentity
entries.docstring:
`recordReportedSessionIdentity`: the reported id and the engine that reported it, in one update.
Splitting them would leave a window in the state `enginePaired` denies.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.saveAgent
entries.docstring: The save-time decision itself.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun
entries.docstring:
`POST /api/agents/:id/runs`, in the one dimension this unit decides.

A session with no engine takes the agent's; a session that has one keeps it, and an agent naming a
different engine is refused with the state **unchanged** — the run row is not written and rolled
back, it is never written. The session is never re-pinned: switching a live session to another
engine is a non-goal of the engine programme, because a session's history belongs to the engine that
produced it.

A `created` answer models the code for a **published** engine id only. The code narrows the engine
it records with `publishedEngineId`, which throws for an id outside `ENGINE_IDS` and so writes no
row; the theorems that conclude `created` carry that hypothesis, and the ones about the rows a
refusal leaves hold of a throw as well.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.unsupportedCapability
entries.docstring:
The capability the engine lacks and the agent demands, or `none`.

Connectors are consulted before skills, and skills before subagents, so a refusal names one
capability rather than a set: the caller fixes one thing and a second save answers the next.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.AnthropicFrame
entries.docstring: A frame of an Anthropic Messages response, abstracted to what metering reads.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ChatFrame
entries.docstring: A frame of a Chat Completions response.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ConnectionFamily
entries.docstring: `MODEL_PROVIDERS`: the provider a model connection names.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.Ingress
entries.docstring:
What the application serves: a model route, the tool route, the tool sandbox route or the
endpoint tool sandbox route.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.Measurement
entries.docstring:
What one response's frames measured. `metered` and `completed` are separate because the two
unmetered outcomes settle differently (ADR-0068 D9).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ModelFormat
entries.docstring: The envelope `GET /v1/models` answers in (ADR-0068 D6).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ResponsesFrame
entries.docstring:
A frame of a Responses response. Usage lives only on the terminal snapshot, which also repeats
every output item — hence the identity list.

The frame kinds below are abstract over *which* item type is a tool call: both of the two the
hosted-tool allowlist admits are — a `function` tool invocation arrives as a `function_call` item and
a `custom` one as a `custom_tool_call` item (`usage/responses.ts`'s `FUNCTION_CALL_ITEM_TYPES`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.Route
entries.docstring: The gateway's public routes, as spec §9 prints them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ToolType
entries.docstring:
A declared tool's `type`. `unnamed` is an entry that names no string type at all, which the
closed allowlist refuses rather than assuming it is a function (ADR-0068 D4).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.asksForUnreachableBackground
entries.docstring:
The request asks to be backgrounded on a route that publishes no way to retrieve the result, so
relaying it would spend tokens no route could ever meter (ADR-0068 D4).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.asksForVendorState
entries.docstring:
The request refers to state the vendor holds, which lives outside the
platform's session boundary and outside `session_transcripts`, keyed by an id the platform never
sees (ADR-0068 D10).

Refused on **every relayed dialect**, like the hosted-tool field: the rule is about where the state
lives, not about which route asked for it, so a field the Chat Completions API does not define cannot
become permissible by arriving on that route. It is the relay's rule alone, so `anthropic-messages`
— which is translated, not relayed — keeps the behaviour it had.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.bodyAsksForVendorState
entries.docstring:
Whether a body with these top-level keys asks for vendor-held state: a listed key is present,
whatever its value, so only an absent field does not ask. This is how `Request.vendorState` is
read off a body.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.clientResponseHeaders
entries.docstring: The headers the client sees: the allowlisted subset of what the upstream answered.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.clientVisibleHeaders
entries.docstring:
Upstream response headers the client may see. The response is rebuilt from this list, so
`set-cookie`, an organisation identifier or an upstream credential header cannot reach the caller.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.extractAnthropic
entries.docstring: Metering an Anthropic Messages response.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.extractChat
entries.docstring:
Metering a Chat Completions response: tool calls are the number of distinct
`(choice, index)` pairs, because one call's deltas fragment across many chunks.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.extractResponses
entries.docstring:
Metering a Responses response: tool calls are the number of distinct tool-call item identities
(`function_call` or `custom_tool_call`), so an item reported twice cannot inflate them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ingressDecision
AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ingressDecisionRouteCurrent
entries.docstring: The decision the gateway took before this unit: the two new paths were not routes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.modelListingFormat
entries.docstring:
The envelope follows the **client**, and the connection family is deliberately not an input:
Claude Code reaches the gateway through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on every family, so keying on the
family would answer an Anthropic SDK with a body it cannot parse. `Accept: application/json` is sent
identically by both SDKs and carries no signal, but `anthropic-version` does: the Anthropic SDK sends
it on every request and no OpenAI SDK sends it. `?format=` wins, then `x-gateway-model-format`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.relayedStore
entries.docstring:
`store` as a relayed body carries it: always `false` on both relayed dialects, whatever the
client sent or did not send. `store: true` retains the turn's prompt and completion at the vendor
under an id the platform never sees — the Responses API even defaults to it — so injecting the value
and overwriting a client `true` are one rule rather than two, and it is the same rule on Chat
Completions, whose stored completions are retained even though no field resumes them (ADR-0068 D10).
`anthropic-messages` is translated rather than relayed, so its body is left as the client wrote it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.routeProtocol?
entries.docstring:
The dialect a route speaks, and so which usage extractor meters it. `/v1/models` and
`/v1/messages/count_tokens` carry no model turn, so they are not metered at all.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.settle
entries.docstring:
The two unmetered outcomes, and which dialects each belongs to (ADR-0068 D9). No sixth accounting
state is invented.

A measured response always records. An unmetered one splits on the **protocol**: a relayed OpenAI
dialect records unpriced zeros once the upstream has declared itself finished, because a compatible
upstream that ignores `stream_options.include_usage` genuinely finishes without reporting anything.
On `anthropic-messages` an unmetered response is a settlement failure however it ended — the rule the
gateway had before it spoke three dialects, and deliberately unchanged, since every real Anthropic
response does declare itself finished (`type: "message"`, or `message_stop`) and so would otherwise
have started settling `unavailable` where it used to settle `failed`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.settledAccounting
entries.docstring:
The accounting state a settled row leaves the run in: an unmetered row carries no price, so
the ledger reads `unavailable`; a measured one that priced reads `complete`.

entries.statement: Bool → AgentWorkspace.Authz.RunToken.Verification → Bool → Option AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ToolRun → Option AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ToolConnector → String → String → AgentWorkspace.Authz.RunToken.GatewayDecision
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.toolDecision
AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.upstreamAllowedHeaders
entries.docstring:
Client request headers that may travel upstream, by name. A closed list rather than the
`openai-` prefix it replaces: `openai-organization` and `openai-project` are real OpenAI request
headers, and admitting them would let the caller choose which account on the stored credential
serves and is billed for the turn — the one thing the model connection decides. The caller's run
token lives in `authorization`, which no list admits.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.upstreamHeaders
entries.docstring:
The headers the gateway sends upstream: the substituted credential, `content-type`, and the
allowlisted client headers. Built from scratch, never by editing the client's own collection.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.vendorStateFields
entries.docstring:
The top-level body fields that refer to state held at the model vendor, in the TypeScript
order: a stored response to resume, a conversation, and a stored prompt object, which carries its
own instructions and its own tools (ADR-0068 D10).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.composeWithCeiling
entries.docstring:
`meetRunCeiling` with the connector meet: meet the stored run with the ceiling, then refuse it
when anything is still wider than the ceiling (only an engine or a model can be).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.step
entries.docstring:
One handler step, including the deprecated revoke alias. Unexpected effect failures are
represented as `500 internal_error`; successful stream events after 200 belong to Events/Sse.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Cli.Engines.columns
entries.docstring:
The table columns `engines list` prints. `capabilities` is absent on purpose: ten fields in
one cell is JSON nobody can read across, and `--json` prints the whole descriptor.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Cli.Engines.listCommand
entries.docstring: `aw engines list`: the SDK's answer, unchanged, or nothing when the request was refused.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Cli.Engines.resolveEngineFlag
entries.docstring:
`resolveEngineFlag`. The catalogue is the authority, not `ENGINE_IDS`: a deployment installs
some of what the contracts publish, and naming an engine it has not installed is the mistake this
refusal is about. So the flag resolves only to a descriptor with this id **and** `installed`; one
the catalogue lists as not installed is refused like one it does not list at all.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Cli.Engines.rows
entries.docstring:
The rows one mode prints. Every mode prints every descriptor, in order: a mode chooses the
rendering, never the result set.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Agent
entries.docstring:
One `agents` row, typed. `policyStored` says whether `policy` is non-`NULL` (a `PUT` has
replaced the policy); the policy's content is a Phase-2/3 concern.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions
entries.docstring: Spec §17 Step 4, "What can this agent do?", in the specification's order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.StateCurrent
entries.docstring: Today's lifecycle: an agent row exists (and is deleted outright).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.StateTarget
entries.docstring: The documented target lifecycle: an agent can also be archived instead of deleted (RF-201).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.bounds
entries.docstring:
The HTTP bounds (`AGENT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS_MAX_LENGTH`,
`AGENT_MODEL_MAX_LENGTH`), in JavaScript string code units.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.mutableFields
entries.docstring: `AGENT_MUTABLE_FIELDS`: what `PATCH` accepts and `POST` requires.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.parseInstructions
entries.docstring:
`parseAgentInstructions`: any string, empty included and not trimmed, of at most
`AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS_MAX_LENGTH` code units.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.parseModel
entries.docstring:
`parseAgentModel`: `null` (the workspace default model), or a string, trimmed, not blank, at
most `AGENT_MODEL_MAX_LENGTH` code units after trimming.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.parseName
entries.docstring:
`parseAgentName`: a string, trimmed, not blank, at most `AGENT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` code units
after trimming; the trimmed value, or the one error message.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.permissionKeys
entries.docstring: `AGENT_PERMISSION_KEYS`, in order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.wireFields
entries.docstring:
The keys of `AgentResourceSchema`, in declaration order. The policy and the assignments are
separate resources (`/policy`, `/resources`), and so are the grants (`/grants`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.ApiKey
entries.docstring: An API key, with every column of `api_keys`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.ApiKeyState
entries.docstring: The states of a key at an instant.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.bearerShaped
entries.docstring:
The anchored fixed-length bearer grammar `^<prefix>[A-Za-z0-9_-]{idLen}_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{secLen}$`
that `API_KEY_PATTERN` and `BROWSER_TOKEN_PATTERN` both instantiate. Because `_` is itself a
base64url character, the halves are read at their fixed lengths, never split on `_`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.credentialFields
entries.docstring:
The concept fields that are credential material: the stored hash, and the plaintext that
only the mint response carries (`key`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.displayPrefixShaped
entries.docstring:
`API_KEY_DISPLAY_PREFIX_PATTERN`: a key's displayable head, `ak_live_<22>` — the key id
alone, which a list may show because it "cannot authenticate".

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.idLength
entries.docstring: `API_KEY_ID_LENGTH`: base64url characters of the public half.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.nameMaxLength
entries.docstring: `API_KEY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.prefix_
entries.docstring: `API_KEY_PREFIX`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.presentedShaped
entries.docstring: `API_KEY_PATTERN`: a whole presented key, `ak_live_<22>_<43>`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.resourceFields
entries.docstring: The fields of `ApiKeyResourceSchema`, in declaration order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.secretLength
entries.docstring: `API_KEY_SECRET_LENGTH`: base64url characters of the secret half.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.BrowserToken
entries.docstring: A browser token, with every column of `browser_tokens`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.Scope
entries.docstring: What a browser token may act on: one run or one session, never both, never neither.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.ScopeKind
entries.docstring: `TOKEN_SCOPE_KINDS`: the two shapes a browser token may be scoped to.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.TokenState
entries.docstring: The states of a token at an instant.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.defaultTtlSeconds
entries.docstring: `BROWSER_TOKEN_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.idLength
entries.docstring: `BROWSER_TOKEN_ID_LENGTH`: base64url characters of the public half.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.maxTtlSeconds
entries.docstring: `BROWSER_TOKEN_MAX_TTL_SECONDS`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.minTtlSeconds
entries.docstring: `BROWSER_TOKEN_MIN_TTL_SECONDS`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.prefix_
entries.docstring: `BROWSER_TOKEN_PREFIX`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.presentedShaped
entries.docstring:
`BROWSER_TOKEN_PATTERN` (and `parsePresentedBrowserToken`): a whole presented token,
`awt_live_<22>_<43>`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.scopeOfRow?
entries.docstring:
Read the scope of a `browser_tokens` row: the kind names which id column is set, and the other
must be `NULL`. `none` for any row the XOR check refuses.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.secretLength
entries.docstring: `BROWSER_TOKEN_SECRET_LENGTH`: base64url characters of the secret half.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.ttlAccepted
entries.docstring: A requested TTL the mint request admits: an integer within the bounds.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.AuthType
entries.docstring: `mcpAuthTypes` / `CONNECTOR_AUTH_TYPES`: §8's None / API Key / Bearer Token / OAuth.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Connector
entries.docstring:
One `mcp_servers` row of kind `mcp`, typed. `args` is the `jsonb` string list (`McpArgs`);
the row's `kind` is `mcp` and its `tool_config` is `NULL` (`Er.Current.Catalog.connectorRow`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Kind
entries.docstring: `connectorKinds` / `CONNECTOR_KINDS` (ADR-0113 C15), in their `as const` order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Resource
entries.docstring:
`ConnectorResource`: the connector as every route renders it. The secret reference is
replaced by `hasCredential`; there is no field a credential value could occupy.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.ToolConnector
entries.docstring:
One `mcp_servers` row of a tool kind (ADR-0113 C15), typed: no transport, command, arguments
or URL, `auth_type` `none`, and `toolConfig` the text PostgreSQL renders the `tool_config` `jsonb`
value in (only whether it is an object matters to the checks; the server parses the rest with
the contracts schema). `kind` ranges over every kind so that `valid` can refuse `mcp`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Transport
entries.docstring: `mcpTransports` / `CONNECTOR_TRANSPORTS`, in §8's order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.admit
entries.docstring:
The create-body admission: `connectorKindOfBody` first, then for `mcp` the MCP rule
`parseCreateConnectorBody` (`parseBody`); a tool kind is handed on without reading another field,
and a `kind` naming no connector kind is refused with `kindError` alone. A body that is not a
JSON object takes the MCP rule, which refuses it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.kindError
entries.docstring: `KIND_ERROR`: the one error a create body gets when its `kind` names no connector kind.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.maxNameLength
entries.docstring: `CONNECTOR_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.parseBody
entries.docstring:
`parseCreateConnectorBody`: `none` for a body that is not a JSON object, else the ordered
error list or the parsed input, exactly as the TypeScript computes them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.wireFields
entries.docstring:
The keys of `ConnectorResourceSchema`, in declaration order. The resource also describes the
tool connectors (ADR-0113 C15): `kind` follows `name` and a missing `kind` means `mcp`; the
`openapi` and `postgres` configurations close the object, and `transport` and `authType` are
`null` for the tool kinds.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.wireOptionalFields
entries.docstring:
The keys of `ConnectorResourceSchema` that may be absent from a resource: `kind` (absent
means `mcp`, so an MCP row renders as before the tool kinds) and the per-kind `openapi` and
`postgres` configurations. Every other key of `wireFields` is always present.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.AgentRequirements
entries.docstring:
What one agent needs: the portable concepts its configuration uses, and the wire protocol of
the model connection it was given.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.ComposeResult
entries.docstring:
The outcome of composing an agent with an engine: accepted, or refused naming the portable
concepts the engine does not support. There is no third arm, and in particular no arm that
accepts having dropped something (ADR-0065 D3).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.Engine
entries.docstring:
The engines ADR-0065 D1 names: the reference engine and the four planned ones. No `WireEnum`
instance, because no engine id is on the wire before ENG-02.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.EngineCapabilities
entries.docstring:
What one engine can do: which portable concepts it honours, and which protocols it speaks.
`supports` is a predicate rather than a list so that the statements below quantify over every
engine an adapter could ever describe, not only the five named today.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.PortableConcept
entries.docstring:
The portable core every engine honours or refuses by name (ADR-0065 D4). Anything outside
this list is an engine-native policy arm and is not a requirement any other engine sees.

`subagents` joined the core with ADR-0133 D14: an agent may name subagents, and an engine declares
whether it can run them, so a demand for them is refused by name like any other concept.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.RunBilling
entries.docstring:
What a run knows about its usage: the gateway's ledger rows, and whatever the engine said
about itself. The second field exists so that its irrelevance can be stated.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.SessionRuns
entries.docstring:
The abstract session of ADR-0065 D8: an engine pinned when the session is created, and the
runs launched into it so far.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.WireProtocol
entries.docstring: The HTTP dialect an engine speaks to the gateway (ADR-0065 D1 and D7).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.billed
entries.docstring: The billed usage of a run: the sum over the gateway's ledger, and nothing else.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.compose
entries.docstring:
Compose an agent's portable requirements with an engine's capabilities: accept when the
engine supports every one, otherwise refuse naming those it does not. This is the decision the
control plane takes at agent save and again at run compose (ADR-0065 D3).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.needsTranslation
entries.docstring:
Whether the gateway has to translate for this pairing: only when the engine cannot speak the
connection's own protocol (ADR-0065 D7). An engine that speaks it does, and translation — which
is approximate — is reserved for single-protocol engines.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File
entries.docstring:
One `files` row, typed. `sizeBytes` is the `bigint` column (an integer, so its non-negativity
is a check, not a type); `createdBy` is the legacy human attribution (a `memberships.user_id` of
the same workspace, or `NULL` when an API-key principal created the row); `owner` is the exact
owning principal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.FileKind
entries.docstring: `fileKinds` / `FILE_KINDS`: a node of the tree is one of exactly two things.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.RenameFile
entries.docstring:
What `renameFile` is given: the new path and content fields. Ownership and the legacy
creator are not part of it ("a rename changes the row's path and content metadata, never who owns
or originally created it").

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.deleteFile
entries.docstring:
`deleteFile(path)`: delete the one row at exactly `path`. Unlike `deleteFilesByPrefix`, the
rows under a folder's path are not touched.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.noDotSegments
entries.docstring:
`files_path_no_dot_segments`: `path !~ '(^|/)[.][.]?(/|$)'` — no segment is `.` or `..`, the
two ways a path escapes its own workspace prefix.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.pathShape
entries.docstring:
`files_path_shape`: `^[^/[:cntrl:]]+(/[^/[:cntrl:]]+)*$` — segments separated by single
slashes, each non-empty and free of control characters, with no leading or trailing slash.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.WorkspaceId → AgentWorkspace.FileId → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.PutFile → List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File → List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.putFile
entries.docstring:
`putFile` on one workspace's catalog: an upsert on `(workspace_id, path)`. An existing row at
that path gets the new kind, key, size and content type, and keeps its id, owner and creator
("an upsert at an existing path never transfers it"); otherwise a new row with the fresh id and
the caller as owner is appended.

entries.statement: String → String → List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File → List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameByPrefix
entries.docstring:
`renameFilesByPrefix`: one `UPDATE` of every row whose path is under the prefix (the `WHERE`
is `pathUnderPrefix` on `path`), so each row keeps its id, owner and creator. The `SET` rewrites
`path`, and, for a `file` row, `storage_key` by the same cut: `case when kind = 'file' then
newPrefix || substr(storage_key, char_length(oldPrefix) + 1) else storage_key end`. The key is
cut by the length of the old prefix whatever it holds, so the rewrite is a rename of the key only
when the key starts with the old prefix (the app writes `storage_key = path`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameFile
entries.docstring:
`renameFile(path, input)`: one `UPDATE files SET input WHERE workspace_id = … AND path = …`.
The row keeps its id, workspace, owner and creator.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renamePath
entries.docstring:
`renameFilesByPrefix` on one path: replace the leading `oldPrefix` by `newPrefix` when the
path lies under it, and leave every other path alone.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.underPrefix
entries.docstring:
`pathUnderPrefix`: `path = prefix` or `path` starts with `prefix` followed by an actual `/`,
never merely the same leading characters.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.wireFields
entries.docstring:
The keys of `FileResourceSchema`, in declaration order: no owner, no creator, and a
modification time the table does not have (it comes from the object store).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.AgentGrant
entries.docstring:
One `agent_grants` row: user `user` (through their membership of `workspace`) may run agent
`agent`. There is no `access` column: "permitted" is binary.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments
entries.docstring: `AgentResourceAssignments`: what `PUT /api/agents/:id/resources` sends and answers.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ConnectorAssignment
entries.docstring: One `agent_mcp_servers` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileAccess
entries.docstring: `fileAccessModes`: §16's "read-only or read-write access".

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileAssignment
entries.docstring: One `agent_files` row: agent `agent` may see file or folder `file` with `access`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ProjectConnectorLink
entries.docstring: One `project_mcp_servers` row, keyed by `(project_id, mcp_server_id)`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ProjectFileLink
entries.docstring: One `project_files` row, keyed by `(project_id, file_id)`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome
entries.docstring: The outcomes of `replace`, `ReplaceAgentResourcesOutcome`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.RunOwnership
entries.docstring:
The answers `resolveAgentRunOwnership` gives (a subset of `decide()`'s `Ownership`; it never
answers `not-applicable`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.SkillAssignment
entries.docstring: One `agent_skills` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.assignmentsBody
entries.docstring:
`AgentResourceAssignmentsSchema.safeParse`: every id non-empty, every access a member of the
closed set, no unknown key; duplicates are *not* refused here (the repository decides them).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.effective
entries.docstring: The read side (`get`): stored file rows re-narrowed by the agent's *current* `writeFiles`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.grantsBody
entries.docstring:
`AgentGrantsSchema`: every id a canonical UUID, lower-cased, and no two equal after
lower-casing; the parsed ids, or `none` when the schema refuses the body.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.grantsRead
entries.docstring: `listPrincipalIds`: the active membership principals whose user holds a grant row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.grantsReplace
entries.docstring:
`replacePrincipalIds`: every requested id must be an active membership principal of this
workspace (else the first that is not is reported); the grant rows are replaced by one row per
requested principal's *user*.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.hasGrant
entries.docstring: `hasGrant(agentId, userId)`: the run-permission check reads the table by user id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.narrow
entries.docstring:
The ceiling an agent's own `writeFiles` permission puts on a file assignment, applied both
when an assignment is written and whenever it is read (issue #133): without `writeFiles`, a
`read-write` assignment is effectively `read`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.readBack
entries.docstring:
What `read(agentId)` returns for the rows just written: files ordered by `file_id`, skills by
`skill_id`, connectors by `mcp_server_id`, each ascending (`orderBy(asc(...))`). A UUID's
canonical lower-case text orders as its bytes, which is PostgreSQL's `uuid` order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace
entries.docstring:
`replace(agentId, requested)` on one workspace: `agent?` is the agent's permissions when the
agent exists in this workspace. File entries are narrowed by `writeFiles`; a repeated file id is
refused (as `unknown-file`, naming the repeat); skill and connector ids are de-duplicated; each
id must name a row of this workspace's catalog, checked files first, then skills, then
connectors; the answer is `read(agentId)` of the rows written, which orders each list by id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.runOwnership
entries.docstring:
`resolveAgentRunOwnership`: `unknown` when the runtime is not configured or the agent cannot
be read, `own` when the caller's principal owns it, `permitted` when an `agent_grants` row names
the caller's user, and `other` otherwise (also when the grants store is not wired or the caller
has no user, as an API-key principal has none).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Invitation.Invitation
entries.docstring: An invitation, with every column of `invitations`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Invitation.InvitationState
entries.docstring: The four states a client shows, in the order the contract lists them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Invitation.credentialFields
entries.docstring:
The credential material of an invitation: the plaintext token (and the link that embeds it),
which only the issue and resend responses carry, and the stored hash.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Invitation.resourceFields
entries.docstring: The fields of `InvitationResourceSchema`, in declaration order: no token, no hash.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Invitation.tokenMaxLength
entries.docstring: `INVITATION_TOKEN_MAX_LENGTH`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Membership
entries.docstring: A membership: one user in one workspace, with one role.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role
entries.docstring: Spec §21's four roles, in `MEMBERSHIP_ROLES` order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.parseRole
entries.docstring:
`parseRole`: a role, or `none` for anything that is not exactly one of the four spellings
(no default, no case folding).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.Config
entries.docstring: A stored config: each field absent or a string.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.ConfigField
entries.docstring: The non-credential settings a connection can carry (`MODEL_CONNECTION_CONFIG_FIELDS`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.ModelChoice
entries.docstring: A model choice: always a connection and a provider-side model id together.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.ModelConnection
entries.docstring: One `model_connections` row as the concept knows it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.Provider
entries.docstring:
The model providers (`modelProviders` in the schema, `MODEL_PROVIDERS` on the wire), in the
`as const` order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.Readiness
entries.docstring: The derived readiness of a connection.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.Resource
entries.docstring: `ModelConnectionResourceSchema`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.apiKeyAccepted
entries.docstring: The value rule for `apiKey` on create: any non-empty string; a key made of spaces is accepted.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.configAccepted
entries.docstring:
`parseProviderConfig`'s key rule, for a config whose present fields all carry a non-empty,
reachable absolute URL or string: accepted exactly when every present field is allowed for the
provider and every required field is present.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.configValuesAccepted
entries.docstring:
`parseProviderConfig` on a stored-shape config: every present field is allowed for the
provider and not blank, and every required field is present. A present `baseUrl` is assumed to be
an absolute URL the egress policy allows (the model does not model URLs or egress).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.createAccepts
entries.docstring:
`parseCreateModelConnection` over the keys of a body (each present value valid): closed, with
`name`, `provider` and `apiKey` required.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.createFields
entries.docstring: The fields `POST /api/model-connections` accepts.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.createRequiredFields
entries.docstring: The fields `POST /api/model-connections` requires; `config` may be omitted.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.isComplete
entries.docstring:
`isModelConnectionConfigComplete`: every field the provider requires is present and not
blank.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.nameAccepted
entries.docstring:
The value rule for a connection's `name` on create and update: a string that is not blank after
JavaScript's `trim`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.ready
entries.docstring: `ready = hasCredential && isModelConnectionConfigComplete(provider, config)`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.resourceFields
entries.docstring: The field names of `ModelConnectionResourceSchema`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.rule
entries.docstring:
`MODEL_PROVIDER_CONFIG_RULES` (and the server's `PROVIDER_CONFIG_SPEC`): the Anthropic
providers and OpenAI take an optional `baseUrl`, OpenAI-compatible requires it, and Azure OpenAI
requires all three fields.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.updateAccepts
entries.docstring:
`parseUpdateModelConnection` over the keys of a body (each present value valid): closed, and
nothing is required, so an empty body is a no-op update.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.updateFields
entries.docstring:
The fields `PATCH /api/model-connections/:id` accepts: the provider is write-once, and an
`apiKey` replaces the saved key (a changed `config.baseUrl` needs one, so the saved key never
follows the connection to a new destination).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Ceiling
entries.docstring:
A parsed `ProjectPolicy`. `caps` are the permission keys the ceiling sets `false`; `none` for
a limit or an allowlist means the key is absent. `minEvalScore` is `promotion.minEvalScore`, the
promotion gate's bar (`Release.gate`): `violations` and `meet` never read it (80-12).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Config
entries.docstring:
`EffectivePolicyConfiguration`: what a ceiling judges at one step. A `none` limit is `null`;
a `none` model means there is no model to judge at this step.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Widening
entries.docstring: One `details` entry of `403 policy_cannot_widen` (`PolicyWidening`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.meet
entries.docstring:
`meetPolicyCeiling`: permissions on only where the ceiling does not cap them, limits capped,
tools kept in input order only where allowed; the engine and the model unchanged.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.violations
entries.docstring:
`policyWidenings`: where `e` asks for more than `c` allows, in C14's order. Empty means
nothing widens.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.within
entries.docstring: Every field of `e` is at or under `c`, judged field by field (no list of details).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Actor
entries.docstring:
The frozen `Principal` object a handler is handed. Ids are the strings the TypeScript
carries.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.ActsForRow
entries.docstring:
What the directory re-reads for the principal a key acts for: that principal's row and whether
its membership row is still present.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.ApiKeyIdentity
entries.docstring: `ApiKeyIdentity`: what a presented API key establishes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.DirectoryRecord
entries.docstring: `DirectoryPrincipalRecord`: what the directory re-reads for a principal id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Kind
entries.docstring: The two principal kinds, in `PRINCIPAL_KINDS` order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.LocalKey
entries.docstring:
A local runtime key's principal as the repair reads it: every API-key principal whose key name
carries `LOCAL_RUNTIME_API_KEY_NAME_PREFIX`, revoked and expired ones included, with the principal
it acts for, if recorded.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.MeResponse
entries.docstring:
The body of `GET /api/me` for an authenticated principal: its id, wire kind, role, workspace,
user id and label, and nothing else.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.OwnedRow
entries.docstring:
A row an owner column names (`owner_principal_id` of agents, sessions, skills, files, MCP
servers and projects; `publisher_principal_id` of shares): its id and its owner.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Principal
entries.docstring: A durable principal: a row of `workspace_principals`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.PrincipalState
entries.docstring: The two states of a principal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.ScopedRow
entries.docstring:
The scoped row `resolveBrowserTokenActor` reads: a run with its status or a session with its
status (`none` when the row is gone).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Source
entries.docstring: A principal's source: exactly one membership or exactly one API key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.SourceRow
entries.docstring:
The source row `principalById` re-reads for a principal: the membership (present or since
deleted), or the API key row (if any).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Via
entries.docstring:
`Via`: which verifier produced an authenticated principal. A browser token is not a third
identity; it is the minter's session or API-key identity with a scope attached.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.actsForOfRow?
entries.docstring: Read the principal a `workspace_principals` row acts for: `acts_for_principal_id`, or `none`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.actsForStands
entries.docstring:
The acts-for conjunct of admission and resolution: a principal that acts for no one passes; one
that acts for someone passes only while that principal — the one named, in the same workspace, a
membership — is active and its membership is present ("a key never outlives the person it acts
for").

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.apiKeyAdmitted
entries.docstring:
`authenticateApiKeyHash`'s whole admission: the key row is live (`ApiKey.live`), the
`workspace_principals` row it joins — same workspace, source this key — is not revoked, and the
principal it acts for, if any, still stands (`actsForStands`). `target` is that principal as the
directory re-reads it; left out, it is absent, so a key that acts for someone is refused.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.backfillActsFor
entries.docstring:
The backfill half of the repair: every local key that records no principal it acts for now
acts for `target`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.browserTokenAdmitted
entries.docstring:
`resolveBrowserTokenActor`'s admission, spec §3.1.1 "Revocation": the token row is live, its
scope is still open, and its minter — the principal the row names, in the row's workspace —
still resolves.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.fromApiKey
entries.docstring: `Principal.fromApiKey`: the owner is the principal the key acts for, or the key's own.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.fromBrowserToken
entries.docstring:
`Principal.fromBrowserToken`: the minter, with `via = browser-token` and the scope attached;
every other field is the minter's, the owner included.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.fromDirectoryRecord
entries.docstring:
`Principal.fromDirectoryRecord`: `via` follows the kind; no scope; an API-key record's owner is
the principal it acts for, or its own, and a membership record always owns what it writes. It
copies the record's `userId` and `apiKeyId` without checking them against the kind.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.principalResolves
entries.docstring:
`principalById` answers a record: the principal row is active, its source row still stands —
the membership still exists, or the key is its own and live at `now` ("a key that has since been
revoked or has expired must stop authenticating a browser token it minted") — and the principal it
acts for, if any, still stands.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.reassignLocalOwnership
entries.docstring:
`reassignLocalRuntimeKeyOwnership`, on the owned rows: every row a local key's principal owns
moves to `coalesce(acts_for_principal_id, target)`. Version authorship, audit actors and
browser-token minters are not owner columns and are never passed here.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.repairLocalOwnership
entries.docstring: The whole repair, in one transaction: the backfilled local keys and the reassigned rows.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.scopeOpen
entries.docstring:
The scope is still open: the scoped row exists, is the one the scope names, and has not reached
a terminal state (a run's `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`, a session's `archived`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.sourceOfRow?
entries.docstring: Read the source of a `workspace_principals` row: `none` for any row the XOR check refuses.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.wireKindOfStorage?
entries.docstring: `wireKind`: the one place the server maps the storage spelling to the wire spelling.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.Project
entries.docstring: One project, with the fields `projects` stores (timestamps as instants, which are inputs).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.ProjectListFilter
entries.docstring: `PROJECT_LIST_FILTERS`: the `?archived=` filter of `GET /api/projects`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.ProjectState
entries.docstring: The project's lifecycle state.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.ProjectVisibility
entries.docstring: `PROJECT_VISIBILITIES` (`projectVisibilities` in the schema).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.hasNonSpace
entries.docstring:
PostgreSQL's `length(btrim(s)) > 0`: one-argument `btrim` strips spaces only, so the text
has a character other than a space (a tab-only name passes).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env
entries.docstring: An environment: a name, and one pointer per agent.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op
entries.docstring: An operation on the release state. A UI edit is a `push`: it saves a new version.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Problem
entries.docstring: Why a step is refused. The codes are the problem codes 80-07, 80-08 and 80-12 return.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release
entries.docstring: The release state.

entries.statement: Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score → Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score → Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Problem
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.gate
entries.docstring:
The promotion gate: a pure decision over the bar and a version's score, `none` when it passes.
With no bar, promotion needs no evaluation. With a bar, a version with no score is not evaluated,
and one scored below the bar fails the gate.

entries.statement: Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op → Except AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Problem AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step
entries.docstring: One step of the release state machine, with the gate's bar as a parameter (`none`: no bar set).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.ModelProvider
entries.docstring: `MODEL_PROVIDERS` (`modelProviders` in the schema): who served a run.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run
entries.docstring: One run, with the fields `runs` stores.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.RunToken
entries.docstring: A gateway token minted for one run (`run_tokens`): only a digest is retained.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind
entries.docstring: The three kinds of frame a client tells apart by name.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.RunEvent
entries.docstring: One stored event. `data` is the JSON text of the `jsonb` column.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.controlFrameNames
entries.docstring: `CONTROL_FRAME_NAMES`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName
entries.docstring: `EVENT_NAME_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.logContiguous
entries.docstring:
The stored log of a run is a window: "Sequence numbers are contiguous per run", and the
oldest may have been pruned.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.relayedEventNames
entries.docstring: `RELAYED_EVENT_NAMES`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.runStatusEvent
entries.docstring: `RUN_STATUS_EVENT`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.Driver
entries.docstring: The runtime drivers (`runtimeProfileDrivers`, `RUNTIME_DRIVERS`), in spec §14.2 order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.Filesystem
entries.docstring: Whether the working tree is writable (`runtimeProfileFilesystems`, `RUNTIME_FILESYSTEM_MODES`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.NetworkPolicy
entries.docstring:
What a runtime may reach over the network (`runtimeProfileNetworkPolicies`,
`RUNTIME_NETWORK_POLICIES`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.RuntimeProfile
entries.docstring:
One `runtime_profiles` row as the concept knows it (sizing as the `integer` columns store
it; the three `jsonb` columns as present or absent).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.connectionCreateAccepts
entries.docstring:
`parseCreateRuntimeConnectionInput` over the keys of a body (each present value valid): it
requires its four fields and, unlike the other configuration request parsers, is open: it ignores
every other key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.connectionCreateFields
entries.docstring: The fields `POST /api/runtime-connections` takes; `endpoint` and `credential` are sealed.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.connectionCreateRequiredFields
entries.docstring: The fields `POST /api/runtime-connections` requires: all four.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.connectionCredentialAccepted
entries.docstring: The value rule for a runtime connection's `credential`: any non-empty string.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.connectionResourceFields
entries.docstring: The field names of `RuntimeConnectionResourceSchema`: no endpoint, no credential.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.connectionTextAccepted
entries.docstring:
The value rule for a runtime connection's `name` and `endpoint`: not blank after JavaScript's
`trim`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.cpuAccepted
entries.docstring: `RUNTIME_PROFILE_BOUNDS.cpu`: greater than zero; fractions are allowed.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.createAccepts
entries.docstring:
`CreateRuntimeProfileInput` (a `.strict()` object) over the keys of a body, each present value
valid: closed, with the four required members.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.createFields
entries.docstring:
The fields `POST /api/runtime-profiles` accepts: every member of spec §15.1's `RuntimeProfile`
but the server-assigned `id`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.createImageAccepted
entries.docstring:
`parseCreateRuntimeProfileInput`'s image rule: an absent image passes, a string must be
`sha256`-pinned, anything else is refused. The driver is an argument because the error message
speaks of "non-local runtime profiles"; the rule does not read it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.decodeDriver
entries.docstring:
`decodeDriver(name)`: the driver half of a runtime-connection secret name, or `none` when the
name is not one. Nothing checks that the result is a known driver.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.encodeSecretName
entries.docstring:
`encodeSecretName(driver, label)`: `RUNTIME_CONNECTION__<DRIVER>__<LABEL>`, or `none` when the
encoded label does not start with a letter or the name exceeds 128 characters.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.encodeSegment
entries.docstring: `encodeSegment`: upper-case, then every character outside `A-Z0-9` becomes `_`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.isSha256Pinned
entries.docstring:
`/^.+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/u`: a non-empty single-line reference, then `@sha256:`, then exactly
64 lower-case hexadecimal digits at the very end.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.jsUpperCaseDivergences
entries.docstring:
