Labels outside ASCII on which JavaScript's Unicode-aware `toUpperCase` makes the real
`encodeSecretName("docker", label)` differ from the model's ASCII upper-casing: the label and the
name the code stores (`none` when the code refuses the label).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.maxSafeInteger
entries.docstring: `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, the ceiling `RUNTIME_PROFILE_BOUNDS` uses.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.nameAcceptedByContract
entries.docstring:
The profile name the contract accepts (`z.string().min(1)`): any non-empty string, blank or
not.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.nullAsValueFields
entries.docstring:
The fields whose `null` is itself a value rather than a clear: a profile reads back
`allowedDomains: null` for "no domains", so a `PATCH` may send that value back (BH061-080).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.patchAcceptsCurrent
entries.docstring:
Today's `PATCH /api/runtime-profiles/:id` (`UpdateRuntimeProfileInput`, whose members are
`.optional()` and so refuse `null`): every key is an updatable field carrying a value; `null`
is refused for every field except where `null` is itself a value (`nullAsValueFields`), so a
nullable field can be changed but not cleared.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.patchAcceptsTarget
entries.docstring:
The documented target (roadmap S-19): `null` clears a field S-19 names; every other field still
cannot be cleared, and a field whose `null` is a value accepts it as today.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.requiredCreateFields
entries.docstring: The fields `POST /api/runtime-profiles` requires (spec §15.1's non-optional members).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.resourceFields
entries.docstring: The field names of `RuntimeProfileResourceSchema`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.s19ClearableFields
entries.docstring:
The fields roadmap S-19 lets a `PATCH` clear: "the nullable sizing fields and
`runtimeConnectionId`", read as the sizing and timeout members. Whether `allowedDomains`,
`persistPaths` and `driverConfig` are meant too the row does not say.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.sizeAccepted
entries.docstring:
`RUNTIME_PROFILE_BOUNDS` for `memoryMb`, `diskMb`, `timeoutSeconds` and `idleTimeoutSeconds`:
a whole number in `[1, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER]`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.updateFields
entries.docstring:
The fields `PATCH /api/runtime-profiles/:id` accepts: `UpdateRuntimeProfileInput` is
`CreateRuntimeProfileInput.partial()`, so every creatable field and nothing else.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Secret.Algorithm
entries.docstring: The envelope algorithms the schema accepts: one, deliberately (`secretAlgorithms`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Secret.Envelope
entries.docstring:
The envelope: the master key that wrapped the data key, and the octet lengths of the seven
`bytea` parts.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Secret.Purpose
entries.docstring: What a secrets row is for, read from its name (the only place today's code records it).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Secret.Resource
entries.docstring: `SecretResourceSchema`: the metadata only.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Secret.Secret

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Skill.wireFields

The keys of `SkillDetailSchema` (every skill body the routes render): no owner, no creator;
`SKILL.md` is `source`, parsed into `description`, `instructions` and `allowedTools`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState
entries.docstring: `ACCOUNTING_STATES`: how far usage accounting for a run has progressed.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.Counters
entries.docstring:
The five usage counters a run and each ledger row carry (`RunUsageSchema` without the
derived total).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord
entries.docstring:
One row of `run_usage_records`: one provider response's usage, keyed for idempotence by
`(run_id, provider_response_id)`. `priceTableVersion` is `none` when the response was captured
with no price catalogue entry for its model; the row is then recorded at zero cost.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.WireProtocol
entries.docstring:

one usage extractor each, and the closed set is carried by this type as well as by the column's

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.isDecimal
entries.docstring: A decimal as PostgreSQL renders `numeric`: an optional `-`, then an unsigned decimal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting

The accounting state the repository recomputes from a run's ledger after a settlement: no
priced row is `unavailable`, every row priced is `complete`, otherwise `partial`. An empty
ledger has had no settlement, which is the column default `pending`. (`failed` is written by a
settlement that could not produce ledger data at all, so the ledger never derives it.)

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.settlementCurrency
entries.docstring: The one settlement currency: "0.1.0 pricing is USD-only and says so explicitly".

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.zeroCost

default `InMemoryRunStore.create` writes and `renderRun` falls back to).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey

through its *assignments*, subagents through its version body (ADR-0133 D14) — and so the values
an `engine_capability_unsupported` refusal may name.

It is a strict subset of {@link engineCapabilities}'s keys, and deliberately so: the rest of the
capability set describes what a *run* may ask for (`resume`, `interrupt`, a turn cap), which no save
decides, so naming one of those in a save-time refusal would promise a check that does not exist.

the field order the TypeScript declares.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.engineDescriptor

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.ApiProblemDetail

server answers the standard envelope instead; an older deployment still answers this one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.CommonProblemCode

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.apiProblemBareCodeCodec

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.apiProblemCodec

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunEvents.agentFrameRawTruncation

`raw` over the cap is truncated with a marker, never rejected: the marker's own shape is what a

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunStatus.isTerminal
entries.docstring: `isTerminalRunStatus`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunStatus.terminal
entries.docstring: `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES`: the statuses a run never leaves.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Check
entries.docstring:
A check constraint. The closed-set checks (`column IN ('a', 'b', …)`, optionally guarded by
`column IS NULL OR`) keep their column and values; every other check is recorded by name and is
refined by the cluster that owns the table.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.FkClass
entries.docstring: The buckets `tenancy.test.ts` sorts every foreign key into.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.SqlType
entries.docstring:
The SQL column types the schema uses, as Drizzle's `getSQLType()` and `drizzle-kit` spell
them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName
entries.docstring: Every table of the schema, in the order the schema barrel re-exports their modules.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Tenancy
entries.docstring:
How a table relates to the tenant: it is the tenant root, a global identity table exempt
from tenant scoping, or scoped by a `workspace_id` column.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue
entries.docstring:
Today's schema, transcribed from `packages/core/src/db/schema/*.ts` as
the latest snapshot (`Er.Snapshot.file`) renders it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.classify
entries.docstring: The tenancy bucket of a foreign key of table `t`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.idColumnsCovered
entries.docstring:
Every `*_id` column of the schema is a foreign-key column or a declared non-reference of the
declared type, and every declaration names an existing column. Without this, `pairingComplete`
could be satisfied by deleting a foreign key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.isIdColumn
entries.docstring: A column named like a reference: its name ends in `_id` (`REFERENCE_SUFFIX`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.isSafeValue
entries.docstring:
`SAFE_VALUE = /^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/` with `MAX_VALUE_LENGTH = 64`: a lower-case
slug that starts with a letter, has single hyphens between runs of letters and digits, and is at
most 64 characters.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.nonReferenceIdColumns
entries.docstring:
`NON_REFERENCE_ID_COLUMNS`: the `*_id` columns that refer to nothing in this schema, each with
the SQL type the declaration pins.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.pairingComplete
entries.docstring:
No foreign key of the schema is `unpaired`: every reference between two tenant-carrying tables
is tenant-paired by itself or by a sibling (the rule `tenancy.test.ts` enforces).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.principalSourceXor
entries.docstring:
`workspace_principals_source_xor`: `(kind = 'membership' and membership_id is not null and
api_key_id is null) or (kind = 'api_key' and api_key_id is not null and membership_id is null)`.
Under SQL's three-valued logic the expression is `NULL`, so the check passes, only when `kind` is
`NULL` (which `kind NOT NULL` forbids separately).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.renderValueList?
entries.docstring:
`renderValueList`: `('a', 'b', …)` for DDL inlining, or `none` where the TypeScript throws
(an empty list, a duplicate, or a value that is not a safe slug).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.tenancyWellFormed
entries.docstring:
The model's tenancy rule for one table. `Authz.Tenancy.testRule1` separately transcribes
rule 1 of `tenancy.test.ts`; the two predicates agree on the current catalogue but differ on
other schemas. Like the test: a scoped table has a `NOT NULL`
`workspace_id` and exactly one single-column reference to `workspaces.id`, and an exempt table
(the root or a global table) has no `workspace_id`. Stricter than the test: the scoped column is
`uuid` (the test leaves that to the foreign key's type agreement) and the root is keyed by `id`.
Weaker than the test: the test also requires `workspace_id` to lead an index. The
`ON DELETE CASCADE` of every root
reference is a separate schema fact (`every_root_reference_cascades`), not part of the rule.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Cluster
entries.docstring: The concept clusters of phase P1b, each the owner of a disjoint set of tables.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.checkSemantics
entries.docstring:
The meaning of check `n` of table `t` on a row: the semantics of the cluster that owns the
table. A check nobody refines holds (there is none: `every_other_check_is_refined`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.consistent
entries.docstring:
Today's database is consistent: every cluster's view of the state is. That is every constraint
of `catalogue` (`Er.Core.consistent`), the meaning of every one of the 88 checks that are not
closed sets, and the identity cluster's cell typing (timestamps are instants, booleans are
`true` or `false`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.otherChecks
entries.docstring: Every check of today's schema that is not a closed set, as (table, constraint name).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.ownerColumn?
entries.docstring:
The column of a row that names the principal owning it, where the schema has one: the
catalogued resources, projects and sessions (`owner_principal_id`), shares
(`publisher_principal_id`), browser tokens (`minted_by_principal_id`) and audit events
(`actor_principal_id`, the only nullable one).

convention `MODEL_CONNECTION_<ID>` points at.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Refinement.fkImage
entries.docstring: The key of the target a foreign key of today's table `t` becomes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Refinement.mapRow
entries.docstring: One row of table `t` of state `st`, as the target stores it.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State → Option String → Option String → Option String
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Refinement.principalOfUser
entries.docstring: The principal of user `uid`'s membership in workspace `ws`, in state `st`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Refinement.toTarget
entries.docstring: The refinement map: every row of today's state, as the target stores it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.conflations
entries.docstring: Words that today denote more than one glossary term, with the terms they denote.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.consistent
entries.docstring: The states the target database can hold.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.erDiagram
entries.docstring:
The target ER as a mermaid `erDiagram`, one relationship per line, generated from `schema`:
`docs/formal/concepts.md` carries this text verbatim and the conformance suite compares them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.glossary
entries.docstring:
The concept glossary: every term with one meaning. `docs/formal/concepts.md` is its prose
form.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.ownerColumn?
entries.docstring:
The column of a row that names its owner principal, in the target: `owner_principal_id` on
every owned resource, including shares.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.schema
entries.docstring: The target schema. Each edit of today's `catalogue` is one proposed cleanup.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.stateInvariants
entries.docstring:
The invariants of the target that are not row checks: every membership and API key has its
principal (RF-101), and every runtime connection a profile names is one (RF-204).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.subjectColumn
entries.docstring: A share subject's column: one nullable, tenant-paired reference per subject type.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.tableName
entries.docstring: The SQL name of each table in the target: the connector tables take the concept's one name.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Target.targetCheck?
entries.docstring: The meaning of each check the target adds, by name; `none` for a check it inherits.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Classified
entries.docstring:
`packages/core`'s `ClassifiedSdkEvent`. It is the *input* of `toAgentFrames` and names nothing on
the wire any more.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.assistantResponse
entries.docstring:
The SDK's `assistantResponseFromAgentEvent`: the visible text of a spoken assistant turn, and
nothing else. Reasoning, tool use, usage and results cannot reach the conversation.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.capRaw
entries.docstring:
Cap a payload: the value when it fits, the marker when it does not, and the marker with no size
when it has no JSON representation to measure. **Total** — there is no arm that drops the frame,
because the neutral fields beside `raw` are the part a consumer renders.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.capRowFrames
entries.docstring:
Cap the frames one row serves: every frame when they fit; otherwise the first 999 and one
`agent.malformed` that reports the remainder. Reported, never guessed and never a stream that stops
parsing: a tenant's agent chooses how many tool calls one turn carries.

entries.statement: List String → List String → List String → AgentWorkspace.JValue → AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Classified
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.classify
entries.docstring:
`classifySdkEvent`, as `packages/core` decides it: discriminate on `type`, then on `subtype` for
`system` and `result`, and reject a non-object, a non-string discriminant or an **empty** `type` by
name rather than falling through to the opaque-forward path (ADR-0015). An empty `type` is refused
because it names nothing: forwarded, it would become an `agent.native` frame whose `type` the
contract refuses, which is a dropped message by another route.

A `malformed` reason is the code's whole diagnostic, `; got …` suffix included, so the replay
compares it with `toEqual` like every other field.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.decode
entries.docstring:
The SDK's validating parser: the engine, the engine-native payload and the frame, or `none` for
a payload that does not satisfy the contract. Reading the arm's fields *positively* is the whole
point — a payload whose `frame` field this build does not know, or whose fields do not match it, is
refused by name rather than read around (ADR-0015).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.describe
entries.docstring:
`describe` in `packages/core/src/schemas.ts`: the offending value in JavaScript's words. `none`
is a key that is absent, which JavaScript reads as `undefined`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.encode
entries.docstring:
The JSON one frame is sent as: the discriminant, the engine, the capped engine-native payload,
then the arm's own fields.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.legacyMessage
entries.docstring: Read the engine message out of a stored envelope, or the code's reason the row is not one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.maxFramesPerRow
entries.docstring:
The most frames one row may serve: sub-indices `0 … 999`, the three digits the documented id
grammar (`WIRE_EVENT_ID_PATTERN`, `cursor.ts`) admits.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.paired
entries.docstring:
Whether every `agent.tool.result` in a sequence is answered by an **earlier**
`agent.tool.call` with the same id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.rawMaxBytes
entries.docstring: The published cap on the engine-native payload a frame may carry, in UTF-8 bytes.

entries.statement: {α : Type} → Option (Nat × Nat) → Nat → Bool → List α → List α
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.resumeWithinRow
entries.docstring:
What a client resumed at `(sequence, subIndex)` is served from a row. `subIndexed` is whether the
row is served in parts — an upgraded legacy row — rather than one-to-one.

The frames after the one it last saw, when the row is the one its cursor named and was served in
parts; every frame of the row otherwise. A cursor into a row the store can no longer retain has
already produced a `stream-reset`, so the oldest retained row is new to the client in its entirety;
and a sub-index on a row served one-to-one is an id this server never wrote, so the row is served
whole rather than dropped on the strength of a position it does not have.

entries.statement: List String → List String → List String → Nat → AgentWorkspace.JValue → List ((Nat × Option Nat) × AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Frame)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.serveLegacyRow
entries.docstring: The ids and frames one legacy row serves, in the order `toAgentFrames` emitted them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.stopReasonOf
entries.docstring:
The neutral stop reason of a `result` subtype. An unrecognised subtype is an `error`: a turn
whose outcome this build cannot name is not one it may report as having gone well.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toAgentEvent
entries.docstring:
The SDK's `toAgentEvent`.

`none` for the platform's own frames: they are already typed on `RunEventFrame` and are the
*platform* speaking about the run and the stream, not the engine speaking about the turn. A runtime
frame whose payload does not decode is a `ContractViolationError` in the code, and `none` here.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toAgentFrames
entries.docstring:
Map one classified Claude Agent SDK message onto neutral frames.

**Never empty, by construction**: whatever `mappedFrames` cannot express becomes `agent.native`, and
a message that could not be parsed becomes `agent.malformed`. There is no arm that returns `[]` for
an event that arrived, and `never_drops_an_engine_message` is one line because of it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toAgentFramesJson
entries.docstring:
The JSON the adapter sends for one engine message: every frame it maps to, each carrying the
capped engine message as its `raw`. `encodedBytes` is the message's `JSON.stringify` size in UTF-8
bytes, or `none` when it has no JSON representation.

Every frame of the message carries it, not only the first: a consumer that resumed inside a
message, or reads only `agent.result`, still holds the words the frame was derived from — and the
result frame's accounting is checked against exactly that.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toolFrames
entries.docstring:
The tool frames one message's content carries.

A `tool_use` block rides only on an `assistant` message and a `tool_result` only on a `user` one,
which is what makes the pairing invariant hold over a whole run without this function having to
remember anything between messages. Each list is a `map` over the blocks it read, so "every frame
here is a call" is an induction rather than an assertion.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toolKindOf
entries.docstring:
`claudeToolKind`: only tools whose effect is known are named; an MCP tool by its prefix, and
everything else `other`, which is the honest answer rather than a default that hides an effect.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.truncationMarker
entries.docstring: The marker `raw` becomes when the payload did not fit, or had no JSON representation.

entries.statement: List String → List String → List String → AgentWorkspace.JValue → List AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Frame
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.upgradeLegacy
entries.docstring:
Upgrade one pre-ENG-03 row.

Deterministic, and by construction the *same two functions* a fresh run applies, in the same order,
over the same input. A row that is not an envelope becomes `agent.malformed` — the frame says the
envelope could not be read, and nothing is invented.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.usageOf
entries.docstring:
The engine's own counters, when at least one `modelUsage` entry is readable.

Summed across models, because R-01 §4 records the record key as unstable; `thinkingTokens` is
reported as `reasoningTokens` and never added to `outputTokens`, which already contains it. An engine
that reported nothing is not an engine that reported zero, so this is `none` rather than a zero
frame.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.wireEventId
entries.docstring:
The id one served frame carries.

`none` for the sub-index is the bare sequence a row served one-to-one, which is every row a run
started after ENG-03 writes. An upgraded legacy row always carries one, even when it produced a
single frame, so an id says which kind of row it came from.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.Resume.parseFrameId
entries.docstring: `<sequence>[.<sub-index>]`, the whole grammar `sse.ts`'s `WIRE_EVENT_ID_PATTERN` documents.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.Resume.parseId
entries.docstring:
The sequence part of an id: at most 19 digits, because `maxEventId` has 19, and inside the range
the column that has to store it can hold.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.Resume.readResumeCursor
entries.docstring: The header wins even if invalid; only a missing header allows a query cursor.

entries.statement: Nat → AgentWorkspace.Events.RunLog.Log → String → AgentWorkspace.JValue → Option (AgentWorkspace.Events.RunLog.Log × AgentWorkspace.Events.RunLog.Event)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.RunLog.append
entries.docstring:
In-memory append allocates `max + 1`, retains only the newest `limit` events, and refuses a
closed log. The database adapter makes the same allocation under its advisory lock.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.RunLog.memoryMayEnd
entries.docstring: The in-memory loop sends all retained events before testing its closed-and-caught-up exit.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.RunLog.repositoryMayEndCurrent
entries.docstring: The repository loop returns after it reads a terminal run and drains the durable tail.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.RunLog.resetFor
entries.docstring:
Both stores announce a gap when the requested beginning has been evicted, including a first
connection without a cursor.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.SdkSse.parseSseFrame
entries.docstring:
An empty `id:` remains `some ""`; an unnamed frame is discarded. Later fields override
earlier `event` and `id`, while data lines concatenate.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.Sse.assembleLine
entries.docstring:
A blank line dispatches only if at least one `data:` field arrived. An empty `id:` clears
the cursor; an id containing NUL is ignored.

entries.statement: String → Option AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunStatus → Option String → AgentWorkspace.Events.Sse.Outcome
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.Sse.classifyRunOutcome
AgentWorkspace.Events.Sse.outcomeFrames
entries.docstring:
`done` follows a known failure and an indeterminate outcome alike. A producer exception is a
different path, with no `done`, so the client may reconnect.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.Sse.publicRuntimeOutcomeReason
entries.docstring:
Runner outcome details are untrusted and remain in server diagnostics. Public terminal
records and frames use a stable message chosen by the outcome kind.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Events.Sse.pushLines
entries.docstring: CR, LF and CRLF terminate relay lines, including a CRLF split across chunk boundaries.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Engines.Descriptor
entries.docstring: One registered engine, in the fields this layer observes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Engines.list
entries.docstring:
`engines.list()`: the route's answer with the `{ engines }` envelope removed. `none` is the
typed `ApiProblemError` the SDK raises, never an empty catalogue.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Engines.listRequest
entries.docstring: `engines.list()`: `GET /api/engines`, expecting `200`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Engines.serve
entries.docstring: `listEngines`: the whole registry, or nothing.

entries.statement: List Char → List Char → List String → List String × String
entries.name: _private.AgentWorkspace.Events.SdkSse.0.AgentWorkspace.Events.SdkSse.splitOnBlankLine
entries.docstring:
The SDK normalises complete CR, LF, and CRLF line endings, splits on blank lines, and retains
a trailing CR in the partial remainder until another chunk or normal EOF resolves it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.RepoWrite.compile
entries.docstring: The statements a repository bound to scope `s` issues for a write.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.claudeTools
entries.docstring: The Claude tools each switch governs.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.narrow
entries.docstring: The permissions a run composes under a withheld list: `policyNarrowedPermissions`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.reverseDeny
entries.docstring: The reverse half: every withheld switch's Claude tools appended to `tools.deny`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.toolKey
entries.docstring: The switch that grants each OpenAI Agents tool.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.translate
entries.docstring:
`translatePolicyForEngineSwitch` from `claude-agent-sdk` to `openai-agents`: the withheld
switches of the new arm (those it already named, plus those the old arm withholds, in key order),
or the untranslatable denials.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Tool
entries.docstring: Mastra's workspace tools the adapter can offer, in `MASTRA_TOOL_NAMES` order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.boundaryEvents
entries.docstring:
The events `startMastraRun` yields for a stream: the forwarded chunks, then — after an `error`
chunk — the `finish` as a native chunk if one came, or otherwise the adapter's terminal event built
from `finish` (`terminal`: the stop, the steps and the usage).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile
entries.docstring: `compileMastraRun`, check for check and in the same order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compileConnectors
entries.docstring:
The connectors compile hands `MCPClient`, in order; an unreadable record is refused
`engine_policy_invalid`, a tool asking for an approval `engine_capability_unsupported`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.holdsProtected
entries.docstring:
Does the subtree at `segments` hold a read-only grant or the adapter's own directory
(`mastraRelativeSubtreeVerdict`)? Segment by segment: the candidate is a prefix of what it holds.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.installedEnvironment
entries.docstring:
`mastraInstalledEnvironment`: the environment Mastra sees when it loads, from whatever the
runner's process held — the switches set, an empty provider base URL removed, the rest kept.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.isDatabaseEnvName
entries.docstring:
Does a variable name carry a database connection? The name is upper-cased first, as
`databaseEnvName` does. `Char.toUpper` is ASCII-only while JavaScript's `toUpperCase` is not; a
name the model matches is all ASCII, where the two agree, so the TypeScript refuses at least every
name the model does.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.journal
entries.docstring:
The journal of a thread: its record, then one entry per message (`threadEntry`,
`messageEntry`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.kindOf
entries.docstring:
The kind of a tool call by name: a workspace tool's own, `read` for a skill tool, `mcp` for a
name under one of the run's connectors (`<server>_<tool>`), and `other` otherwise.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.modelSpecOf
entries.docstring: What `./boundary.ts#modelFor` hands the `Agent`: the provider `mastraProviderSpec` decides.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.priced
entries.docstring: Can a cap on this model be priced? The port's provisional table (`provisionalPriceFor`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.processSwitches
entries.docstring: `MASTRA_PROCESS_ENVIRONMENT`: the switches the boundary sets before Mastra loads.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.providerSpec
entries.docstring:
`mastraProviderSpec`: the factory, token option and method each API is reached through, at the
connection's own base URL.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.readThread
entries.docstring: `readMastraThread`: the thread's messages, or `none` when the stream is not this thread's.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.removeAllowed
entries.docstring:
`mastraRemoveVerdict`: a path may be removed, or moved away, when it may be written and its
subtree holds nothing protected. `deleteFile`, `rmdir` and `moveFile`'s source ask it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.resolveWorkspacePath
entries.docstring:
`mastraWorkspacePath`, before its normalisation: `LocalFilesystem`'s own resolution restated
(`~` expanded, an absolute path taken as is, anything else under the base path), with the two
spellings that leave the workspace refused. The comparison is on the character list.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.step
entries.docstring:
One chunk, given the mapper's state: the next state and the frames. Native payloads are
carried as `null`; the replay compares every neutral field.

entries.statement: Option Nat → Nat → List Bool → Nat × AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.StopReason
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.stepRun
entries.docstring:
The run's stop over the steps its model would take, in order: each flag says whether that step
asked for tools (Mastra would take another step). A step that asked for none ends the run
`end_turn`; the step that reaches `maxSteps` still asking for tools is the last Mastra takes, and
the adapter reports the run `max_turns`. The first component is the steps taken.

entries.statement: Nat → Option String → Option Nat → Bool → Bool → AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.StopReason
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.stopReason
entries.docstring:
`mastraStopReason`: the adapter's verdict on a drained run. The budget cap wins, then the
caller's interrupt; otherwise a run whose last allowed step still asked for tools
(`stepResult.reason` is `tool-calls`) was cut short, and any other ends `end_turn`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.toolPlan
entries.docstring:
The tool plan: every tool its switch allows, in order, with the command tools withheld while a
read-only grant exists (a redirect would write what the grant protects, and a subprocess's writes
never pass the filesystem wrapper).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.writeAllowed
entries.docstring: May the wrapped filesystem write `candidate`? `mastraWriteAllowed`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.writeVerdict
entries.docstring:
`mastraWriteVerdict`: resolve the path, refuse what leaves the workspace and the root itself,
and ask `writeGrantVerdict` about the rest.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool
entries.docstring: The five function tools the adapter can offer, in `OPENAI_AGENTS_TOOL_NAMES` order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.budgetRunFrom
entries.docstring:
The boundary's budget stop over the estimated cost of each model response, in order, in
micro-dollars: after each response the spend so far is compared with the cap, and the run stops
`max_budget` at the first response that brings it to the cap or over; a run whose responses stay
under it ends as the model ends it. The first component is the responses performed.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile
entries.docstring: `compileOpenAiAgentsRun`, check for check and in the same order.

entries.statement: {α : Type} → List (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Entry α) → Option Nat → Option (List α)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.getItems
entries.docstring: `getItems(limit)` over the store: list, unwrap, keep the last `limit`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.priced
entries.docstring: Can a cap on this model be priced? `openAiAgentsPriceFor(model) !== null`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.pricedModels
entries.docstring:
The models the provisional price table prices: the keys of `OPENAI_AGENTS_PROVISIONAL_PRICES`,
in its order. A cap on any other model (or on the SDK's unnamed default) is refused.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.runOutcome
entries.docstring:
The SDK's native `maxTurns` contract (a hypothesis, see the header): a run whose model would
take `wanted` responses performs `min wanted limit` of them and ends `max_turns` when it was cut
short.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.FrameContext → List String → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Event → List String × List AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Frame
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.step
entries.docstring:
One event, given the call ids announced so far: the new announced list and the frames.
Native payloads are carried as `null` here; the replay compares every neutral field.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.toolPlan
entries.docstring:
The tool plan: every tool its switch allows, in order, with `shell` withheld while a
read-only grant exists (a redirect would write what the grant protects).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.writeAllowed
entries.docstring: May the compiled Editor write `candidate`? `workspaceWriteAllowed`, over the compiled grants.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Tool
entries.docstring: pi's four built-in tools the adapter can offer, in `PI_TOOL_NAMES` order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile
entries.docstring: `compilePiRun`, check for check and in the same order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.guard
entries.docstring:
The guard's decision on one call, on the path the model named (`piToolCallVerdict`): a tool the
plan does not offer is blocked; `bash` runs when offered; `read` needs a path that resolves inside
the workspace; `write` and `edit` need a path `workspaceWriteVerdict` allows.

entries.statement: List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Line → List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Line → List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Line
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.persist
entries.docstring: `PiSessionMirror.persist`: append the lines of the file the stream does not hold yet.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.pinnedLoad
entries.docstring:
What the pinned loader returns, of everything present on the host: the skills it finds under
`.pi/skills` that the run grants, then the instructions. Nothing else is ever consulted.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.priced
entries.docstring: Can a cap on this model be priced? The port's provisional table (`provisionalPriceFor`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.readStream
entries.docstring:
`readPiStream`: a stream is resumable as `sid` only when it starts with `sid`'s header and the
rest is a tree under it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.resolveWorkspacePath
entries.docstring:
`resolveWorkspacePath`, before its normalisation: refuse a rewritten spelling, strip an
absolute `cwd` prefix, and map `.` or `cwd` to the root. An absolute path outside `cwd` is left as
it is, so normalising it refuses it as absolute. The comparison is on the character list, which
reduces in the kernel where `String.startsWith` does not.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.skillSet
entries.docstring:
The skills a compile hands the loader: the request's names without repeats, sorted
(`[...new Set(skillNames)].sort()`). Strings compare by code point here and by UTF-16 code unit in
TypeScript; the two agree on every name below U+10000, which a skill name is.

entries.statement: List String → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Event → List String × List AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Frame
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.step
entries.docstring:
One event, given the call ids announced so far: the new announced list and the frames. Native
payloads are carried as `null` here; the replay compares every neutral field.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.toolPlan
entries.docstring:
The tool plan: every tool its switch allows, in order, with `bash` withheld while a read-only
grant exists (a redirect would write what the grant protects).

entries.statement: Option Nat → Nat → List Bool → Nat × AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.StopReason
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.turnRun
entries.docstring:
The adapter's turn stop over the turns a run's model would take, in order: each flag says
whether that turn ran tools (so pi would ask the model again). A turn that ran none ends the run
`end_turn`; the turn that reaches the limit with tools still running is the last, ended by the
`terminate` hint, and the run ends `max_turns`. The first component is the turns taken.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.workspaceWriteVerdict
entries.docstring:
`workspaceWriteVerdict`: resolve the path, refuse the root with its own reason, and ask
`writeGrantVerdict` about the workspace-relative rest.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.writeAllowed
entries.docstring: May a tool of the compiled run write `candidate`? `workspaceWriteAllowed`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ConnectionFamily.credentialHeader
entries.docstring:
The header this family's substituted credential travels in. Three schemes, because the two
vendors disagree: Anthropic reads `x-api-key`, Azure reads `api-key`, and OpenAI reads a bearer.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ConnectionFamily.isOpenAIFamily
entries.docstring: The family relays the OpenAI dialects: it has a `WireProtocolForwarder` (ADR-0068 D2).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ConnectionFamily.pinsModel
entries.docstring:
Azure addresses a deployment, never a model name, so its adapter pins the relayed body's
`model`. Every other family relays the client's own choice (ADR-0068 D8).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ConnectionFamily.providerId
entries.docstring:
The registry id the resolver maps a connection onto: `anthropic-compatible` is served by the
`anthropic` adapter, so the router only ever sees four ids.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ConnectionFamily.speaks
entries.docstring:
Which protocol this family accepts. Anthropic Messages is translated by every adapter; the two
OpenAI dialects are relayed, and only by an OpenAI-family connection.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.Ingress.metered
entries.docstring: Whether the usage recorder meters a request on this path.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.Ingress.resolvesModelKey
entries.docstring:
Whether serving the path resolves (and so decrypts) the run's model key. Health is a process
probe and the tool routes stop after the run token, so none of them does.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.Route.existedBeforeIngress
entries.docstring: The route existed before this unit. The two OpenAI dialects did not, so they answered 404.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ToolType.isRelayable
entries.docstring:
The closed allowlist: only a tool the platform executes inside its own sandbox is relayed.
Everything else runs at the model vendor, past the egress policy and the connector model.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Agent.valid
entries.docstring:
The only `agents` check that is not a key: `agents_name_not_blank`. Empty instructions are
valid ("no extra instructions").

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.ApiKey.live
entries.docstring:
The key's own half of `authenticateApiKeyHash`'s admission query:
`revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now)`. Here `now` abstracts the
query's `greatest(now(), $now)` — the later of the database clock and the caller's clock — so a
caller cannot move a key's expiry by passing an earlier instant. The other half, that the key's
`workspace_principals` row is not revoked, is `Principal.apiKeyAdmitted`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ApiKey.ApiKey.valid
entries.docstring:
The checks of `api_keys` as a predicate on the concept: name, prefix and hash are not blank,
an expiry is after creation, and a revocation is not before creation.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.BrowserToken.live
entries.docstring:
`findActiveBrowserTokenByHash`'s row half: not revoked and not yet expired. This is only the
token row's own half of admission; spec §3.1.1's "Revocation" (the scoped run or session reaching
a terminal state, the minting principal revoked) is `Principal.browserTokenAdmitted`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.BrowserToken.valid
entries.docstring:
The checks of `browser_tokens` that are not the scope shape: expiry after creation, and a
revocation not before creation. (The hash has no not-blank check, unlike `api_keys`.)

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.AuthType.needsCredential
entries.docstring: `credentialedMcpAuthTypes`: every authentication type except `none` needs a credential.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Connector.valid
entries.docstring: Every `mcp_servers` check holds on the row (the two closed sets hold by the types).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.ToolConnector.valid
entries.docstring:
Every `mcp_servers` check holds on the tool row: the kind is not `mcp`, the `tool_config` is
a JSON object, a `postgres` connector names its credential, and the name is not blank.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Transport.isRemote
entries.docstring: `remoteMcpTransports`: the transports reached over a URL.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.SessionRuns.launch
entries.docstring:
Launch a run into a session. A request for another engine is refused (`409
session_engine_mismatch`) rather than re-pinning the session or running it anyway.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File.valid
entries.docstring:
Every `files` check holds on the row: the two path checks and the four content checks. The
closed set `files_kind_valid` holds by the type of `kind`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Invitation.Invitation.stateAt
entries.docstring: `invitationStateOf`: revoked, then accepted, then expired (`expiresAt ≤ now`), then pending.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Invitation.Invitation.unresolved
entries.docstring:
The partial unique index's notion of pending: neither accepted nor revoked, whatever the
clock says (`WHERE accepted_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Invitation.Invitation.valid
entries.docstring: The checks of `invitations` as a predicate on the concept.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.ModelConnection.credentialSecretName
entries.docstring: The secret name that holds this connection's credential.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.ModelConnection.toResource
entries.docstring:
`toModelConnectionResource`, given the stored credential if there is one: only whether it
exists reaches the resource.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Actor.wellFormed
entries.docstring:
The structural half of `Principal.isPrincipal`: a scope is present exactly for a browser
token; a membership principal came from a session (or a token it minted), names a user and no
key, and owns what it writes; an API-key principal came from a key (or a token it minted), names a
key and no user, and may own through the principal it acts for.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Kind.toStorage
entries.docstring: The storage spelling: `workspace_principals.kind` and the server's `PrincipalKind`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.MeResponse.acceptedCurrent
entries.docstring:
What `MeResponseSchema` accepts today: every field present and non-empty, `userId` null or
non-empty — whatever the kind.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.MeResponse.acceptedTarget
entries.docstring:
What the schema's own comment documents: additionally, `userId` is `null` for exactly an
API-key principal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Principal.active
entries.docstring:
`revoked_at IS NULL`: the filter `authenticateApiKeyHash`, `resolveMembership` and
`principalById` all apply to the `workspace_principals` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Principal.actsForValid
entries.docstring:
`workspace_principals_acts_for_api_key_only` and `workspace_principals_acts_for_not_self`: only
an API-key principal acts for someone, and never for itself.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.Project.defaultModelPair
entries.docstring:
`projects_default_model_pair` ("#129, mirroring `workspaces_default_model_pair`"): the default
connection and the default model are set together or not at all (the model is "the provider-side
model id paired with `defaultModelConnectionId`. NULL together"). This is the project rung of the
same rule `StartRunRequestSchema` states for a run's own override: "no layer of the
model-resolution ladder may mix a connection from one level with a model from another".

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.Project.listedBy
entries.docstring: Whether a listing with filter `f` includes the project (`archivedPredicate`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.Project.nameNotBlank
entries.docstring: `projects_name_not_blank`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.Project.state
entries.docstring: `isProjectArchived`: `archivedAt !== null`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.agentVia
entries.docstring: The run's agent, reached through its session (`runs` has no `agent_id`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.costNonNegative
entries.docstring: The cost part of `runs_counters_non_negative` (the counters are natural numbers).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.create
entries.docstring:
A new run as both stores create it: `queued`, no timestamps but `createdAt`, zero usage,
zero cost in USD, no price, accounting `pending`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.currencyUsd
entries.docstring: `runs_cost_currency_usd`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.durationMs
entries.docstring: `durationMs`: "`null` until both `startedAt` and `endedAt` exist", and never stored.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.endedAfterStarted
entries.docstring: `runs_ended_after_started`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.endedAtIffTerminal
entries.docstring:
`runs_ended_at_iff_terminal`: "A finished run has an end time and an unfinished one does
not." (a schema comment; no document states it, finding F-9).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.ownerVia
entries.docstring:
The run's owning principal, reached through its session (`runs` has no
`owner_principal_id`; `RunRecord.ownerPrincipalId` is "the exact workspace principal that owns
the session").

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.priceVersionMatches
entries.docstring:
`runs_price_version_matches_accounting_state`: a price table version exactly when some usage
is priced.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.stamp
entries.docstring:
What a store writes with a status change at instant `now`: `running` stamps `startedAt`; a
terminal status stamps `endedAt`, and a `startedAt` if the run never had one ("a run that is
finished without ever having been marked running still gets a start").

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.unpricedCostZero
entries.docstring: `runs_unpriced_cost_zero`: a run with no priced usage costs exactly zero.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.RunToken.expiryAfterCreated
entries.docstring: `run_tokens_expiry_after_created`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.RunToken.revokedAfterCreated
entries.docstring: `run_tokens_revoked_after_created`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.durable
entries.docstring: Whether frames of a kind carry a resume `id:` (are durable run events).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Secret.Envelope.wellFormed
entries.docstring:
The envelope checks: a named master key (`secrets_master_key_id_not_blank`), and every part at
its exact size (`…_wrapped_data_key_size`, `…_nonce_sizes`, `…_tag_sizes`), with a non-empty
ciphertext (`…_ciphertext_not_empty`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Secret.Secret.toResource
entries.docstring: `toSecretResource`: the resource a secret renders as.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.Session.enginePaired
entries.docstring:
ADR-0065's pairing: a session that carries an engine session id always names its engine.

`recordReportedSessionIdentity` is the one writer, and it writes both cells in one update, so the
state `engine = NULL ∧ engine_session_id ≠ NULL` is unreachable after migration 0025 backfills the
rows written before the column existed.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.Session.identityCurrent
entries.docstring:
Today's identity invariant: the SDK session id is absent or equals the platform id. Only the
application keeps it; `engine_session_id` is free text to the database.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.Session.launchMode
entries.docstring: `sessionForLaunch`: fresh until the SDK has reported an id, resume afterwards.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.Session.recordReported
entries.docstring:
`recordReportedSessionIdentity`: the runtime's reported SDK session id is recorded only when
it equals the platform id; any other id is refused (the function throws).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.Session.resumable
entries.docstring:
`resumable`: "active, and known to the SDK" (`row.status === 'active' &&
row.engineSessionId !== null`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.Transcript.projectKeyIsWorkspace
entries.docstring:
The transcript is stored under its workspace's own key: `projectKey` is the workspace id.
The repository refuses any other key; the database does not.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.TranscriptMessage.positionAtMostSequence
entries.docstring:
A delivery is never placed after itself: its position is its own sequence (first delivery)
or an earlier one (a redelivery).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Decimal.parse?
entries.docstring:
Parse a decimal literal: `-`? digits+ (`.` digits+)?. Anything else (empty, a `+`, spaces,
exponents, a bare `.`) is `none`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Expiry.durationMs?
entries.docstring: The lifetime of an expiry in milliseconds, `none` for `never` (`EXPIRY_MS`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRefusal.message
entries.docstring: The public message of each refusal, as `ShareService.publish` words it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share.budgetExhausted
entries.docstring:
The budget of a runnable share is exhausted: `spent_usd >= budget_cap_usd`. A share without a
budget is never exhausted (and never runnable).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share.dbValid
entries.docstring: The four non-closed-set checks of `shares`, on the typed row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share.modeOnlyForAgent
entries.docstring: `shares_agent_mode_only`: only an agent share has a mode.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share.publiclyOpen
entries.docstring:
A public link opens at `now` (before any passphrase): the share is public and live. This is
the availability test of `ShareService.resolve` and of the unscoped token lookup
`findShareWorkspace`, which only finds public shares.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share.resolveAt
entries.docstring:
`ShareService.resolve` at instant `now`: a closed link is unavailable whatever the passphrase;
an open link with a passphrase opens only for the right one; an open link without one opens.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share.stateAt
entries.docstring: The state of a share at instant `now`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share.toRow
entries.docstring: The share as a `shares` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share.url?
entries.docstring: The public URL a share carries on the wire: `/p/<token>` for a public share, absent otherwise.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share.wellPublished
entries.docstring:
A share as `ShareService.publish` writes it: the database checks hold; the share has a mode
exactly when its subject is an agent; it has a budget exactly when it is runnable; a non-session
share includes nothing; the token has the `pub_` prefix; and it starts unstopped, unrevoked,
unsuspended and with nothing spent.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ShareRunCharge.dbValid
entries.docstring: `share_run_charges_nonnegative`: the accumulated charge is `≥ 0`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ShareRunCharge.toRow
entries.docstring: The charge as a `share_run_charges` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ShareView.toRow
entries.docstring: The view as a `share_views` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.table
entries.docstring:
The table a subject lives in: the polymorphic target of `shares.subject_id`, which no foreign
key enforces.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Skill.Skill.valid
entries.docstring: Both `skills` checks hold on the row: `skills_name_shape` and `skills_skill_md_not_blank`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.isPriced
entries.docstring:
At least one ledger row is priced, so the run carries a price table version
(`accounting_state in ('complete', 'partial')`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.isSettled
entries.docstring: "Only `'complete'` is a settled answer."

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.Counters.totalTokens
entries.docstring: `totalTokens`: "Derived by the server: the sum of the four counters above".

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord.unpricedIsZero
entries.docstring:
An unpriced response is "recorded, at `cost_usd = '0'`, rather than dropped": the
repository's invariant, which no database check enforces.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord.wellFormed
entries.docstring:
The two checks of `run_usage_records`: a non-negative cost (the counters are natural numbers
already) and the settlement currency.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.WireProtocol.columnDefault
entries.docstring:
The column's default, which is what lets a gateway pod from the release before the column
existed keep inserting rows while `migrate` runs at container start.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Workspace.Workspace.valid
entries.docstring:
The row invariants the database enforces on a workspace (its checks), as a predicate on the
concept: a well-formed slug and a non-blank name. The default-model pair holds by construction.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.CommonProblemCode.status
entries.docstring: `COMMON_PROBLEM_CODES[code]`: the HTTP status each shared code travels under.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.idKind?
entries.docstring: The identifier kind of a table whose primary key is a single `id` column, if it has one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.agentRow
entries.docstring:
An agent as its `agents` row, stamped with `ts` for both timestamps. The stored policy's
content is not modelled (`Agent.policyStored` says only whether it is non-`NULL`), so a stored
policy is rendered as the placeholder `{}`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.checkSql
entries.docstring:
The SQL body of each check `clusterCheckHolds` gives a meaning to, as `drizzle-kit` rendered it in
the latest snapshot (`Er.Snapshot.file`): the semantics above are the semantics of exactly these
expressions, and the conformance suite fails when a body changes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.clusterCheckHolds
entries.docstring:
The semantics of every check on the cluster's tables that is not a closed set, read from the
check bodies in
`packages/core/src/db/schema/{agent-versions,agent-version-evaluations,agents,skills,files,mcp-servers}.ts`. A check
passes unless it is false, so a comparison with a `NULL` column passes (SQL's three-valued
reading), and a disjunction passes when one of its disjuncts is not false. That is how the MCP
checks of `mcp_servers`, guarded by `kind <> 'mcp' or …`, pass on a tool connector's `NULL`
transport. The other guard columns are `NOT NULL`, so their `NULL` case only arises in states
`consistent` already refuses. `size_bytes` is compared as the text PostgreSQL renders a `bigint`
in, a version's `number` and an evaluation's `passed` and `total` as the text of an `integer`
(`positiveNumeral`, `numeralValue`), and `tool_config` as the
text of a `jsonb` value (`Connector.jsonbObject`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.consistent
entries.docstring:
The states PostgreSQL can hold for this cluster: `Er.Core.consistent` under today's schema,
and the cluster's own checks.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.tables
entries.docstring: The fourteen tables of the catalog cluster, in barrel order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Cluster.tables
entries.docstring: The tables each cluster models.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Configuration.clusterForeignKeys
entries.docstring:
Every foreign key that starts or ends in the cluster, as (declaring table, constraint name,
target table): the cluster's own references to the root and to `secrets`, and every reference
from elsewhere into a cluster table.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Configuration.clusterTables
entries.docstring: The tables of the configuration cluster.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Configuration.configCheckHolds
entries.docstring:
The semantics of the non-closed-set checks this cluster owns or depends on, by constraint
name; any other name holds here (the owning cluster refines it).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Configuration.consistentConfig
entries.docstring: The states PostgreSQL can hold, with this cluster's checks given their meaning.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Configuration.runtimeConnectionsTyped
entries.docstring:
Target (RF-204, `docs/sdk/04-api-specification.md` §5.5): every secret a runtime profile names
is a runtime connection. Today nothing enforces it; the foreign key accepts any secret of the
workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Identity.CheckExpr
entries.docstring: The shapes the 36 non-closed-set checks of the identity tables take.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Identity.checks
entries.docstring:
Every non-closed-set check of the identity tables, with its meaning, table by table in
`tables` order and, within a table, in the order `catalogue` lists them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Identity.consistent
entries.docstring:
Today's identity cluster is consistent: every constraint of `catalogue` holds
(`Er.Core.consistent`), and on the fourteen identity tables every refined check holds and every
cell is well typed.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Identity.everySourceHasPrincipal
entries.docstring:
RF-101's target: every membership and every API key of a state has a principal
("one human principal per Membership and one machine principal per APIKey").

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Identity.relationships
entries.docstring: Every foreign key the fourteen identity tables declare.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Identity.tables
entries.docstring:
The fourteen tables of the identity cluster. `cli_sessions` (SDK-10, #242, ADR-0083) is one
`aw login` of one person, referenced through their membership. Then come ADR-0134's endpoint
clients: what one external platform may reach (`endpoint_clients`), the agents it names
(`endpoint_client_agents`), the API keys bound to it (`endpoint_client_api_keys`) and the OAuth
codes and tokens issued to it for a member (`oauth_tokens`, part 3). The last,
`runtime_verifications`, is the workspace's record of which runtime drivers passed Test Runtime
(#827); it references only the workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.chargesRunKey
entries.docstring: `(share_run_charges.run_id, workspace_id) → runs (id, workspace_id)`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.chargesShareKey
entries.docstring: `(share_run_charges.share_id, workspace_id) → shares (id, workspace_id)`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.checkSemantics?
entries.docstring:
The semantics of a non-closed-set check of the cluster on one row, by name; `none` for a
name the cluster does not own.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.checkSql
entries.docstring:
The SQL of each non-closed-set check of the cluster, as `migrations/meta/0025_snapshot.json`
records it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.consistent
entries.docstring:
The states PostgreSQL can hold, as far as this cluster knows: every constraint of every table
holds, and the cluster's own checks hold with their semantics.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.sharesCreatorKey
entries.docstring:
`(shares.workspace_id, created_by) → memberships (workspace_id, user_id)`: the creator is a
member of the share's workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.sharesPublisherKey
entries.docstring: `(shares.workspace_id, publisher_principal_id) → workspace_principals (workspace_id, id)`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.tables
entries.docstring: The tables of the publication cluster.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.viewsShareKey
entries.docstring: `(share_views.share_id, workspace_id) → shares (id, workspace_id)`, `ON DELETE CASCADE`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Witness.state
entries.docstring:
Two workspaces. `w1` has two members (`u1` its owner, `u2` a viewer) and an API key, each
with its principal; a model connection (the workspace and project default) and its credential; a
runtime connection and the profile that names it, and a passing Test Runtime of its driver; a connector with its credential; an agent with
a file, a skill and the connector assigned and a grant to the viewer; a project that links the
file and the connector; a session with its transcript and a message; a completed run with an
event, a usage row, a run token and a browser token; an audit event; an invitation; and a public
agent share with a view and a charge. `w2` has `u2` as its owner and an agent of its own.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.AuditAction
entries.docstring:
`AUDIT_ACTIONS` (`auditActions` in the schema): the control-plane actions the audit trail
records.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.AuditEvent
entries.docstring:
One audit row: who, what, to which thing, when. The labels are snapshots taken when the row
was written; `subjectId` is text with no foreign key, because the subject may be gone.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.Cardinality
entries.docstring: How many parent rows a child row links through a foreign key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.auditCells
entries.docstring: The cells of an `audit_events` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.fkCardinality
entries.docstring: The cardinality a foreign key imposes on its child rows.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.messageCells
entries.docstring: The cells of a `session_messages` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.projectCells
entries.docstring: The cells of a `projects` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.runCells
entries.docstring: The cells of a `runs` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.runEventCells
entries.docstring: The cells of a `run_events` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.runTokenCells
entries.docstring: The cells of a `run_tokens` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.sessionCells
entries.docstring: The cells of a `sessions` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.terminalWires
entries.docstring:
The wire spellings of the terminal run statuses, as `terminalRunStatuses` renders them into
`runs_ended_at_iff_terminal`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.transcriptCells
entries.docstring: The cells of a `session_transcripts` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.usageCells
entries.docstring: The cells of a `run_usage_records` row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.workCheck
entries.docstring:
The semantics of each check of the work tables that is not a closed set, by constraint name,
reading a row under SQL's three-valued logic: a comparison with a `NULL` operand is `NULL`, and a
check passes unless it is `false`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.workCheckSql
entries.docstring:
The exact bodies `drizzle-kit` rendered for the work tables' other checks (compared with
the latest snapshot (`Er.Snapshot.file`) by the conformance suite, which is a snapshot that
carries the three session-state tables this cluster gained in 0026).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.workConsistent
entries.docstring:

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.workTables
entries.docstring:
The fourteen tables of the work cluster.

ENG-06 (#305) added the last three: `session_state_streams`, `session_state_entries` and
`session_state_blobs` are the engine-scoped generalisation of `session_transcripts` and
`session_messages`, and they belong to the same cluster because they are the same fact about a
session told for every engine rather than for one. The Claude pair stays until the contract step of
the expand/contract migration (ADR-0071).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzDecide.decode_step_is_well_formed
entries.docstring:
Every step of `decodeURIComponent` that succeeds reads well-formed UTF-8: a plain character, or
a `%HH` escape whose lead byte is ASCII, or a lead byte in `C2`…`F4` followed by exactly the number of
continuation bytes (`10xxxxxx`) it announces, encoding a scalar value, and the rest decodes too. So
by induction on the input no lone continuation byte, lead byte `F5`…`FF`, truncated or interrupted
sequence, overlong form or surrogate is ever accepted anywhere in it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzDecide.encoded_traversal_stays_protected

Traversal and encoding attacks on the prefix rule: dot segments (plain, percent-encoded, doubly
encoded, overlong UTF-8), overlong slashes, surrogate escapes, encoded slashes and letters,
backslashes, doubled slashes and case all land on the protected surface, and an upper-case `/P/` is
not released as public.

The feedback cell is keyed by its sub-resource and belongs to the session scope alone: a run
scope never reaches `POST /api/runs/:id/feedback`, and the session scope's `run` verb on `runs`
does not extend to `interrupt` (or any other sub-resource but `feedback`).

`/p`, case-sensitively, and not under `/api` in any case.

entries.docstring:
A run-scoped browser token is allowed only reads of its run, including equivalent UUID
spellings of its id (the row or a sub-resource read with `GET`/`HEAD`).

entries.docstring:
No browser token of either kind is ever allowed to mint a token, and when it is allowed a read
of `runs`, its path names a row: `tokens` is in no grammar, and a scope reads one run, never the
collection.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzDecide.secrets_are_owner_only
entries.docstring:
Secrets are Owner-only: no other role, whatever path spelling, method, ownership or scope it
supplies, is ever allowed on `secrets`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzDecide.session_scoped_token_reaches_only_run_reads_and_agent_runs

A session-scoped browser token is allowed nothing but reads of a single run, the `run` verb
on `agents` (starting a run) and the `run` verb on a run's `feedback` sub-resource (rating it),
outside the public surface. No other `runs` sub-resource reaches the `run` verb: `interrupt` stays
out.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzDecide.uri_decode_rejects_bad_lead_and_continuation_bytes
entries.docstring:
`decodeURIComponent` throws where JavaScript's does on malformed bytes: after a 2-, 3- or 4-byte
lead, any byte that is not a continuation byte (`%C2%41`, `%E0%A0%41`, `%F0%90%80%41`); a lone
continuation byte `%80`…`%BF`; and every lead byte `%F5`…`%FF`, whatever continuation bytes follow.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzDecide.uri_decode_rejects_overlong_and_surrogate_forms
entries.docstring:
`decodeURIComponent` throws on every overlong 2-byte form (`%C0`/`%C1` with any continuation
byte), on the overlong 3- and 4-byte forms and the out-of-range 4-byte form at their boundaries, and
on the surrogate range `%ED%A0%80`…`%ED%BF%BF`, while it decodes the shortest forms on either
side of each bound.

entries.statement: ∀ (lead : Nat) (conts : List Nat) (cp : Nat), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.utf8CodePoint lead conts = some cp → (conts.length = 1 → 128 ≤ cp) ∧ (conts.length = 2 → 2048 ≤ cp) ∧ (conts.length = 3 → 65536 ≤ cp ∧ cp ≤ 1114111) ∧ ¬(55296 ≤ cp ∧ cp ≤ 57343) ∧ 1 ≤ conts.length ∧ conts.length ≤ 3
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzDecide.utf8_accepts_only_shortest_scalar_values
entries.docstring:
Every UTF-8 sequence the decoder accepts is the shortest form of a Unicode scalar value: a
2-byte sequence encodes at least `U+0080`, a 3-byte one at least `U+0800`, a 4-byte one lies in
`U+10000`…`U+10FFFF`, no accepted code point is a surrogate, and only 2- to 4-byte sequences are
read. An overlong `/` or `.` therefore never decodes into a path separator or dot segment.

A Viewer writes nothing but its own shares and workspace memberships: every write it is
allowed is on `shares` or `workspaces`, for a row it owns or a collection.

the run (`// ponytail:` in `authorizeToolCall`, until S2-02e).

B's connector is the one `403 tool_not_in_run`, whatever that connector is.

used for another run id, regardless of the resolver's state.

connector, and the same call is refused once the run ends or the connector is disabled.

bearer, an invalid token and an expired token keep their codes and their order.

bootstrap mints nothing once `mayOpenSession` refuses it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzRunToken.visitor_session_pins_the_resolved_version
entries.docstring:
A visitor session opened on an environment is pinned to the version that environment pointed
at (`sessions.agent_version_id = resolved.versionId`); with `session_version_stable`, no later
push, promote or rollback moves it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzRunToken.visitor_token_has_allow_witness
entries.docstring:
The refusals are not vacuous: the token reads a run of its own session, starts a turn in it
and rates one of its runs, and the same requests for another session are refused.

entries.statement: ∀ (loopback sameOrigin admitted : Bool) (allowed : List String) (origin : Option String) (opened : Option AgentWorkspace.SessionId) (scope : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.Scope), AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.mintAfterOpen (AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.openVerdict loopback sameOrigin allowed origin AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.OpenMode.session) admitted opened = some scope → AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.openVerdict loopback sameOrigin allowed origin AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.OpenMode.session ≠ AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.OpenVerdict.refused ∧ ∃ s, opened = some s ∧ scope = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.Scope.session s
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzRunToken.visitor_token_minted_only_after_open_verdict
entries.docstring:
A visitor token is minted only after `mayOpenSession` admits the bootstrap: whatever the
loopback flag, same-origin verdict, allowed list, `Origin` and the route's later steps, a minted
token means `openVerdict` did not refuse, and its scope is the one session `runtime.open` opened.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.SessionId) (req : AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.Request), AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.visitorDecision (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.Scope.session s) req = AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.Decision.proceed → req.sessionId = some s.val ∧ (req.resource = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.Resource.runs ∧ req.op = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Operation.read ∧ req.pathId.isSome = true ∨ req.resource = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.Resource.agents ∧ req.op = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Operation.run ∨ req.resource = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.Resource.runs ∧ req.op = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Operation.run ∧ req.sub = some "feedback")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzRunToken.visitor_token_proceeds_only_inside_its_grammar
entries.docstring:
The token goes on only inside its grammar and its own session: reading one run by id (and its
events), running an agent, or rating a run (`feedback`), and in each case for session `s`.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.SessionId) (req : AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.Request), req.sessionId ≠ some s.val → AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.visitorDecision (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.Scope.session s) req = AgentWorkspace.Authz.VisitorSession.Decision.deny 403 "token_out_of_scope"
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzRunToken.visitor_token_reaches_only_its_session
entries.docstring:
A visitor's session-scoped token for session `s` is refused with `403 token_out_of_scope` on
every request naming another session `s′ ≠ s`: reading one of its runs or their events, a turn
whose body names it, and a rating of one of its runs. Whatever the route, the scope grammar or the
session match refuses it, and both with the same code.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzTenancy.accepted_key_cannot_escape_the_workspace_root
entries.docstring:
A key or prefix the object store accepts cannot step outside the workspace root, whatever the
caller sends: a non-empty accepted key has no empty segment, no `.` or `..` segment, and no segment
spelling the reserved metadata marker in any case.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzTenancy.foreign_run_is_indistinguishable_from_absent
entries.docstring:
A run of another workspace is indistinguishable from no run at all: adding a foreign run row
(with any id, including the one asked for) changes no run route's answer.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzTenancy.forged_scope_is_refused
entries.docstring:
A value `WorkspaceScope` did not mint — a cast object literal, an
`Object.create(WorkspaceScope.prototype)`, anything that is not an object — is refused by
`requireWorkspaceScope`, whatever workspace id it carries; only a minted scope passes, unchanged.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzTenancy.run_route_sees_only_the_callers_workspace
entries.docstring:
No run route lets a caller observe another workspace's runs: two states whose runs of the
caller's workspace are the same give every run route the same answer, for every route, caller,
run id and continuation.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzTenancy.scoped_read_is_blind_to_other_workspaces
entries.docstring:
A scoped read cannot observe another workspace: two states that agree on workspace `ws`'s
rows of a table give every read scoped to `ws` the same answer, whatever else they hold.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.AuthzTenancy.workspace_resolvers_conceal_foreign_workspaces
entries.docstring:
The workspace routes cannot be used to enumerate workspaces: two repositories that hold the
same memberships for the caller give both resolvers the same answer, however many other
workspaces (or other people's memberships) either holds — "no such workspace" and "not a member"
are one `404`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptCatalog.forged_id_names_a_row_of_the_writers_workspace
entries.docstring:
Whatever value a writer puts in the id column `c` of a tenant-paired reference, any row of the
parent table carrying that id belongs to the writer's workspace: the database refuses every
other state.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptCatalog.grants_body_admits_only_distinct_uuids
entries.docstring:
Whatever ids a caller sends, the grants body the schema admits is a list of distinct ids, each
the lower-cased form of a canonical UUID the caller sent, as many as were sent: two spellings of
one id never reach the repository as two rows.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptCatalog.grants_name_only_active_membership_principals
entries.docstring:
No grant replacement, whatever ids it names, grants an agent to an API-key principal, a
revoked principal or a principal of another workspace: every id written names an active
membership principal of this workspace.
