A caller who does not own an agent and whose user no `agent_grants` row of that agent names
is never `permitted` to run it, whatever else the input holds (an API-key caller, which has no
user, never is).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptConfiguration.connector_cannot_use_another_workspaces_secret
entries.docstring:
Whatever secret id a writer puts on a connector as its credential, naming a secret of another
workspace makes the state inconsistent: the composite key finds no secret with that id in the
connector's workspace, and the id identifies one secret.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptIdentity.browser_token_acts_only_as_its_minter_in_its_workspace
entries.docstring:
Whatever principal row a caller gets a browser token checked against, an admitted token acts
only as the principal its row names as minter, and only if that principal is in the token's own
workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptIdentity.browser_token_acts_only_on_its_own_scoped_row
entries.docstring:
Whatever scoped row a request resolves, a browser token is admitted only on the very run or
session its row names: the admitted row's scope is the token's scope.

Whatever API-key id a principal row names, in every consistent state the key with that id
belongs to the principal's workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptIdentity.foreign_membership_cannot_back_a_principal

Whatever membership id a principal row names, in every consistent state the membership with
that id belongs to the principal's workspace: no principal is backed by another workspace's
member.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptIdentity.foreign_principal_cannot_mint_a_browser_token
entries.docstring:
Whatever principal id a browser-token row names as its minter, in every consistent state the
principal with that id belongs to the token's workspace: no token is minted in the name of
another workspace's principal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptIdentity.foreign_run_cannot_scope_a_browser_token

Whatever run id a run-scoped browser-token row names, in every consistent state the run with
that id belongs to the token's workspace: a token cannot be scoped to another workspace's run.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptIdentity.foreign_session_cannot_scope_a_browser_token

Whatever session id a session-scoped browser-token row names, in every consistent state the
session with that id belongs to the token's workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptIdentity.forged_principal_source_is_refused

inconsistent: the forged row is refused.

acts for a principal is refused once that principal is revoked or its membership is gone (or it
cannot be re-read at all): the key is not admitted, its principal no longer resolves, and no browser
token it minted is admitted.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptIdentity.token_for_one_run_cannot_act_on_another_run

A token minted for run `R` cannot act on any other run `R′`, whatever that run's status, the
minter, or the instant.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ConceptIdentity.token_for_one_session_cannot_act_on_another_session

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ContractsFoundation.accepted_id_has_no_path_character

No path-significant or control character appears in an id that `isUuid` accepts, whatever
JSON value the attacker sends.

Every body `readProblem` accepts, over all JSON an attacker can send, yields a code of at
least one UTF-16 unit.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.ContractsFoundation.accepted_standard_envelope_has_no_extra_key
entries.docstring:
An accepted standard envelope, whatever the attacker sent, has `error` as its only top-level
key and only `code`, `message`, `details` and the deprecated `detail` inside it: no extra field
reaches the client.

An accepted environment's credential-shaped variables all hold this run's gateway token.

The load-bearing half: it names no provider and no engine, so a variable nobody has heard of is
covered by it as long as it is spelled like a credential.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.EngineSandboxEnv.accepted_environment_has_no_master_key
entries.docstring: An accepted environment carries no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, under any casing.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.EngineSandboxEnv.an_unheard_of_provider_key_is_refused
entries.docstring:
The negative witness: a provider key in a variable this repository has never heard of is
refused, and the refusal names the variable.

entries.docstring:
A compile that succeeded produces an environment the sandbox contract accepts.

Quantified over the capabilities and the engine arm, so it is a statement about the port and not
about one adapter: whatever an engine's `compile` decides about its own policy, it cannot reach
the success arm with an environment that failed the check.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.EngineSandboxEnv.todays_composed_environment_is_accepted
entries.docstring: The positive witness: the environment every Claude run composes today is accepted.

Rule 3 of `tenancy.test.ts`: whoever deletes every foreign key over an undeclared `*_id`
column of a table (so that the pairing rule has nothing left to check) fails the
"every reference is declared" gate.

key is left to be unpaired) but fails the declared-reference gate, which is why rule 3 exists.

tenant-carrying row of a different workspace is not a state the database accepts, whatever ids
the writer copied into the row.

connection pins. Never a third thing, and never another connection's.

A refusal sends nothing upstream at all, so neither allowlist is even reached: the hosted-tool
and wrong-protocol rules are decided before any network call.

entries.docstring:
A token minted for one run never reaches another run's connection, whatever the protocol: the
expected-run check happens before the resolver is consulted at all.

entries.docstring:
The application's route table is exactly §9's fenced block: the six model routes, in order,
then the three tool routes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.GatewayIngress.model_ingress_is_route

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.GatewayIngress.no_protocol_forwards_on_a_revoked_token
entries.docstring: No protocol forwards on a revoked token, however well formed its claims are.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.GatewayIngress.no_protocol_forwards_on_an_expired_token
entries.docstring: No protocol forwards on an expired token.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.GatewayIngress.no_protocol_forwards_on_an_invalid_token

entries.docstring:
The caller's run token never travels upstream. It arrives in `authorization`, which the
allowlist does not admit, so no relayed client header carries it — and the gateway's own
`authorization` carries the substituted credential instead.

entries.docstring:
Every unauthenticated outcome, across the whole protocol × family product, forwards nothing.
The witness for the statements above, spelled out cell by cell.

The `authorization` header a caller sent is dropped rather than relayed, so an
`Authorization: Bearer <run token>` cannot reach the upstream even by accident. The list is closed by
name: `openai-organization` and `openai-project` do not travel either, so the caller cannot choose
which account on the stored credential serves and is billed for the turn (ADR-0068 D7, D10).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.GatewayIngress.the_client_response_never_carries_the_credential
entries.docstring:
The client-visible response never carries the stored credential, because it is rebuilt from a
name allowlist that contains no credential-bearing header.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.GatewayIngress.tool_ingress_is_unmetered
entries.docstring: The tool routes are never metered: they are dispatched before the model boundary.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.GatewayIngress.tool_ingress_never_resolves_a_model_key
entries.docstring: The tool routes never resolve, and so never decrypt, the run's model key.

entries.statement: ∀ (family : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ConnectionFamily) (credential : String) (clientHeaders : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.Header) (h : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.Header), h ∈ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.upstreamHeaders family credential clientHeaders → h.name = family.credentialHeader ∧ h.value = credential ∨ h = { name := "content-type", value := "application/json" } ∨ h ∈ clientHeaders ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.travelsUpstream h.name = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.GatewayIngress.upstream_headers_are_exactly_the_allowlist
entries.docstring:
Every header the gateway sends upstream is one of exactly three things: the substituted
credential, the fixed `content-type`, or a client header the allowlist admitted. Nothing else is
relayed, so the caller's own collection cannot smuggle a header through.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.ok c → ∃ b t w p, r.gateway = some (b, t, w) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.ofWire? w = some p ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.modelRequests c.connection = [(AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.stripTrailingSlashes b ++ "/v1" ++ p.path, "Bearer " ++ t)]
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Mastra.every_model_request_goes_to_the_gateway_with_the_run_token
entries.docstring:
Every model request an accepted configuration can issue targets the gateway's base URL plus
`/v1` and the connection's own protocol path, carries the run token as `Authorization: Bearer`,
and there is exactly one such endpoint. Model requests only: an HTTP connector reaches its own
host, and is not one.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.ok c → r.environmentClean = true ∧ ∀ (name : String), name ∈ r.envNames → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.isDatabaseEnvName name = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Mastra.no_accepted_run_carries_a_database_credential
entries.docstring:
An accepted request's **platform** environment (`request.env`) carries no provider credential,
and no variable of it is a database connection variable by the `DATABASE_ENV` pattern
(`DATABASE_URL` or `*_DATABASE_URL`, libpq's `PG*`, `LIBSQL_*`/`TURSO_*`, in any case): memory goes
through the platform's store, so the platform's own environment holds no database to reach. This
covers only the platform's own environment: a tenant's stdio connector may still carry its own
database secret in its own `env`, merged in after this check, so a tenant's database-backed MCP
server keeps working (ADR-0084 D2; Owner decision on #309).

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (candidate : String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.removeAllowed c candidate = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some c.grants ∧ ∃ relative segments, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.resolveWorkspacePath c.cwd candidate = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Resolved.relative relative ∧ AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.protectedDirectory) c.grants relative = AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Verdict.ok segments ∧ segments.isPrefixOf [AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.protectedDirectory] = false ∧ ∀ (g : AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant), g ∈ c.grants → g.readOnly = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.covers g segments = false ∧ segments.isPrefixOf g.segments = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Mastra.no_permitted_removal_takes_a_read_only_grant
entries.docstring:
No removal or move the filesystem wrapper permits takes a protected location with it: the path
resolved inside the workspace, may itself be written, and its subtree holds no read-only grant of
the request and not the adapter's own directory. The write rule is about the target; this is the
subtree rule `deleteFile`, `rmdir` and `moveFile`'s source add to it.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (candidate : String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.writeAllowed c candidate = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some c.grants ∧ c.cwd = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.stripTrailingSlashes r.cwd ∧ ∃ relative segments, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.resolveWorkspacePath c.cwd candidate = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Resolved.relative relative ∧ AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.protectedDirectory) c.grants relative = AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Verdict.ok segments ∧ ∀ (g : AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant), g ∈ c.grants → g.readOnly = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.covers g segments = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Mastra.no_permitted_write_lands_in_a_read_only_grant
entries.docstring:
No write the filesystem wrapper permits lands inside a read-only grant of the request, however
the path is spelled: the grants it enforces are the request's own, normalised; the root it
resolves against is the request's `cwd`; an allowed write resolved to a workspace-relative path,
and that path normalises outside every read-only grant.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.ok c → c.observability.telemetry = false ∧ c.observability.exporters = [] ∧ ∀ (env : List (String × String)), List.lookup "MASTRA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED" (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.installedEnvironment env) = some "1" ∧ List.lookup "MASTRA_OFFLINE" (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.installedEnvironment env) = some "1" ∧ ∀ (e : String × String), e ∈ env → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.keptVariable e = true → e ∈ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.installedEnvironment env
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Mastra.observability_is_off_for_every_compiled_agent
entries.docstring:
Observability and telemetry exporters are off for every compiled agent, and — whatever the
runner's process environment held, the switches included with other values — the environment
Mastra loads under says `MASTRA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` and `MASTRA_OFFLINE=1`, and keeps every other
variable but an empty provider base URL. That no `Mastra` instance is constructed is the module
header's hypothesis, enforced by the boundary suite.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.ok c → (∃ b t w p, r.gateway = some (b, t, w) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.ofWire? w = some p ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.modelSpecOf c.connection = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.ModelSpec.provider (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.providerSpec c.connection) ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.providerSpec c.connection).baseURL = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.stripTrailingSlashes b ++ "/v1" ∧ ((AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.providerSpec c.connection).factory = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Factory.createAnthropic ↔ p = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.anthropicMessages) ∧ ((AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.providerSpec c.connection).option = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.AuthOption.authToken ↔ p = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.anthropicMessages) ∧ ((AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.providerSpec c.connection).method = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Method.responses ↔ p = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.openaiResponses)) ∧ ∀ (id : String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.modelSpecOf c.connection ≠ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.ModelSpec.routedString id
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Mastra.the_model_is_an_explicit_provider_at_the_gateway
entries.docstring:
The model of every accepted agent is the explicit provider `mastraProviderSpec` decides, at
the gateway's `/v1`: built with `createAnthropic` and the token as its `authToken` exactly for the
Messages protocol, with `createOpenAI` and the token as its `apiKey` otherwise, through
`.responses()` exactly for the Responses protocol; and never a `"provider/model"` string.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → ∃ b t w, r.gateway = some (b, t, w) ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.modelRequests c.connection).length = 1 ∧ ∀ (req : String × String), req ∈ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.modelRequests c.connection → req.fst = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.stripTrailingSlashes b ++ "/v1" ++ c.connection.protocol.path ∧ req.snd = "Bearer " ++ t
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.OpenAiAgents.every_model_request_goes_to_the_gateway_with_the_run_token
entries.docstring:
Every model request an accepted configuration can issue targets the gateway's base URL plus
`/v1`, carries the run token as `Authorization: Bearer`, and there is exactly one such endpoint.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (candidate : String) (segments : List String), AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) c.grants candidate = AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Verdict.ok segments → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some c.grants ∧ ∀ (g : AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant), g ∈ c.grants → g.readOnly = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.covers g segments = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.OpenAiAgents.no_permitted_write_lands_in_a_read_only_grant
entries.docstring:
No write the compiled Editor permits lands inside a read-only grant of the request: the grants
it enforces are the request's own, normalised, and an allowed write is outside every read-only one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.OpenAiAgents.tracing_is_disabled_for_every_compiled_run
entries.docstring:
Every compiled run has tracing disabled. The SDK's side — `setTracingDisabled(true)` before
`run`, and no trace export after it — is the declared hypothesis the boundary suite enforces.

entries.statement: have grants := [{ directory := false, segments := ["config", "app.yaml"], readOnly := true }]; (AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict none grants "config/app.yaml").isOk = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict none grants "config/other.yaml" = AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Verdict.ok ["config", "other.yaml"]
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PathGrant.a_file_grant_does_not_cover_its_siblings
entries.docstring: A file grant protects exactly itself, and a directory grant protects its descendants.

entries.statement: have grants := [{ directory := true, segments := ["docs"], readOnly := true }]; AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict none grants "docs-private/secret.md" = AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Verdict.ok ["docs-private", "secret.md"] ∧ AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict none grants "scratch/out.md" = AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Verdict.ok ["scratch", "out.md"]
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PathGrant.a_name_that_starts_with_a_grant_is_not_inside_it
entries.docstring:
Containment is by segment: a sibling whose name merely starts with a grant is writable.

The positive witness, and the direction that matters — a prefix comparison the other way round
would treat `docs` as covering nothing and allow a write into it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PathGrant.absolute_paths_are_refused
entries.docstring:
An absolute path — POSIX or Windows — is refused rather than read as a relative one.

The Windows arms matter because a grant composed on one platform is enforced on another: `C:\x`
read as a relative path is one oddly-named file *inside* the sandbox, which is not what its
author meant.

entries.statement: ∀ (protectedDirectory : Option String) (grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant) (candidate : String) (segments : List String), AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict protectedDirectory grants candidate = AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Verdict.ok segments → ∀ (g : AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant), g ∈ grants → g.readOnly = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.covers g segments = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PathGrant.allowed_write_is_outside_every_read_only_grant
entries.docstring: An allowed write lands outside every read-only grant. The claim itself.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PathGrant.an_unreadable_grant_refuses_the_whole_list
entries.docstring: A grant list with one unreadable entry is refused whole, never narrowed by dropping it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PathGrant.climbing_above_the_root_is_refused
entries.docstring:
A `..` that climbs above the workspace root is refused rather than clamped.

Clamping — treating `../../etc/passwd` as `etc/passwd` — is the repair a careless normaliser
makes, and it turns an escape into a write inside the sandbox at a path nobody granted.

entries.statement: have grants := [{ directory := true, segments := ["docs"], readOnly := true }]; (AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict none grants "docs/spec.md").isOk = false ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict none grants "docs/./spec.md").isOk = false ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict none grants "notes/../docs/spec.md").isOk = false ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict none grants "docs/nested/../spec.md").isOk = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PathGrant.every_spelling_of_a_covered_path_is_refused
entries.docstring:
Every spelling of a path inside a read-only directory grant is refused a write.

Written as a table of the shapes an escape is actually written in, because the property that
matters is not "one of them is refused" but "the redundant spellings all normalise to the same
thing and none of them gets through".

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Pi.every_model_request_goes_to_the_gateway_with_the_run_token
entries.docstring:
Every model request an accepted configuration can issue targets the gateway's base URL plus
`/v1/messages`, carries the run token as `Authorization: Bearer`, and there is exactly one such
endpoint; the key the provider is given is the public placeholder, never the token.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (name candidate : String), name = "write" ∨ name = "edit" → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.guard c name (some candidate) = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some c.grants ∧ c.cwd = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.stripTrailingSlashes r.cwd ∧ ∃ relative segments, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.resolveWorkspacePath c.cwd candidate = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Resolved.relative relative ∧ AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.writeGrantVerdict (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.protectedDirectory) c.grants relative = AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Verdict.ok segments ∧ ∀ (g : AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant), g ∈ c.grants → g.readOnly = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.covers g segments = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Pi.no_permitted_write_lands_in_a_read_only_grant
entries.docstring:
No write the guard permits lands inside a read-only grant of the request, however the path is
spelled — relative, or absolute under the sandbox root: the grants it enforces are the request's
own, normalised; the root it resolves against is the request's `cwd`; an allowed `write` or `edit`
resolved to a workspace-relative path, and that path normalises outside every read-only grant.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Pi.the_pinned_loader_admits_only_platform_resources
entries.docstring:
The pinned resource loader admits only what the platform materialised for this run — built
from the compiled configuration alone: a placed skill the run grants, or the agent's instructions —
and never anything under `~/.pi`, under `~/.agents` or from project discovery, whatever is present
on the host.

entries.docstring: Any stored state composes at or under the ceiling: an `ok` run has no widening left.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PolicyCeiling.composed_run_refuses_only_engine_or_model
entries.docstring: A refusal names only the engine and the model, exactly as `meet_le_ceiling` leaves them.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PolicyCeiling.composed_run_refuses_resolved_model_outside
entries.docstring: A model the S1-23 ladder resolves outside the ceiling is refused, and the refusal names it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.PolicyCeiling.composed_tools_subset_ceiling
entries.docstring:
Every connector a composed run keeps is one the ceiling's `tools` lists (C16: the snapshot
records only these).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Release.session_version_stable
entries.docstring:
No step changes the version of a started conversation: not `push`, `point`, `promote` or
`rollback`, and not a second `startSession` for the same conversation.

entries.statement: ∀ (t : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score) (r r' : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release) (op : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step t r op = Except.ok r' → ∀ (a : AgentWorkspace.AgentId), (r'.versions a).length = (r.versions a).length + if op.addsVersionTo a = true then 1 else 0
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.Release.ui_edit_is_a_version
entries.docstring:
Every content-changing operation adds exactly one version, and every other operation adds
none: a UI edit is a `push`, so it is a version.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.RunCompose.master_key_never_compiles
entries.docstring: The compiler refuses a provider master key instead of emitting an environment containing it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.RunCompose.policy_keeps_read_denials
entries.docstring:
Stored policy cannot drop a checkbox-derived denial.

The union moved into the Claude adapter with ENG-04b (#325); the rule did not.
`Theorems/Refinement/EngineToolPolicy.lean` states that the two produce the same lists.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.RunCompose.selected_skill_is_assigned
entries.docstring: Selected skills are exactly the requested names that remain assigned to the agent.

entries.statement: have all := { readFiles := true, writeFiles := true, runCommands := true, unrestrictedNetwork := true }; AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.agentDeny all ["WebFetch"] = ["WebFetch"]
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.RunCompose.stored_policy_denial_survives
entries.docstring: A stored tool denial survives union with checkbox-derived denials.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (pinned : Option String) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey) (batch : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.authorised tok k.workspace k.session = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.engineAccepts pinned k.engine = true → k.engine = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.claudeEngine → k.stream.startsWith (k.workspace ++ "/") = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveGuardedWrite tok pinned st k batch = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Outcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Refusal.projectKeyMismatch
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.a_claude_write_outside_its_project_key_is_refused
entries.docstring:
**A Claude write outside the caller's project key is refused `403 project_key_mismatch`**, and
nothing is stored: a runtime whose SDK silently fell back to a `cwd`-derived key is told so rather
than writing a stream the public read cannot find.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey) (batch : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry) (pinnedEngine : String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.authorised tok k.workspace k.session = true → (pinnedEngine == k.engine) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveWrite tok (some pinnedEngine) st k batch = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Outcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Refusal.engineMismatch
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.a_stream_of_another_engine_is_refused
entries.docstring: **A stream whose engine differs from the session's is refused**, with its own code.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey) (batch : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.authorised tok k.workspace k.session = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveWrite tok none st k batch = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Outcome.stored (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.append st k batch)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.an_unpinned_session_accepts_any_engine
entries.docstring:
**A session no run has pinned yet accepts any engine.**

Not a hole: `sessions.engine` is NULL until a run reports the session's identity, so refusing a NULL
would refuse the first write of every new session — which is the write that exists to make the
session resumable in the first place.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (pinned : Option String) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey) (batch : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry), (k.engine != AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.claudeEngine) = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveGuardedWrite tok pinned st k batch = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveWrite tok pinned st k batch
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.another_engines_stream_key_is_opaque
entries.docstring:
**Every other engine's stream key stays opaque**: the guarded write is exactly the unguarded
one.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (pinned : Option String) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.BlobKey) (size : Nat), (tok.session == k.session) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveBlob tok pinned st k size = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Outcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Refusal.notFound
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.another_sessions_blob_cannot_be_written
entries.docstring:
**…nor its blobs.** Quantified over the size, so the cap cannot leak the session's existence
either: an over-cap blob for a session the caller cannot reach is still a `404`.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (pinned : Option String) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey), (tok.session == k.session) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveRead tok pinned st k = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Outcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Refusal.notFound
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.another_sessions_stream_cannot_be_read
entries.docstring: **…nor read**, with the same answer, so the two cannot be told apart.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (pinned : Option String) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey) (batch : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry), (tok.session == k.session) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveWrite tok pinned st k batch = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Outcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Refusal.notFound
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.another_sessions_stream_cannot_be_written
entries.docstring:
**A token for another session cannot write.** Quantified over the store and the batch: what the
stream holds, and what the caller wanted to put in it, cannot change the answer.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (pinned : Option String) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey) (batch : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry), (tok.workspace == k.workspace) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveWrite tok pinned st k batch = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Outcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Refusal.notFound
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.another_workspaces_stream_is_refused
entries.docstring:
**Another workspace's stream is refused the same way**, even when the session id matches. Two
tenants can hold the same session id only by coincidence, and a check on one half is not a check.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.the_concealing_refusal_is_a_404
entries.docstring: The refusal a caller sees is a `404` carrying `session_state_not_found`, never a `403`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.the_engine_refusal_is_a_409
entries.docstring: The engine refusal is a `409` carrying `session_engine_mismatch`.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey) (batch : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry) (pinnedEngine : String), (tok.session == k.session) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveWrite tok (some pinnedEngine) st k batch = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Outcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Refusal.notFound
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.the_engine_refusal_never_leaks_a_hidden_session
entries.docstring:
**Authorisation is decided before the engine.**

The claim this makes precise: a caller that may not reach the session gets `notFound` whatever the
session is pinned to, so the `409` cannot be used to learn which engine a hidden session runs.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.the_project_key_refusal_is_a_403
entries.docstring:
The project-key refusal travels as `403 project_key_mismatch`, the code the legacy
`POST …/transcript` has always used for the same disagreement.

entries.statement: ∀ (tok : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.RunToken) (pinned : Option String) (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey) (batch : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry), (tok.session == k.session) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.serveGuardedWrite tok pinned st k batch = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Outcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Refusal.notFound
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Adversarial.SessionState.the_project_key_refusal_never_leaks_a_hidden_session
entries.docstring:
**The guard never answers for a hidden session**: a caller that may not reach the session gets
`notFound` whatever key it sent, so the `403` cannot be used to probe another session.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.a_row_serves_at_most_the_grammar_bound
entries.docstring:
**Every served id fits the documented grammar**: a row serves at most `maxFramesPerRow` frames,
so a sub-index never needs a fourth digit, whatever a tenant's agent put in one turn.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.never_drops_an_engine_message
entries.docstring:
**Every classified engine message maps to at least one neutral frame.**

There is no input for which `toAgentFrames` answers nothing: a message the neutral vocabulary cannot
express becomes `agent.native`, and one that could not be parsed becomes `agent.malformed`. This is
the guarantee the runner's writer relies on without re-checking, and the reason the closed frame set
is safe to close.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.no_tool_frames_from_another_role
entries.docstring: A turn that is neither the assistant's nor the user's carries no tool frame at all.

entries.statement: ∀ {α : Type} (cursorSequence i sequence : Nat) (subIndexed : Bool) (served : List α), ¬cursorSequence = sequence → AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.resumeWithinRow (some (cursorSequence, i)) sequence subIndexed served = served
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.resume_serves_a_different_row_whole
entries.docstring:
A cursor naming another row's sequence serves that row whole: a cursor into a row the store can
no longer retain has already produced a `stream-reset`, and the oldest retained row is then new to
the client in its entirety.

entries.statement: ∀ {α : Type} (sequence i : Nat) (served : List α), AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.resumeWithinRow (some (sequence, i)) sequence false served = served
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.resume_serves_a_one_to_one_row_whole
entries.docstring:
A sub-indexed cursor naming a row that was served **one-to-one** serves that row whole.

The server never writes such an id — only an upgraded legacy row is served in parts — so the cursor
is stale or forged; the row is delivered rather than dropped on the strength of a position it does
not have, the same "reported, not guessed" answer the rest of the read path gives.

entries.statement: ∀ {α : Type} (sequence i : Nat) (served : List α), List.take (i + 1) served ++ AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.resumeWithinRow (some (sequence, i)) sequence true served = served
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.resume_within_row_loses_and_repeats_nothing
entries.docstring:
**Resuming inside a row neither loses a frame nor repeats one.**

A client that last saw `<sequence>.<i>` is re-served that whole row — the store seeks by row and
cannot deliver half of one — and given only the frames after `i`. Concatenating what it already had
with what it is served back reconstructs the row exactly once.

entries.statement: ∀ {α : Type} (xs : List α), List.map Prod.fst (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.indexed xs) = List.range xs.length
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.row_positions_are_a_range
entries.docstring:
The positions a row's frames are served under are `0, 1, …`, so the ids inside one row are
strictly increasing by construction.

entries.statement: ∀ (systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes : List String) (sequence : Nat) (data : AgentWorkspace.JValue), List.map Prod.snd (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.serveLegacyRow systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes sequence data) = AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.capRowFrames (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.upgradeLegacy systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes data) ∧ List.map Prod.fst (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.serveLegacyRow systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes sequence data) = List.map (fun i => (sequence, some i)) (List.range (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.capRowFrames (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.upgradeLegacy systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes data)).length) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.idsIncreasing (List.map Prod.fst (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.serveLegacyRow systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes sequence data)) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.served_frames_keep_emission_order
entries.docstring:
**A row's frames are served in the order the mapping emitted them, under ascending ids.**

The served frames are exactly the frames `toAgentFrames` produced (capped at the grammar's bound),
in its order; the sub-indices are `0, 1, …` in that same order; and the ids are strictly increasing.
This is the general form of `engine_message_fans_out_in_order`.

entries.statement: ∀ (items : List AgentWorkspace.JValue), (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toolFrames "assistant" (some (AgentWorkspace.JValue.arr items))).all AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Frame.isToolCall = true ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toolFrames "user" (some (AgentWorkspace.JValue.arr items))).all AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Frame.isToolResult = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.tool_frames_follow_the_turn_that_can_carry_them
entries.docstring:
**A call frame can only come from an assistant turn, and a result frame only from a user turn.**

This is what makes the pairing invariant hold across a whole run without the mapping remembering
anything: the Claude Agent SDK carries a `tool_use` block on the assistant's message and the matching
`tool_result` on the *following* user message, so the frame announcing a `toolCallId` is always
emitted before the frame answering it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.unmapped_message_is_carried_natively
entries.docstring:
The fallback of an unmapped message names the engine's own message, so nothing is lost when the
neutral vocabulary has nothing to say about it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.wire_ids_follow_the_documented_grammar
entries.docstring: And the ids are rendered under the documented grammar.

entries.statement: ∀ (q : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Query) (f : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.RouteFacts), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideOrdinary q = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Decision.allow (some f) → ∃ role sub id op, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Roles.parseRoleInput q.role = some role ∧ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.parsePath q.path = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.ParsedPath.ok f.resource sub id ∧ f.operation = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.RouteOperation.ofOperation op ∧ f.grant = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.grantFor role f.resource op ∧ f.grant ≠ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grant.none ∧ (f.grant = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grant.own → q.ownership = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.own ∨ q.ownership = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.notApplicable) ∧ (f.grant = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grant.permitted → q.ownership = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.permitted)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AuthzDecide.every_allow_is_backed_by_the_table
entries.docstring:
Every `allow` that consulted §21's table is backed by it: the role parses, the path parses to
the allowed resource, the grant is that role's cell, it is not `none`, an `own` grant saw an `own`
or `not-applicable` fact, and a `permitted` grant saw a `permitted` fact.

entries.statement: ∀ (q : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Query) (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.Scope), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideOrdinary { role := q.role, method := q.method, path := q.path, ownership := q.ownership, scope := some s } = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideOrdinary { role := q.role, method := q.method, path := q.path, ownership := q.ownership, scope := none } ∨ ∃ d, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideOrdinary { role := q.role, method := q.method, path := q.path, ownership := q.ownership, scope := some s } = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Decision.deny none (some d)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AuthzDecide.scope_only_narrows
entries.docstring:
A browser-token scope only narrows: the scoped decision is the unscoped one, or a
`token_out_of_scope` deny — never an `allow` the minter would not get, and never a different
refusal.

entries.statement: ∀ (q : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Query) (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.BrowserToken.Scope) (f : Option AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.RouteFacts), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideOrdinary { role := q.role, method := q.method, path := q.path, ownership := q.ownership, scope := some s } = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Decision.allow f → AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideOrdinary { role := q.role, method := q.method, path := q.path, ownership := q.ownership, scope := none } = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Decision.allow f
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AuthzDecide.scoped_allow_implies_unscoped_allow
entries.docstring:
A scoped query is allowed only if the same query without the scope is allowed, with the same
route facts.

entries.statement: ∀ (q : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Query), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideOrdinary { role := q.role, method := q.method, path := q.path, ownership := AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.unknown, scope := q.scope } = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideOrdinary { role := q.role, method := q.method, path := q.path, ownership := AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.other, scope := q.scope }
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AuthzDecide.unknown_owner_is_decided_as_other
entries.docstring:
An undetermined owner (`unknown`) is decided exactly as another member's row (`other`): the
handler that has not read the row gains nothing by saying so.

entries.statement: ∀ (acceptWs : String → Bool) (ws : String) (op : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOp), ws.toList.contains '/' = false → ∀ {ks : List String}, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedObjectOp acceptWs ws op = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOutcome.backend ks → ∀ (k : String), k ∈ ks → ∃ R, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.splitSlash k.toList = "workspaces".toList :: ws.toList :: R
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.object_keys_carry_their_workspace
entries.docstring:
Every backend key or prefix a scoped object-store call reaches begins with the two segments
`workspaces` and the store's workspace id, whenever that id is a single segment (always, under the
target acceptance rule; for today's rule, whenever the id has no `/`).

entries.statement: ∀ (ws₁ ws₂ : String), ws₁ ≠ ws₂ → ∀ (op₁ op₂ : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOp) {ks₁ ks₂ : List String}, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedObjectOpTarget ws₁ op₁ = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOutcome.backend ks₁ → AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedObjectOpTarget ws₂ op₂ = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOutcome.backend ks₂ → ∀ {k₁ k₂ : String}, k₁ ∈ ks₁ → k₂ ∈ ks₂ → k₁ ≠ k₂ ∧ ¬AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.splitSlash k₁.toList <+: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.splitSlash k₂.toList
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.object_keys_of_two_workspaces_are_disjoint
entries.docstring:
Under the target acceptance rule, no key or listing prefix of one workspace's object store is
a key of another workspace's, nor a segment prefix of one: a key of workspace A is never a key of
workspace B, and listing A never lists B.

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State) (ws pid : String) (now : Nat) (rec : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.DirectoryRecord), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.principalById st ws pid now = some rec → rec.workspaceId = ws ∧ (rec.kind = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Kind.membership → ∃ m, m ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.memberships ∧ m.get "workspace_id" = some ws ∧ m.get "role" = some rec.role ∧ m.get "user_id" = rec.userId ∧ ∃ u, u ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.users ∧ u.get "id" = rec.userId ∧ u.get "name" = some rec.label) ∧ (rec.kind = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Kind.apiKey → ∃ k, k ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.apiKeys ∧ k.get "workspace_id" = some ws ∧ k.get "id" = rec.apiKeyId ∧ k.get "role" = some rec.role ∧ k.get "name" = some rec.label ∧ k.get "revoked_at" = none ∧ ((k.get "expires_at").isNone = true ∨ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.after (k.get "expires_at") now = true))
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.principal_by_id_reads_only_its_workspace
entries.docstring:
`principalById(ws, pid)` builds its record only from rows of workspace `ws`: a membership
principal's role comes from a membership of `ws` (and its label from that membership's user), an
API-key principal's role and label from a key of `ws` that is neither revoked nor expired at
`now`.

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State) (s : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.WorkspaceScope) (w : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.RepoWrite), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.isScopedTable w.table = true → ∀ (u : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName) {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.rowTenant u r ≠ some s.workspaceId → (r ∈ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.repoCommit st s w u ↔ r ∈ st u)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.repository_write_touches_only_its_workspace
entries.docstring:
A repository write bound to scope `s` on a tenant-scoped table, once PostgreSQL commits or
rolls it back, leaves every row that is not of `s`'s workspace — every other tenant's rows and
every global row — exactly as it was: no scoped operation reaches another workspace.

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State) (s : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.WorkspaceScope) (t : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName) (p : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row → Bool) {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r ∈ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedSelect st s t p → AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.rowTenant t r = some s.workspaceId
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.scoped_select_reads_only_its_workspace
entries.docstring: A scoped read returns only rows whose workspace is the scope's.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AzureGateway.dynamic_sessions_reach_configured_gateway
entries.docstring: Enabling Dynamic Sessions makes the configured gateway reachable from their sandboxes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AzureGateway.external_ingress_still_requires_run_token
entries.docstring: Public ingress never grants an unauthenticated caller access to a model route.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AzureGateway.internal_ingress_blocks_dynamic_session
entries.docstring: Internal ingress cannot carry a model request from a Dynamic Session, even with a valid token.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.AzureGateway.no_dynamic_sessions_keep_gateway_internal
entries.docstring: Disabling Dynamic Sessions leaves the gateway internal and reachable to environment apps.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.a_run_never_claims_an_engine_session_id
entries.docstring:
A run never writes an engine session id either: the identity is recorded only after the runner
reports one, by {@link recordIdentity}.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.a_run_never_repins_the_session
entries.docstring:
No run ever re-pins its session, whatever it asks for. Switching a live session to another engine
is a non-goal of the engine programme: the session's history belongs to the engine that produced it,
so a run that cannot join it is refused rather than allowed to take it over.

entries.statement: ∀ (agentEngine : String) (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchState), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.launchPaired s = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.launchPaired (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine s).snd = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.a_run_preserves_the_pairing
entries.docstring: A fresh session satisfies the pairing, and a run does not break it: a run writes neither cell.

entries.statement: ∀ (engine : String) (engineSessionId : Option String) (runs : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.RunRow), engine ∈ AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.engineIds → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun engine { sessionEngine := some engine, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs } = (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.created engine, { sessionEngine := some engine, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs ++ [{ engine := engine }] })
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.a_run_records_the_engine_the_session_is_pinned_to
entries.docstring:
A run in a session pinned to a **published** engine records that engine, and appends exactly
one row.

The hypothesis is the code's, not a convenience: `pinSessionEngine` narrows the engine it records
with `publishedEngineId`, which throws — and so writes no row — for an id outside `ENGINE_IDS`
(`apps/web/server/runs/api.test.ts`, "refuses to record a run for an engine the contracts do not
publish"). `startRun` below models the published case only.

entries.statement: ∀ (agentEngine : String) (engineSessionId : Option String) (runs : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.RunRow), agentEngine ∈ AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.engineIds → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine { sessionEngine := none, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs } = (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.created agentEngine, { sessionEngine := none, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs ++ [{ engine := agentEngine }] })
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.an_unpinned_session_accepts_any_engine
entries.docstring:
A session no run has pinned accepts any **published** engine, and records the agent's own. This
is what makes `sessions.engine` NULL a real state rather than a missing value: a project session
created before its first run is launched, not refused.

"Any" is every id the contracts publish, not every string: `pinSessionEngine` narrows the agent's
engine with `publishedEngineId` before it can be recorded, and that throws, writing no row, for an
id outside `ENGINE_IDS`. The refusal theorems above need no such hypothesis, because a refusal and a
throw both leave the rows as they were.

entries.statement: ∀ (engine reported : String) (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchState), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.launchPaired (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.recordIdentity engine reported s) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.recording_identity_establishes_the_pairing
entries.docstring:
Recording a reported identity pins the engine and the id together, so the pairing invariant holds
of the state it produces from **any** prior state. Migration 0025 closes the same gap for rows
written before this code.

entries.statement: ∀ (agentEngine : String) (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchState), (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine s).fst = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.engineMismatch → (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine s).snd = s
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.session_engine_mismatch_creates_no_run
entries.docstring:
A run whose agent's engine differs from `sessions.engine` is refused, and the state is
**unchanged**: no run row is created, not created-and-rolled-back.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.session_engine_mismatch_is_a_four_oh_nine
entries.docstring:
The refusal travels as `409 session_engine_mismatch`, apart from `session_not_usable`: the
request is well formed, and the session has a history this run does not belong to.

entries.statement: ∀ (agentEngine pinned : String) (engineSessionId : Option String) (runs : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.RunRow), (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine { sessionEngine := some pinned, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs }).fst = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.engineMismatch ↔ pinned ≠ agentEngine
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.session_engine_mismatch_is_exactly_a_different_pin
entries.docstring:
The refusal happens **exactly** when the session is pinned to another engine: a session pinned to
the agent's own engine is never refused, and one pinned to any other engine always is.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.State) (tx : List AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Stmt), AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.consistent s.er = true → AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.consistent (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.commit AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.consistent s.er tx) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourRuns.committed_run_write_preserves_er
entries.docstring:
Current-schema transactions either pass every constraint or leave a consistent pre-state
unchanged. The repository applies this check at write/commit, not after a read or stream.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.State), s.er AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.runs = s.erBase AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.runs ++ List.map AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.RunRow.toErRow s.runs
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourRuns.er_run_projection
entries.docstring:
The modeled run projection is exactly the current ER run table joined to its surrounding
rows. It cannot drift into an unrelated, independently carried run list.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.State) (p : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.Principal) (r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.Request), (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.step s p r).state.foreignRuns p.workspaceId = s.foreignRuns p.workspaceId
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourRuns.every_route_preserves_foreign
entries.docstring:
Each of the seven route branches either leaves the run projection alone, creates a run in
the caller's workspace, or interrupts a row established by the workspace-filtered lookup.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.State) (p : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.Principal) (row : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.RunRow), row.workspaceId = p.workspaceId → (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.interruptState s p row).foreignRuns p.workspaceId = s.foreignRuns p.workspaceId
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourRuns.interrupt_preserves_foreign
entries.docstring: Interrupt changes only a run in the caller's workspace, including when abstract rows reuse an id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourRuns.response_excludes_credential_keys
entries.docstring: The HTTP envelope does not contain gateway or browser credential keys.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.State) (p : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.Principal) (r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.Request), (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.startState s p r).foreignRuns p.workspaceId = s.foreignRuns p.workspaceId
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourRuns.start_preserves_foreign
entries.docstring: A created run names the authenticated workspace, leaving every foreign projected row alone.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.State) (p : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.Principal) (r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.Request), Option.map (fun row => (row.ownerId, row.sessionId)) (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Runs.startState s p r).runs.head? = some (p.id, r.newSessionId)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourRuns.start_records_owner_and_session
entries.docstring:
The inserted row is attributed to the authenticated principal and to the session returned
by the session-resolution seam, not to an arbitrary owner or the raw agent id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.CliRuns.conflicting_start_flags_make_no_sdk_calls
entries.docstring: Conflicting start flags stop command routing before any SDK request.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.CliRuns.courtesy_interrupt_preserves_exit
entries.docstring: The courtesy interrupt's own outcome cannot replace the original interrupt exit.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.exitCode false (some (AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.fromSdkFailure (AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Runs.Failure.transport false))) = 4 ∧ AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.exitCode false (some (AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.fromSdkFailure (AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Runs.Failure.apiProblem 409 "conflict"))) = 1 ∧ AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.exitCode false (some (AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.fromSdkFailure AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Runs.Failure.contractViolation)) = 3
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.CliRuns.sdk_failure_maps_to_exit
entries.docstring: SDK transport, API and contract failures retain their three distinct CLI exit classes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.CliRuns.sigint_exit_priority
entries.docstring: SIGINT wins over every error classification, including a failed courtesy interrupt.

entries.statement: ∀ (first second : AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.Command) (failure : AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.Failure), AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.commandExit first false (some failure) = AgentWorkspace.Cli.Runs.commandExit second false (some failure)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.CliRuns.typed_failure_exit_is_command_independent
entries.docstring: Each typed SDK error class determines one CLI exit code regardless of command.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.RawField) (m : Option String), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.parseModel r = Except.ok m → m = none ∨ ∃ t, m = some t ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.notBlank t = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.utf16Length t ≤ 200
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.accepted_agent_model_is_default_or_visible
entries.docstring:
Every model id `parseAgentModel` accepts is `null` (the workspace default) or a trimmed,
non-blank string within `AGENT_MODEL_MAX_LENGTH`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.accepted_agent_name_passes_the_table_check
entries.docstring:
Every name `parseAgentName` accepts passes the `agents_name_not_blank` check and the HTTP
bound, so an agent row carrying it is valid: the route's parser is at least as strict as the
table.

entries.statement: ∀ (b : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.RawAssignments) (a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.assignmentsBody b = some a → b.extra = [] ∧ (∀ (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.RawFileEntry), e ∈ b.files → e.fileId ≠ "" ∧ (e.access = "read" ∨ e.access = "read-write")) ∧ (∀ (k : String), k ∈ b.skillIds → k ≠ "") ∧ (∀ (c : String), c ∈ b.connectorIds → c ≠ "") ∧ List.map (fun x => x.file) a.files = List.map (fun x => x.fileId) b.files ∧ a.skills = b.skillIds ∧ a.connectors = b.connectorIds
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.accepted_assignment_body_keeps_every_id
entries.docstring:
A body `AgentResourceAssignmentsSchema` accepts has no unknown key, a non-empty id and a
closed-set access on every file entry, and non-empty skill and connector ids, and the parsed
assignment keeps every id in order, repeats included (the schema does not refuse duplicates;
`replace` does, for files).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.accepted_instructions_are_the_string_sent
entries.docstring:
Every instruction block `parseAgentInstructions` accepts is the string sent, unchanged, and
within `AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS_MAX_LENGTH`.

entries.statement: ∀ (b : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Body) (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Parsed), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.parseBody (some b) = Except.ok p → ∀ (id : AgentWorkspace.ConnectorId) (ws : AgentWorkspace.WorkspaceId) (sid : AgentWorkspace.SecretId) (createdBy : Option AgentWorkspace.UserId) (owner : AgentWorkspace.PrincipalId), (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).stdioHasCommand = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).remoteHasUrl = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).argsStdioOnly = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).commandNotBlank = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).urlShapeOk = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).credentialRequired = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.created_connector_meets_the_shape_checks
entries.docstring:
"Validating here means the database's constraints are a backstop": every body
`parseCreateConnectorBody` accepts yields a row that passes the six shape checks of `mcp_servers`
(command xor URL by transport, arguments only for `stdio`, a non-blank command, an absolute
`http(s)` URL, and a credential secret exactly when the authentication type needs one).

Deleting one file (`deleteFile`) removes exactly the row at that path; unlike a subtree
delete, the rows under a folder's path stay.

entries.statement: ∀ (ps : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.PrincipalView) (users : List AgentWorkspace.UserId) (x : AgentWorkspace.PrincipalId), x ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.grantsRead ps users → ∃ p, p ∈ ps ∧ p.id = x ∧ p.user.isSome = true ∧ p.revoked = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.grants_read_names_only_active_members
entries.docstring:
Reading grants names only active membership principals of the workspace: never an API-key
principal and never a revoked one.

entries.statement: ∀ (ps : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.PrincipalView) (req : List AgentWorkspace.PrincipalId) (users : List AgentWorkspace.UserId), (∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.PrincipalView), p ∈ ps → ∀ (q : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.PrincipalView), q ∈ ps → p.user.isSome = true → p.user = q.user → p = q) → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.grantsReplace true ps req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.GrantsOutcome.updated users → ∀ (x : AgentWorkspace.PrincipalId), x ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.grantsRead ps users ↔ x ∈ req
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.grants_round_trip
entries.docstring:
The grants round trip: when every user is behind at most one principal of the workspace (one
membership per user and one principal per membership), reading the grants back after replacing
them with a set of principal ids yields exactly that set, although the table stores users.
