entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.consistent st = true → ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers → ∃ r', r' ∈ st (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").refTable ∧ r'.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").refColumns = r.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").columns ∧ ∀ (r'' : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row), r'' ∈ st (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").refTable → r''.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").refColumns = r.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").columns → r'' = r'
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk_names_exactly_one_parent
entries.docstring: In every consistent state, every `project_mcp_servers` row names exactly one `workspaces` row through `project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk` (its columns are `NOT NULL`).

entries.statement: ∀ (ws : AgentWorkspace.WorkspaceId) (fresh : AgentWorkspace.FileId) (input : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.PutFile) (fs : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), (∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), f ∈ fs → f.path ≠ input.path) → ∃ f', f' ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.putFile ws fresh input fs ∧ f'.id = fresh ∧ f'.owner = input.owner ∧ f'.workspace = ws ∧ f'.path = input.path
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.put_file_at_a_new_path_is_owned_by_the_caller
entries.docstring: A file upload at a new path creates a row owned by the uploading principal.

entries.statement: ∀ (ws : AgentWorkspace.WorkspaceId) (fresh : AgentWorkspace.FileId) (input : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.PutFile) (fs : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File) (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), f ∈ fs → f.path = input.path → ∃ f', f' ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.putFile ws fresh input fs ∧ f'.id = f.id ∧ f'.owner = f.owner ∧ f'.createdBy = f.createdBy ∧ f'.path = input.path ∧ f'.storageKey = input.storageKey
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.put_file_never_transfers_owner
entries.docstring:
A file upload at a path that already exists updates the row's content and never its id,
owner or creator: "an upsert at an existing path never transfers it".

entries.statement: ∀ (ws : AgentWorkspace.WorkspaceId) (fresh : AgentWorkspace.SkillId) (input : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Skill.PutSkill) (ss : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Skill.Skill) (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Skill.Skill), s ∈ ss → s.name = input.name → ∃ s', s' ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Skill.putSkill ws fresh input ss ∧ s'.id = s.id ∧ s'.owner = s.owner ∧ s'.createdBy = s.createdBy ∧ s'.skillMd = input.skillMd
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.put_skill_never_transfers_owner
entries.docstring:
A skill import under a name that already exists updates `SKILL.md` and `enabled` and never
the row's id, owner or creator.

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (stored : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments), p.writeFiles = false → ∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileEntry), f ∈ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.effective p stored).files → f.access = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileAccess.read
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.read_narrows_stale_write_access
entries.docstring:
Whatever access a stored `agent_files` row carries, reading an agent's assignments without
its `writeFiles` permission yields only `read` access (a stale `read-write` row is narrowed on
read).

entries.statement: ∀ (S : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Schema) (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.consistent S st = true → ∀ {t : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName} {fk : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.ForeignKey}, fk ∈ (S t).foreignKeys → AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.targetIsExactKey S fk = true → ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r ∈ st t → r.present fk.columns = true → ∃ r', r' ∈ st fk.refTable ∧ r'.project fk.refColumns = r.project fk.columns ∧ ∀ (r'' : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row), r'' ∈ st fk.refTable → r''.project fk.refColumns = r.project fk.columns → r'' = r'
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.reference_names_one_parent
entries.docstring:
In a consistent state, a row whose foreign key is set names exactly one parent row, provided
the key targets an exact key of the parent.

entries.statement: ∀ (old new : String) (fs : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), List.map (fun f => (f.id, f.workspace, f.owner, f.createdBy)) (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameByPrefix old new fs) = List.map (fun f => (f.id, f.workspace, f.owner, f.createdBy)) fs
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.rename_by_prefix_keeps_every_identity
entries.docstring:
A subtree move rewrites paths by `UPDATE`, so every row keeps its id, workspace, owner and
creator, and with them every assignment and project link that names it.

entries.statement: ∀ (old new : String) (fs : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), (∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), f ∈ fs → f.storageKey = if f.kind = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.FileKind.file then some f.path else none) → ∀ (g : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), g ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameByPrefix old new fs → g.storageKey = if g.kind = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.FileKind.file then some g.path else none
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.rename_by_prefix_keeps_the_key_at_the_path
entries.docstring:
A subtree move keeps each file's object key at its path: a row whose key is its own path (as
every upload writes it) or which is a folder with no key still has that shape after the move.

entries.statement: ∀ (old new : String) (fs : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File) (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), f ∈ fs → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.underPrefix old f.path = false → f ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameByPrefix old new fs
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.rename_by_prefix_leaves_other_rows_alone
entries.docstring: A subtree move leaves every row outside the prefix exactly as it was.

entries.statement: ∀ (old new : String) (fs : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File) (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), f ∈ fs → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.underPrefix old f.path = true → ∃ g, g ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameByPrefix old new fs ∧ g.id = f.id ∧ g.path = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renamePath old new f.path
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.rename_by_prefix_moves_the_rows_under_it
entries.docstring:
A subtree move renames every row under the prefix: its new path is the new prefix followed by
what followed the old one.

entries.statement: ∀ (path : String) (input : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.RenameFile) (fs : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameFile path input fs = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.RenameOutcome.missing ↔ ∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), f ∈ fs → f.path ≠ path
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.rename_file_is_missing_iff_no_row
entries.docstring: A single-file rename answers `null` exactly when no row of the workspace is at the old path.

entries.statement: ∀ (path : String) (input : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.RenameFile) (fs fs' : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File) (row : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameFile path input fs = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.RenameOutcome.renamed fs' row → ∃ f, f ∈ fs ∧ f.path = path ∧ row.id = f.id ∧ row.workspace = f.workspace ∧ row.owner = f.owner ∧ row.createdBy = f.createdBy ∧ row.path = input.path ∧ row ∈ fs'
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.rename_file_keeps_the_rows_identity
entries.docstring:
A single-file rename (`renameFile`) is an `UPDATE` of the row at the old path: the returned
row keeps that row's id, workspace, owner and creator, carries the new path, and is in the new
catalog ("a rename changes the row's path and content metadata, never who owns or originally
created it").

entries.statement: ∀ (path : String) (input : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.RenameFile) (fs fs' : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File) (row g : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameFile path input fs = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.RenameOutcome.renamed fs' row → g ∈ fs → g.path ≠ path → g ∈ fs'
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.rename_file_leaves_other_rows_alone
entries.docstring: A single-file rename leaves every row at another path exactly as it was.

entries.statement: ∀ (path : String) (input : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.RenameFile) (fs fs' : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File) (row : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.renameFile path input fs = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.RenameOutcome.renamed fs' row → input.path = path ∨ ∀ (g : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), g ∈ fs → g.path ≠ input.path
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.rename_file_never_takes_an_occupied_path
entries.docstring:
A single-file rename never lands on a path another row holds: a successful rename either
keeps the path or moves the row to a path no row had (PostgreSQL raises the
`files_workspace_path_key` violation otherwise).

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (cat : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.CatalogIds) (req a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.updated a → List.Pairwise (fun f g => f.file ≤ g.file) a.files ∧ List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 => x1 ≤ x2) a.skills ∧ List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 => x1 ≤ x2) a.connectors
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.replace_answers_in_id_order
entries.docstring:
The answer of a successful replacement lists files, skills and connectors each in ascending
id order, as `read(agentId)` returns them (`orderBy(asc(...))`), not in request order.

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (cat : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.CatalogIds) (req a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.updated a → (∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileEntry), f ∈ a.files → f.file ∈ cat.files) ∧ (∀ (k : String), k ∈ a.skills → k ∈ cat.skills) ∧ ∀ (c : String), c ∈ a.connectors → c ∈ cat.connectors
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.replace_assigns_only_catalogued_resources
entries.docstring:
Replacing an agent's assignments writes only ids that name a file, skill or connector of the
agent's own workspace catalog: "importing a skill puts it in the workspace's catalog; assigning it
is what makes one particular agent's runs able to load it".

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (cat : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.CatalogIds) (req : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments) (id : String), (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.unknownSkill id → (List.map (fun x => x.file) req.files).Nodup ∧ (∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileEntry), f ∈ req.files → f.file ∈ cat.files) ∧ id ∈ req.skills ∧ ¬id ∈ cat.skills) ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.unknownConnector id → (List.map (fun x => x.file) req.files).Nodup ∧ (∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileEntry), f ∈ req.files → f.file ∈ cat.files) ∧ (∀ (k : String), k ∈ req.skills → k ∈ cat.skills) ∧ id ∈ req.connectors ∧ ¬id ∈ cat.connectors)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.replace_checks_files_then_skills_then_connectors
entries.docstring:
The check order, read back from the answer: an `unknown-skill` answer means every file id was
distinct and catalogued, and an `unknown-connector` answer means that and every skill id was
catalogued; the id named is a requested id outside the catalog.

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (cat : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.CatalogIds) (req a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.updated a → (∀ (k : String), k ∈ a.skills ↔ k ∈ req.skills) ∧ (∀ (c : String), c ∈ a.connectors ↔ c ∈ req.connectors) ∧ (List.map (fun x => x.file) a.files).Perm (List.map (fun x => x.file) req.files)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.replace_keeps_every_requested_id
entries.docstring:
The answer of a successful replacement holds every requested file, skill and connector id and
no other, whatever order the request used (the answer is the read-back, in id order).

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (cat : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.CatalogIds) (req a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.updated a → ∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileEntry), f ∈ a.files → ∃ g, g ∈ req.files ∧ g.file = f.file ∧ f.access.le g.access = true ∧ (p.writeFiles = false → f.access = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileAccess.read)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.replace_never_widens_past_write_files
entries.docstring:
An agent's written file assignments never exceed what was requested, and without the agent's
own `writeFiles` permission every one of them is `read` ("narrow, never widen").

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (cat : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.CatalogIds) (req : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments) (pre post : List String) (id : String), (List.map (fun x => x.file) req.files).Nodup → (∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileEntry), f ∈ req.files → f.file ∈ cat.files) → (∀ (k : String), k ∈ req.skills → k ∈ cat.skills) → req.connectors = pre ++ id :: post → (∀ (x : String), x ∈ pre → x ∈ cat.connectors) → ¬id ∈ cat.connectors → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.unknownConnector id
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.replace_reports_the_first_uncatalogued_connector
entries.docstring:
Replacement checks the connector ids last: when every file id is distinct and catalogued,
every skill id is catalogued, and `id` is the first requested connector id that names no
connector of the workspace, the answer is `unknown-connector` naming `id`.

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (cat : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.CatalogIds) (req : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments) (pre post : List String) (id : String), List.map (fun x => x.file) req.files = pre ++ id :: post → (List.map (fun x => x.file) req.files).Nodup → (∀ (x : String), x ∈ pre → x ∈ cat.files) → ¬id ∈ cat.files → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.unknownFile id
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.replace_reports_the_first_uncatalogued_file
entries.docstring:
Replacement checks the file ids first: when the file ids are distinct and `id` is the first
requested file id that names no file of the workspace, the answer is `unknown-file` naming `id`,
whatever the skills and connectors are.

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (cat : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.CatalogIds) (req : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments) (pre post : List String) (id : String), (List.map (fun x => x.file) req.files).Nodup → (∀ (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.FileEntry), f ∈ req.files → f.file ∈ cat.files) → req.skills = pre ++ id :: post → (∀ (x : String), x ∈ pre → x ∈ cat.skills) → ¬id ∈ cat.skills → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.unknownSkill id
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.replace_reports_the_first_uncatalogued_skill
entries.docstring:
Replacement checks the skill ids second: when every file id is distinct and catalogued and
`id` is the first requested skill id that names no skill of the workspace, the answer is
`unknown-skill` naming `id`, whatever the connectors are.

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Agent.Permissions) (cat : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.CatalogIds) (req a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.Assignments), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.replace (some p) cat req = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Grant.ReplaceOutcome.updated a → (List.map (fun x => x.file) a.files).Nodup ∧ a.skills.Nodup ∧ a.connectors.Nodup
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.replace_writes_each_resource_once
entries.docstring:
Replacing assignments writes each file, skill and connector at most once, as the three
natural keys require: a repeated file id is refused and repeated skill and connector ids are
merged.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.skills_created_by_workspace_fk_joins_one_workspace
entries.docstring: In every consistent state, a `skills` row and the `memberships` row it references through `skills_created_by_workspace_fk` belong to the same workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.skills_created_by_workspace_fk_names_one_parent_when_set
entries.docstring: In every consistent state, a `skills` row whose nullable key `skills_created_by_workspace_fk` is set names exactly one `memberships` row (a `NULL` key names none).

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.consistent st = true → ∀ {r1 r2 : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r1 ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills → r2 ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills → r1.present ["id", "workspace_id"] = true → r1.project ["id", "workspace_id"] = r2.project ["id", "workspace_id"] → r1 = r2
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.skills_id_workspace_key_identifies_one_row
entries.docstring: In every consistent state, two `skills` rows that agree on `(id, workspace_id)` are the same row: PostgreSQL enforces the key, which composite tenant-paired references target.

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.consistent st = true → ∀ {r r' : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.References AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills "skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk") r r' → AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.tenantOf AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills r = AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.tenantOf AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills "skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk").refTable r'
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk_joins_one_workspace
entries.docstring: In every consistent state, a `skills` row and the `workspace_principals` row it references through `skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk` belong to the same workspace.

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.consistent st = true → ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills → ∃ r', r' ∈ st (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills "skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk").refTable ∧ r'.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills "skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk").refColumns = r.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills "skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk").columns ∧ ∀ (r'' : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row), r'' ∈ st (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills "skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk").refTable → r''.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills "skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk").refColumns = r.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.skills "skills_owner_principal_workspace_fk").columns → r'' = r'

shape and an envelope whose parts all have their exact sizes and a non-empty ciphertext.

entries.docstring:
Admission of an API key, once lost, is lost for good: for fixed key and principal rows, a key
not admitted at an instant is not admitted at any later instant.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptIdentity.api_key_liveness_is_lost_for_good
entries.docstring:
A key that is not live at an instant is not live at any later instant: revocation and expiry
are both permanent for a fixed row.

different total lengths (74 and 75 characters), so `apps/web/proxy.ts` can tell them apart by

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptIdentity.owner_differs_from_the_actor_only_for_an_api_key
entries.docstring:

that differs from the acting principal belongs to an API-key principal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.charge_and_share_share_a_workspace

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.charge_db_valid_iff_row_check
entries.docstring:
The database check of `share_run_charges` holds on a charge's row exactly when the typed
charge is `dbValid`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.charge_funds_runs_of_its_share's_workspace
entries.docstring:
A share's budget only ever funds runs of the share's own workspace: the run and the share a
charge joins are in one workspace.

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.consistent AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue st = true → ∀ {c : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, c ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.shareRunCharges → ∃ u, u ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.runs ∧ u.get "id" = c.get "run_id" ∧ u.get "workspace_id" = c.get "workspace_id" ∧ ∀ (u' : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row), u' ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.runs → u'.get "id" = c.get "run_id" → u' = u
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.charge_has_exactly_one_run
entries.docstring: In a consistent state every run charge funds exactly one run, of its own workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.charge_has_exactly_one_share
entries.docstring: In a consistent state every run charge draws on exactly one share, of its own workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.charge_is_non_negative
entries.docstring: In a consistent state every run charge is a non-negative amount.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share) (now : Nat), s.publiclyOpen now = false → ∀ (a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PassphraseAttempt), s.resolveAt now a = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ResolveOutcome.unavailable
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.closed_link_is_unavailable_whatever_the_passphrase
entries.docstring:
A closed link answers `share_unavailable` whatever passphrase is presented, so a visitor of a
closed link learns nothing about whether it has a passphrase.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share) {t1 t2 : Nat}, t1 ≤ t2 → s.publiclyOpen t1 = false → s.publiclyOpen t2 = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.closed_link_stays_closed
entries.docstring:
A public link that does not open at an instant does not open at any later instant: every
cause (visibility, revocation, suspension, the stop, expiry) persists as time passes.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share) {t1 t2 : Nat}, t1 ≤ t2 → s.stateAt t1 = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ShareState.expired → s.stateAt t2 = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ShareState.expired
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.expired_state_is_permanent
entries.docstring:
A share's derived state never returns to `live` once it has expired: expiry is permanent as
time passes.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRequest) (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (re : Bool) (now : Nat) (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Published), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role false re now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.published p → r.visibility ≠ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Visibility.public
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.no_public_share_is_published_while_sharing_is_off
entries.docstring: While public sharing is off, no admitted publish is a public share.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRequest) (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (pse : Bool) (now : Nat) (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Published), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role pse AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.runnableReleased now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.published p → p.mode ≠ some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode.runnable ∧ p.budgetCapUsd = none
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.no_runnable_share_is_published_today
entries.docstring: While the release gate is closed (today), no admitted publish writes a runnable share.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRequest) (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (pse re : Bool) (now : Nat) (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Published), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role pse re now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.published p → p.expiresAt = Option.map (fun x => now + x) (r.expiry.getD AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Expiry.never).durationMs?
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.published_expiry_counts_from_now
entries.docstring:
An admitted publish expires exactly its expiry's lifetime after `now`, and never with
`never` or no expiry.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRequest) (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (pse re : Bool) (now : Nat) (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Published), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role pse re now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.published p → p.mode.isSome = (r.subjectType == AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.agent) ∧ p.budgetCapUsd.isSome = (p.mode == some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode.runnable)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.published_mode_and_budget_fit
entries.docstring:
An admitted publish gives a mode exactly to an agent share, and a budget exactly to a
runnable one: the two row-local halves of `wellPublished` hold for everything the service writes.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share) (now : Nat) (a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PassphraseAttempt), s.resolveAt now a = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ResolveOutcome.opened ↔ s.publiclyOpen now = true ∧ (s.passphraseRequired = false ∨ a = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PassphraseAttempt.right)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.resolve_opens_iff
entries.docstring:
A link opens exactly when it is public and live and, if it has a passphrase, the right one is
presented.

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.consistent AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue st = true → ∀ {c1 c2 : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, c1 ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.shareRunCharges → c2 ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.shareRunCharges → c1.get "run_id" = c2.get "run_id" → c1 = c2 ∧ c1.get "share_id" = c2.get "share_id"
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.run_is_funded_by_at_most_one_share
entries.docstring:
In a consistent state a run is funded by at most one share: two charge rows for the same run
are the same row (`run_id` is the primary key).

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.consistent st = true → ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.shares → Option.all AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.nonNegativeAmount (r.get "spent_usd") = true ∧ Option.all AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.nonNegativeAmount (r.get "budget_cap_usd") = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptPublication.share_amounts_are_non_negative
entries.docstring:
In a consistent state every share's spend is a non-negative amount, and its budget cap is
absent or a non-negative amount.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.appendEvent
entries.docstring:
The repository's `append` on the stored events of one table: insert the next event, then,
when `cutoff = next - maxEvents` is positive, delete the run's events at or below it.

entries.statement: ∀ (events : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.RunEvent) (run : AgentWorkspace.RunId) (ws : AgentWorkspace.WorkspaceId) (type data : String) (now maxEvents : Nat), (0 < AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.nextSequence events run - maxEvents → ∀ (s : Nat), s ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.sequencesOf (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.appendEvent events run ws type data now maxEvents) run → AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.nextSequence events run - maxEvents < s) ∧ (0 < maxEvents → AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.nextSequence events run ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.sequencesOf (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.appendEvent events run ws type data now maxEvents) run)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.append_prunes_at_the_cutoff_and_keeps_the_newest
entries.docstring:
The repository's `append` prunes exactly at the cutoff: once `cutoff = next - maxEvents` is
positive, every event the run keeps has a sequence above it; and with room for at least one
event, the event just appended is always kept. Together with contiguity this bounds a run's
stored log to its newest `maxEvents` events.

entries.statement: ∀ (events : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.RunEvent) (run run' : AgentWorkspace.RunId) (ws : AgentWorkspace.WorkspaceId) (type data : String) (now maxEvents : Nat), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.logContiguous events run' = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.logContiguous (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.appendEvent events run ws type data now maxEvents) run' = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.appending_an_event_keeps_every_log_contiguous
entries.docstring:
The repository's `append` keeps every run's stored event log contiguous: allocating
`max(sequence) + 1` extends the appending run's window by one, pruning its events at or below
`next - maxEvents` cuts the window from below and leaves it a window, and no other run's
events change ("assigning one contiguous sequence per run").

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.set_reference_has_a_target
entries.docstring:
In every consistent state, a row whose foreign-key columns are all set references a parent
row through that key (PostgreSQL's `MATCH SIMPLE`).

entries.statement: ∀ (steps : List (AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.RunOp × Nat)) (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run), r.wellFormed = true → AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.clockFrom r.lastStamp (List.map (fun x => x.snd) steps) = true → ∀ {s e d : Nat}, (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.timedSteps r steps).startedAt = some s → (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.timedSteps r steps).endedAt = some e → (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.timedSteps r steps).durationMs = some d → s ≤ e ∧ ↑d = ↑e - ↑s
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.store_durations_are_exact
entries.docstring:
The model's durations are exact: every run the store operations produce from a well-formed
run (with a clock that never runs backwards) ends no earlier than it starts, so the natural-number
`durationMs` is the integer difference `endedAt - startedAt` that `renderRun` computes, never a
truncated negative one.

entries.statement: ∀ (steps : List (AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.RunOp × Nat)) (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run), r.wellFormed = true → AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.clockFrom r.lastStamp (List.map (fun x => x.snd) steps) = true → (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.timedSteps r steps).wellFormed = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.store_operations_preserve_run_checks
entries.docstring:
Every run check is preserved by every sequence of store operations whose clock never runs
behind the run's own timestamps: `markRunning` and `finish` never produce a row that
`runs_ended_at_iff_terminal` or `runs_ended_after_started` refuses, and leave the accounting
checks untouched.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run) (target : AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunStatus) (now : Nat), (r.status = AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunStatus.queued → AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.timedStep r AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.RunOp.markRunning now = { id := r.id, workspace := r.workspace, session := r.session, status := AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunStatus.running, model := r.model, provider := r.provider, modelConnection := r.modelConnection, startedAt := some now, endedAt := r.endedAt, counters := r.counters, costUsd := r.costUsd, costCurrency := r.costCurrency, priceTableVersion := r.priceTableVersion, error := r.error, accountingState := r.accountingState, accountingError := r.accountingError, createdAt := r.createdAt, updatedAt := r.updatedAt }) ∧ (r.status ≠ AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunStatus.queued → AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.timedStep r AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.RunOp.markRunning now = r) ∧ (r.status.isTerminal = false → target.isTerminal = true → AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.timedStep r (AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.RunOp.finish target) now = { id := r.id, workspace := r.workspace, session := r.session, status := target, model := r.model, provider := r.provider, modelConnection := r.modelConnection, startedAt := some (r.startedAt.getD now), endedAt := some now, counters := r.counters, costUsd := r.costUsd, costCurrency := r.costCurrency, priceTableVersion := r.priceTableVersion, error := r.error, accountingState := r.accountingState, accountingError := r.accountingError, createdAt := r.createdAt, updatedAt := r.updatedAt }) ∧ (r.status.isTerminal = true ∨ target.isTerminal = false → AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.timedStep r (AgentWorkspace.Lifecycle.RunOp.finish target) now = r)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.store_stamps_follow_the_status
entries.docstring:
What each store operation writes, status by status: `markRunning` on a queued run moves it to
`running` and stamps `startedAt` with the store's clock (and nothing else); `finish` with a
terminal target on a live run moves it there, stamps `endedAt`, and stamps `startedAt` only if
the run never had one; every other call writes nothing, because the store refuses it (`markRunning`
on a non-queued run answers `false`, `finish` with a non-terminal target rejects or throws) or
ignores it (`finish` on an already terminal run).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.timedStep
entries.docstring:
One store operation at instant `now`: the status machine decides whether the run moves
(`Lifecycle.runStep`), and a move writes the timestamps `Run.stamp` gives.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.uniqueness_keys_refuse_a_second_row
entries.docstring:
The uniqueness keys exclude a second, distinct row: adding to the witness state another event
at a stored `(run, sequence)`, another ledger row for a recorded provider response, another
session of the workspace with a recorded SDK session id, or another token with a stored digest
leaves a state PostgreSQL cannot hold.

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.consistent AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue st = true → ∀ {u1 u2 : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, u1 ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.runUsageRecords → u2 ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.runUsageRecords → u1.get "run_id" = u2.get "run_id" → u1.get "provider_response_id" = u2.get "provider_response_id" → u1.present ["run_id", "provider_response_id"] = true → u1 = u2
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ConceptWork.usage_response_is_recorded_once
entries.docstring:
In every consistent state a run's ledger holds at most one row per provider response, which
is what lets a delayed usage frame be retried "without charging the run twice".

entries.statement: ∀ (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.Engine) (requests : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.Engine) (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.SessionRuns), (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.SessionRuns.pin e).launchAll requests = some s → s.pinned = e ∧ ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.EngineRun), r ∈ s.runs → r.engine = e
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.Engine.every_run_of_a_session_carries_the_session_engine
entries.docstring:
Every run reachable in a session pinned to an engine carries that engine: a launch for a
different engine is refused (`409 session_engine_mismatch`) rather than re-pinning the session.

entries.statement: ∀ (driver : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.ImageDriver) (images : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.EngineImageMap) (label : String → String) (state state' : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.Sandboxes) (session engine image : String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.LabelHonest label images → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.create driver images state session engine = (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.CreateResult.created image, state') → label image = engine ∧ state'.created = state.created ++ [(session, image)]
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineImages.driver_starts_only_in_the_runs_engine_image
entries.docstring:
Whatever the driver, a sandbox is created only in the image the map holds for the run's engine,
so under a label-honest map its engine label is the run's engine.

entries.statement: ∀ (driver : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.ImageDriver) (images : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.EngineImageMap) (state : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.Sandboxes) (session engine : String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.installed images engine = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.create driver images state session engine = (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.CreateResult.refused "engine_not_installed", state)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineImages.engine_without_image_creates_no_sandbox
entries.docstring:
An engine with no configured image is refused with `engine_not_installed` by every driver, and
the driver's sandboxes are exactly what they were.

entries.statement: ∀ (driver : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.ImageDriver) (images : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.EngineImageMap) (label : String → String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.LabelHonest label images → ∀ (requests : List (String × String)) (session image : String), (session, image) ∈ (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.createAll driver images { } requests).created → ∃ engine, (session, engine) ∈ requests ∧ label image = engine
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineImages.every_sandbox_carries_its_runs_engine
entries.docstring:
Over any sequence of runs started from no sandbox, every sandbox a driver holds was created for
one of those runs, in an image labelled with that run's engine.

entries.statement: ∀ (poolEngine poolImage : String) (state : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.Sandboxes) (session engine : String), engine ≠ poolEngine → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.createInPool poolEngine poolImage state session engine = (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.CreateResult.refused "engine_not_installed", state)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineImages.pool_refuses_other_engines
entries.docstring: The ACA pool refuses every engine but its own, before an allocation.

entries.statement: ∀ (poolEngine poolImage : String) (label : String → String) (state state' : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.Sandboxes) (session engine image : String), label poolImage = poolEngine → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.createInPool poolEngine poolImage state session engine = (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.CreateResult.created image, state') → label image = engine
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineImages.pool_starts_only_in_the_runs_engine_image
entries.docstring:
The ACA session pool holds one image for one engine; under an honest pool label it too creates
a session only in an image labelled with the run's engine.

entries.statement: ∀ (images : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.EngineImageMap) (runs : List String) (runId engine : String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.installed images engine = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.startRun images runs runId engine = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.RouteAnswer.refused 422 "engine_not_installed" runs
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineImages.route_refuses_before_a_run_row
entries.docstring:
The run route answers `422 engine_not_installed` for an engine with no image, and the run
store is unchanged: no run row exists for a run no sandbox could carry.

entries.statement: ∀ (version dir : String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.loadEngine [] "openai-agents-sdk" = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Lookup.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Refusal.engineNotInstalled ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.loadEngine [{ id := "claude-agent-sdk", version := version, protectedConfigDirectory := dir, loads := false }] "claude-agent-sdk" = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Lookup.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Refusal.engineNotInstalled
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EnginePort.absent_and_unloadable_are_the_same_refusal
entries.docstring:
An engine absent from the table is refused, and an engine present but unloadable is refused
the same way. From the caller's side those are one fact about this image.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EnginePort.an_image_with_no_adapter_reports_none
entries.docstring:
An image carrying no adapter reports no engines, which is the `/healthz` half of the
acceptance criterion.

entries.statement: ∀ (table : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.InstalledAdapter) (capabilities : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Capabilities) (request : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Request) (projectKey configDir : String) (framesIfStarted : Nat) (reason : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Refusal), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.loadEngine table request.engine = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Lookup.refused reason ∨ (∃ adapter, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.loadEngine table request.engine = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Lookup.found adapter) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.compileTarget capabilities request projectKey configDir = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.CompileResult.refused reason → (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.serveRun table capabilities request projectKey configDir framesIfStarted).frames = 0 ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.serveRun table capabilities request projectKey configDir framesIfStarted).terminal = "run-error" ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.serveRun table capabilities request projectKey configDir framesIfStarted).code = some reason.code
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EnginePort.every_refusal_before_start_emits_no_frame
entries.docstring:
Every refusal *before start* emits no frame and answers `run-error` with the refusal's code:
the engine did not load, or it loaded and `compile` refused. Stated over the refusal rather than
over the terminal name, so it does not depend on `run-error` meaning only a refusal — which it
does not in the server, where a run that fails mid-stream also ends with `run-error`.

entries.statement: ∀ (table : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.InstalledAdapter) (capabilities : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Capabilities) (request : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Request) (projectKey configDir : String) (framesIfStarted : Nat), (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.serveRun table capabilities request projectKey configDir framesIfStarted).terminal = "run-error" → (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.serveRun table capabilities request projectKey configDir framesIfStarted).frames = 0
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EnginePort.every_refusal_emits_no_frame
entries.docstring:
In the model, a `run-error` terminal carries no frame — because the model's only `run-error`
is a refusal *before start*. A policy the adapter cannot read and a credential it refuses are
decided by `compile`, which runs before `start`, so the property is about the *ordering* rather
than about one code.

Read the hypothesis as "the model answered `run-error`", not as "the server sent `run-error`":
`apps/runner/src/server.ts` also ends a run that started, streamed frames and then threw with
`run-error`, and `serveRun` has no arm for such a mid-stream failure. The implementation-shaped
statement is `every_refusal_before_start_emits_no_frame` below, which is quantified over the
refusal itself and stays true whatever arms `RunOutcome` later gains.

entries.statement: ∀ (table : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.InstalledAdapter) (id version : String), (id, version) ∈ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.installedEngines table → ∃ row, row ∈ table ∧ row.id = id ∧ row.version = version ∧ row.loads = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EnginePort.healthz_reports_only_what_loaded
entries.docstring:
`/healthz` never reports an engine whose package did not load. This is the other half of the
same claim: the catalogue's `installed` flag is the result of loading, not a reading of a list.

entries.statement: ∀ (table : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.InstalledAdapter) (capabilities : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Capabilities) (request : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Request) (projectKey configDir : String) (framesIfStarted : Nat), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.loadEngine table request.engine = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Lookup.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Refusal.engineNotInstalled → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.serveRun table capabilities request projectKey configDir framesIfStarted = { frames := 0, terminal := "run-error", code := some "engine_not_installed" }
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EnginePort.unregistered_engine_emits_no_frame
entries.docstring:
An engine this image does not carry produces **zero** frames, whatever the engine would have
produced had it been there. Quantified over `framesIfStarted`, which is exactly the "before any
output" claim: the number of frames a started run would have made cannot change the answer.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSkills.a_dropped_skill_is_refused_and_an_empty_request_is_not
entries.docstring:
The vacuity control. An adapter that places nothing must not pass a check about where its
skills land — so a granted skill with no placement is a refusal, and a request that grants nothing
is accepted with zero files.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSkills.a_placement_for_an_ungranted_skill_is_refused
entries.docstring: A placement for a skill nobody granted is refused: those bytes came from somewhere else.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSkills.a_placement_outside_the_declared_directory_is_refused
entries.docstring: A placement at the sandbox root is refused: tenant content beside the agent's working files.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSkills.a_placement_that_climbs_out_is_refused
entries.docstring:
A path that climbs out of the workspace is refused as unusable, before anything about the
configuration directory is asked.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSkills.a_second_engines_directory_is_accepted_the_same_way
entries.docstring:
The same rule, with a **different** engine's directory: the invariant is about the declaration,
not about `.claude`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSkills.a_sibling_directory_is_not_inside_it
entries.docstring:
A sibling directory whose name merely *starts with* the declared one is refused, because the
comparison is by segment and not by string prefix.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSkills.claude_places_every_skill_inside_its_own_directory
entries.docstring: The Claude adapter's own placement is accepted, and every file is written.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSkills.the_directory_itself_is_refused
entries.docstring: The declared directory itself is not inside itself: a file written *at* it is not a skill.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineSkills.skillPlacementVerdict [{ skill := "document-writer", path := ".claude/skills/w/SKILL.md" }, { skill := "document-writer", path := ".claude/skills/w/./SKILL.md" }] [{ name := "document-writer", files := 1 }] AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineSkills.claudeProtectedConfigDirectory = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineSkills.Verdict.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineSkills.Refusal.duplicatePath
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSkills.two_placements_on_one_path_are_refused
entries.docstring:
Two placements on one path are refused: the second write wins silently, and the run would then
use a skill whose contents nobody chose.

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Permissions) (w : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.Key), (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.narrow p w).unrestrictedNetwork = true → p.unrestrictedNetwork = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSwitch.the_narrowing_never_opens_the_network
entries.docstring: The narrowing never turns the network switch on.

entries.statement: ∀ (withheld : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.Key) (deny : List String), (∀ (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.Key), k ∈ withheld → ∀ (n : String), n ∈ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.claudeTools k → n ∈ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.reverseDeny withheld deny) ∧ ∀ (n : String), n ∈ deny → n ∈ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.reverseDeny withheld deny
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSwitch.the_reverse_switch_denies_every_withheld_tool
entries.docstring:
The reverse switch denies every Claude tool of every switch the `openai-agents` arm withheld,
and keeps every denial the new body already had.

entries.statement: ∀ (a : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.ClaudeArm) (existing w : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.Key) (p : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Permissions) (hasReadOnlyGrant : Bool) (t : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.translate a existing = Except.ok w → t ∈ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.toolPlan (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.narrow p w) hasReadOnlyGrant → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.EngineSwitch.claudeAllowsTool p a t = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSwitch.the_switch_never_widens_the_tool_plan
entries.docstring:
The switch never widens the tool plan: every tool the OpenAI Agents adapter offers under the
translated arm is one whose capability the old Claude arm allowed.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.EngineSwitch.the_switch_refuses_exactly_what_it_cannot_express
entries.docstring:
A translation succeeds exactly when no denial of the old arm is untranslatable, and a refusal
names exactly those denials — so an MCP or glob denial is never silently dropped.

entries.statement: ∀ (S : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Schema) (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.consistent S st = true → ∀ {t : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName} {n c : String} {vs : List String}, AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Check.oneOf n c vs ∈ (S t).checks → ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r ∈ st t → ∀ {v : String}, r.get c = some v → v ∈ vs
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.closed_set_value_is_in_its_set
entries.docstring:
In a consistent state, every row of a table with a closed-set check carries in that column
either `NULL` or one of the check's values, under any schema.

entries.docstring:
Under a schema with no unpaired reference, no consistent state holds a reference from a row
of one workspace to a tenant-carrying row of another: cross-tenant references are
unrepresentable in the database.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.null_key_row_preserves_fk
entries.docstring:
A foreign key never constrains a row with a `NULL` in its key (`MATCH SIMPLE`): adding such
a row to a state where the key holds keeps it holding.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.paired_reference_preserves_tenant
entries.docstring:
A reference through a tenant-paired foreign key joins two rows of the same workspace, in any
state and under any schema: the database compares the two tenant columns as part of the key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.principal_has_exactly_one_source
entries.docstring:
In a consistent state, under today's schema, every principal has exactly one source: a
membership principal has a membership and no API key, and an API-key principal has a key and no
membership.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.reference_preserves_tenant
entries.docstring:
In a consistent state, every reference through a foreign key that is neither unpaired nor a
reference to a global table joins two rows of the same workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.root_id_is_the_tenant
entries.docstring:
The typed primary key of a row of the tenant root is exactly its tenant: a `workspaces` row
is its own workspace, so `Row.id?` at kind `workspace` reads the root's tenant column `id`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.scoped_workspace_id_is_the_tenant
entries.docstring:
The typed owning workspace of a row of a tenant-scoped table is exactly its tenant:
`Row.workspaceId?` reads the tenant column `workspace_id`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.sibling_reference_preserves_tenant
entries.docstring:
In a consistent state, a single-column reference covered by a tenant-paired sibling also
joins two rows of the same workspace: the sibling pins a parent row in the child's workspace,
and the parent key is unique, so both constraints reach that one row.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.tenant_path_preserves_tenant
entries.docstring:
Under a schema with no unpaired reference, every row reached from a row by a chain of
references through tenant-carrying tables belongs to the starting row's workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErCore.tenant_row_has_workspace
entries.docstring:
In a consistent state every row of a tenant-carrying table has a workspace (its tenant
column is `NOT NULL`), provided the schema declares that column `NOT NULL`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErSynthesis.composite_reference_stays_in_workspace
entries.docstring:
In any state of today's database, consistent or not, a reference through a composite foreign
key joins two rows of the same workspace.

entries.docstring:
A transaction whose writes would leave a reference from one workspace to a tenant-carrying
row of another is rolled back: the database stays in the state before it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErSynthesis.empty_database_is_consistent
entries.docstring: The empty database satisfies every constraint of today's whole schema.

For each of the five clusters there is a state that satisfies every constraint of the bare
catalogue yet is inconsistent for the whole schema, because it breaks exactly one check that only
that cluster gives a meaning to.

Every composite foreign key of today's schema pairs the child's tenant column with the
parent's, so the database itself compares the two workspaces as part of the key.

workspace to a tenant-carrying row of another.

entries.docstring:
In every consistent state of today's database, every row of a table whose owner column is
`NOT NULL` has exactly one owning principal, in its own workspace.

may be a deleted principal or none.

one principal, and that principal belongs to the row's own workspace.

today's database with a reference from one workspace to a tenant-carrying row of another.

entries.docstring:
In every consistent state of today's whole schema, every row reached from a row by a chain of
references through tenant-carrying tables belongs to the starting row's workspace.

The two checks two clusters both give a meaning to, `workspaces_default_model_pair` (identity
and configuration) and `projects_default_model_pair` (work and configuration), mean the same on
every row in both clusters.

principal of the grant's own workspace.

In every consistent state of the target schema, no foreign-key reference joins a row of one
workspace to a tenant-carrying row of another.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErSynthesis.target_reachable_grant_names_one_principal
entries.docstring:
In every state reachable under the target's constraints, a grant names exactly one principal,
of the grant's own workspace.

entries.docstring:
In every state reachable under the target's constraints, a share's subject column names
exactly one row of its subject type's table, in the share's own workspace.

No sequence of committed transactions under the target's constraints reaches a state with a
reference from one workspace to a tenant-carrying row of another.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErSynthesis.target_share_subject_stays_in_workspace
entries.docstring:
In every consistent state of the target, a share's subject column names exactly one row of its
subject type's table, and that row is in the share's own workspace: a share can no longer name a
missing subject or another workspace's.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.ErSynthesis.target_witness_is_reachable
entries.docstring:
The image of today's witness is reachable under the target's constraints: loading it into an
empty target database in one transaction commits.

entries.docstring:
In every consistent state of today's database, every row of a tenant-scoped table has exactly
one owning workspace: one `workspaces` row whose `id` is the row's `workspace_id`.

entries.docstring:
Successful append keeps exactly the newest `limit` rows of the previous retained log plus
the new event. This states the retention suffix, not merely its size.

One tool call whose arguments fragment across many chunks is charged once, because the deltas
all repeat the same `(choice, index)` pair; three distinct pairs are three calls.

entries.docstring:
Counting distinct item identities is what stops a repeated `function_call` inflating the row:
the stream and the terminal snapshot both name the same item, and it is charged once.

more than the whole one.

the extractor never invents a count.

of its own beyond choosing between a row and a failure. Stated for all three dialects.

the two are additive in the price table, so relaying the raw figure would bill it twice.

neutral frame, `agent.native` or `agent.malformed`.

the step limit, and otherwise the run ends `max_turns` exactly when it reached `maxSteps` with its
last step still asking for tools — so a run that used exactly `maxSteps` steps and stopped on its
own ends `end_turn` — and `end_turn` with no limit.

estimate to the cap: never before it is reached.

entries.docstring:
The adapter's session round trip, as it runs: a readable pi session file is mirrored into an
empty store stream by one `persist` of a prefix of it (an earlier `turn_end`) and a second of the
whole grown file, which rebuilds exactly the file — only the new lines are appended — and reading
the stream back gives the same `id`/`parentId` tree.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.Pi.tool_pairing_holds
entries.docstring:
Tool pairing holds on every mapped stream: every `agent.tool.result` answers a call an earlier
`agent.tool.call` announced and no earlier result answered.

entries.statement: ∀ (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Config) (c : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Ceiling), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.violations (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.meet e c) c = List.map AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Widening.wire (List.filter AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Widening.fixed (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.widenings e c))
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.PolicyCeiling.meet_le_ceiling
entries.docstring:
After the meet, the only widenings left are the engine and the model — exactly those of the
input, which the meet cannot narrow and the caller refuses instead.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.PolicyCeiling.meet_le_input
entries.docstring: The meet asks for no more than the configuration it was given.

entries.statement: ∀ (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Config) (c₁ c₂ : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Ceiling), c₁.le c₂ → (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.meet e (some c₁)).le (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.meet e (some c₂))
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.PolicyCeiling.meet_monotone_in_ceiling
entries.docstring: A tighter ceiling meets to a configuration no wider than a looser ceiling's.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.PolicyCeiling.switch_then_meet_le_ceiling
entries.docstring:
An engine switch, then the ceiling: when the permissions are the switch's narrowing, the meet
keeps every switch the ceiling caps off, and every tool the OpenAI Agents adapter offers under the
met permissions is one the old Claude arm allowed (`the_switch_never_widens_the_tool_plan`).

entries.statement: ∀ (t : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score) (r r' : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release) (op : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op), r.WellFormed → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step t r op = Except.ok r' → r'.WellFormed ∧ ∀ (a : AgentWorkspace.AgentId) (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env) (v : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.VersionNo), r'.pointer a e = some v → r'.hasVersion a v = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.Release.pointer_targets_existing_version
entries.docstring:
Every environment points at a version that exists, for the same agent: a step from a
well-formed state (every history entry names a saved version) reaches a well-formed state, so every
pointer it leaves names a saved version.

entries.statement: ∀ (t : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score) (r r₁ : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release) (a : AgentWorkspace.AgentId) (src dst : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step t r (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op.promote a src dst) = Except.ok r₁ → (r.pointer a dst).isSome = true → ∃ r₂, AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step t r₁ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op.rollback a dst) = Except.ok r₂ ∧ r₂.pointer a dst = r.pointer a dst
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.Release.rollback_after_promote_is_identity
entries.docstring:
Promote then rollback leaves the pointer where it was, whenever the target environment already
pointed somewhere.

entries.statement: ∀ (t : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score) (r r' : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release) (a : AgentWorkspace.AgentId) (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step t r (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op.rollback a e) = Except.ok r' → ∃ cur prev rest, r.history a e = cur :: prev :: rest ∧ r'.pointer a e = some prev ∧ r'.history a e = prev :: rest
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.Release.rollback_restores_previous
entries.docstring:
After `rollback`, the pointer equals the second entry of the history before the step, and the
version it left comes off the history, so a second rollback steps further back (BH061-004).

entries.statement: ∀ (t : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score) (r r' : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release) (op : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step t r op = Except.ok r' → ∀ (a : AgentWorkspace.AgentId), r.versions a <+: r'.versions a
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.Release.versions_append_only
entries.docstring:
No step deletes or changes a saved version: every agent's versions before a step are a prefix
of its versions after it.

No reachable status is ever left for `queued`: once a run has left `queued` it never
returns.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.Runs.run_terminal_is_absorbing
entries.docstring:
A terminal run's status never changes, whatever sequence of operations follows
("first terminal transition wins").

A registry holding a descriptor the published contract cannot describe yields **no** list —
never the publishable subset, which a caller would read as the whole catalogue.

The CLI is the same projection again: `aw engines list` prints the SDK's answer unchanged, in
every output mode. A mode chooses the rendering, never the result set.

The whole of "a total projection": for a registry the contract can describe, the list a client
receives **is** the registry — the same descriptors, each exactly once, in the registry's order.

And a registry with one engine the contracts do not publish answers nothing at all, even
though the other descriptor in it is perfectly describable.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SdkEngines.the_columns_are_scalar_fields
entries.docstring:
The columns name fields of a descriptor, and `capabilities` is deliberately not one of them:
a table cell cannot render it, and `--json` carries it instead.

`--engine` names an engine this deployment registers and installs, or it is refused before
anything is created or changed. There is no third answer, and no silent fall-back to the default:
a descriptor the catalogue lists with `installed := false` is refused exactly like an id it does
not list.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SdkEngines.the_refusal_names_the_published_code

The deployment this release ships projects to itself: every engine it registers is one the
contracts publish.

entries.docstring: Every successful reconnect increments the cumulative count by exactly one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SdkRuns.unexpected_status_precedes_body_validation

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.a_blob_over_the_cap_is_refused
entries.docstring:
**A blob over the cap is refused, and the state is unchanged.**

`putBlob` answers `none`, which the route turns into `413 session_state_too_large`. The unchanged
half is structural: there is no path through the function that writes and then refuses.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.a_clean_store_returns_the_adapters_answer
entries.docstring:
…and the fold can only ever make a verdict worse: a store with nothing to report returns the
adapter's own answer unchanged.

entries.statement: ∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Store) (k : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.StreamKey), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.publicTranscriptRead (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.publicTranscriptDelete st k).fst k (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.publicTranscriptDelete st k).snd = none
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.a_deleted_transcript_reads_as_not_found
entries.docstring:
**After `DELETE …/transcript` the read is `404`**, for a post-ENG-06 session and a legacy one
alike: the stream is gone and so are the legacy rows, so neither side of the fallback answers.

entries.statement: ∀ (adapterSaysDurable : Bool) (failures : Nat), failures ≠ 0 → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.durable adapterSaysDurable failures = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.a_failed_store_write_is_not_durable
entries.docstring:
**A failed store write makes the run non-durable, for every engine.**

The adapter's own answer is quantified over, which is the engine-neutral half: whatever the engine
told its adapter, a store that could not write makes the verdict `false`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.a_posted_transcript_is_read_back
entries.docstring:
**What `POST …/transcript` stores is what `GET …/transcript` reads**, whatever the legacy
tables hold: the append lands in the stream the read serves first.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.an_over_cap_blob_answers_413
entries.docstring: The same claim as the route sees it: the outcome is the refusal, with its code and its status.

entries.statement: ∀ (es : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry) (e : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry), e.key = none → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.upsert es e = es ++ [e]
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.append_of_a_keyless_entry_always_grows_the_stream
entries.docstring:
**An entry with no key is always appended.** The other half of R-01 §7: an entry the engine gave
no identity has nothing to dedup on, so the store must not invent one for it.

entries.statement: ∀ (es : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry) (e : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.Entry) (k : String), e.key = some k → (es.any fun x => x.key == some k) = true → (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.SessionState.upsert es e).length = es.length
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.append_of_a_known_key_does_not_grow_the_stream
entries.docstring:
**Appending an entry whose key is already in the stream does not grow it.**

R-01 §7: the Agent SDK's retries redeliver a batch, so an append must upsert on the entry's key.
The stream a redelivery leaves behind has the same length as the one it found — which is the whole
of "appending the same `entry_key` twice stores one entry".

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.delete_last_of_an_empty_stream_is_empty
entries.docstring: **Delete-last on an empty stream leaves an empty stream**, so a retry is not a failure.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.delete_last_removes_exactly_the_last
entries.docstring: **Delete-last removes exactly the last entry**, and nothing else.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Invariants.SessionState.replace_all_yields_exactly_those_entries
entries.docstring: **Replace-all yields exactly the given entries.** The `PUT` half of the store's contract.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.AuthzDecide.admin_is_not_above_builder_exactly_at
entries.docstring:
The table is **not** monotone in the order Admin ⊇ Builder, and the counterexamples are
exactly these cells: Admin holds nothing over `projects` where Builder does, and no `run` on
`connectors` (unreachable by any path). ADR-0116 closed the `skills` and `files` cells.

entries.statement: (∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (res : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.Resource) (op : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Operation), (AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.grantsFor r res).get op ≠ (AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.grantsForW9Auth165 r res).get op ↔ r = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role.admin ∧ res = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.Resource.runs ∧ op = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Operation.run) ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.grantsForW9Auth165 AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role.admin AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.Resource.runs).run = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grant.none ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.grantsFor AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role.admin AgentWorkspace.Authz.Resources.Resource.runs).run = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grant.any ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideAuth { role := "admin", method := "POST", path := "/api/runs/:id/interrupt", ownership := AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.other, scope := none }).effect = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Effect.allow
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.AuthzDecide.admin_run_verbs_adrs_disagree_at_one_cell
entries.docstring:
W9-AUTH-165's text ("an Admin still cannot start, cancel, or write a run") and SDK-03-RUN-235
(Admin `run: 'any'`, which the code follows) describe tables that differ in exactly one cell,
`(admin, runs, run)`, so an Admin's interrupt is allowed today and denied under W9-AUTH-165.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.AuthzDecide.builder_is_not_above_viewer_exactly_at_agent_runs
entries.docstring:
The table is **not** monotone in the order Builder ⊇ Viewer, at exactly one cell: running an
agent, where Builder holds `own` and Viewer `permitted` (suspicious point 11). Admin is above
Viewer everywhere.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.AuthzDecide.refused_declared_routes_are_the_auth_routes_and_accept
entries.docstring:
Of the 155 declared routes, `decide()` refuses exactly the ten `/api/auth/*` routes,
`GET /api/cron/retention` and the two `/api/a2a/*` routes (an unclassified resource each; the cron
route authenticates itself with `CRON_SECRET`, ADR-0120 clause 7, and the A2A routes with an API
key, ADR-0135), `POST /mcp/projects/:name` and the seven OAuth routes under `/.well-known/` and
`/oauth/` (paths outside `/api`, which the classifier reads as pages; the endpoint authenticates
itself with an endpoint API key, ADR-0134, and the OAuth routes are public by protocol or require a
browser session, ADR-0134 part 3) and `POST /api/invitations/:id/accept` (an unclassified
sub-resource) — twenty-two of the twenty-three routes the matrix exempts by name; the
twenty-third, `GET /api/setup/runtime-detect`, parses as a `setup` row and is decided.

entries.docstring:
§3.1.1 lists two routes a run scope reaches, but `decide()`'s run-scope cell is by
`(resource, operation)` with no sub-resource key, so a run scope also passes `decide()` for
`GET`/`HEAD` on every other `runs` sub-resource of its run (`interrupt`, `revoke-tokens`,

entries.docstring:
Finding: 04 §2 says every row that can be own or other carries `ownerPrincipalId`, and the
tables do, but only the agent and connector bodies carry it on the wire; the file and skill

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.ConceptCatalog.grant_names_two_different_relations
entries.docstring:
The word "grant" names two tables: the data-plane page's "read-only grant" is an `agent_files`
assignment (it has an `access`), while an agent grant (`agent_grants`) has none. The two are
different relations with different endpoints.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.ConceptCatalog.openapi_credential_pairing_is_not_a_database_check
entries.docstring:
Declared gap (ADR-0113 C15): the database does not read inside `tool_config`, so whether an
`openapi` connector names a credential is not tied to its configured authentication. A row whose
`tool_config` asks for a bearer token passes every check of `mcp_servers` with a credential and
without one; the server's admission and `ConnectorResourceSchema` enforce the pairing.

two identifiers are allowed to diverge", but a subtree move cuts the key by the length of the old
path prefix whatever the key holds, so a file whose key is not its path gets a key that names no
object.

Finding: a repeated file id in an assignment body is reported as an unknown file, although it
names a file of the catalog; the same repetition of a skill or connector id is merged silently.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.ConceptCatalog.revoked_principal_keeps_a_hidden_grant
entries.docstring:
Finding: a grant is stored against the user, not the principal, so revoking a membership
principal hides its grant from `listPrincipalIds` without removing the row; the run check, which
reads by user id, still finds it, and un-revoking the principal would show it again. Today no
code path revokes a membership principal (removing a member deletes the membership, which
cascades), so the divergence is latent.

Two slug grammars coexist: a skill name may start with a digit and repeat a hyphen, which the
`oneOf` value gate for closed sets refuses, while a closed-set value such as `read-write`
satisfies both.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.ConceptCatalog.uploading_over_an_existing_path_does_not_make_the_caller_owner
entries.docstring:
Finding: the ownership page says that putting a file in the catalog makes you its
`owner_principal_id`, but uploading to a path that already exists keeps the previous owner and
creator (the catalog's upsert "never transfers it"), so the caller `p2` does not become the owner
of `docs/a.md` that `p1` uploaded first; the same holds for a skill imported under an existing
name.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.ConceptConfiguration.agent_model_may_outlive_its_connection
entries.docstring:
Agents have no pair check: a consistent state holds an agent with a model and no connection,
which is what deleting its connection leaves behind, although the specification says a model
choice is never one without the other.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.ConceptConfiguration.blank_name_rules_disagree
entries.docstring:
Model connections and runtime connections refuse a blank name after JavaScript's `trim`, but
the runtime-profile contract accepts any non-empty name, so a name of one ideographic space is a
valid profile name and PostgreSQL's `btrim` check accepts it too.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.ConceptConfiguration.blank_profile_name_passes_the_contract_but_not_the_check
entries.docstring:
The contract accepts a runtime-profile name made of spaces, which
`runtime_profiles_name_not_blank` refuses: the create route passes it to the database, and the
repository does not classify that violation.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Meta.ConceptConfiguration.connection_encoding_model_is_ascii_only
entries.docstring:
The runtime-connection encoding model is faithful on ASCII labels only: on each recorded
non-ASCII label (`straße`, `ıd`, `ﬁle`) the model's name differs from the one JavaScript's
Unicode-aware `toUpperCase` makes the code store, and none of them is an ASCII label.
