entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.creator_is_legacy_nullable_attribution
entries.docstring:
The ER diagram's `shares.created_by FK`: the legacy creator column is nullable (an API-key
principal has no user) and references `users`, paired with a membership of the same workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.default_runnable_budget_is_twenty_dollars
entries.docstring:
"Budget cap $20 total": a runnable share published without a cap gets twenty dollars, which
fits `budget_cap_usd numeric(12, 4)`.

entries.statement: ∀ (t : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.optionsFit t none false false false false = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.optionsFit AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.agent (some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode.runnable) false true false true = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.optionsFit AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.agent (some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode.definition) false false false true = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.optionsFit AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.session none true false true false = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.every_option_fits_its_subject
entries.docstring:
A command with no options fits every subject type, and each option passes the request schema
on the subject that takes it (the service then refuses `runnable`; see
`runnable_is_refused_in_this_release`).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.every_share_has_a_publisher_principal
entries.docstring:
The ER diagram's `workspace_principals ||--o{ shares : "publisher_principal_id"`: every share
has a non-null publisher, and the key to its principal is tenant-paired.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.expiry_and_passphrase_are_optional
entries.docstring: "Optional expiry … and optional passphrase. Neither is required": both columns are nullable.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share) (e : Nat), s.expiresAt = some e → s.visibility = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Visibility.public → s.revokedAt = none → s.suspendedAt = none → s.stopped = false → s.publiclyOpen e = false ∧ (0 < e → s.publiclyOpen (e - 1) = true)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.expiry_closes_the_link_at_its_instant
entries.docstring:
"Optional expiry": a share whose expiry has come (`expires_at <= now`) does not open, and at
the instant before it a public share with no other cause still opens.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.WireEnum.wires AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Expiry = ["24 h", "7 days", "30 days", "never"] ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Expiry.hours24.durationMs? = some (24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Expiry.days7.durationMs? = some (7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Expiry.days30.durationMs? = some (30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Expiry.never.durationMs? = none
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.expiry_options_and_lifetimes
entries.docstring:
"Optional expiry (`24 h`, `7 days`, `30 days`, `never`)": the four options, of 24 hours, 7
days and 30 days, and `never` sets no expiry.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.files_are_not_shareable
entries.docstring: "Files are not independently shareable": no subject type names the `files` table.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.five_messages_per_visitor_per_hour
entries.docstring: "Per-visitor limit 5 messages per hour": the limit is five and the window one hour.

entries.statement: ∀ (t : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType) (m : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode) (i b tr d : Bool), t ≠ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.session → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.optionsFit t m i b tr d = true → i = false ∧ tr = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.include_and_transcript_are_session_only
entries.docstring:
"`include` is for a session share only": a command for any other subject that fits carries
no `include` and no transcript.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share) (now : Nat), s.publiclyOpen now = true → s.passphraseHash = none → ∀ (a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PassphraseAttempt), s.resolveAt now a = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ResolveOutcome.opened
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.link_without_passphrase_opens_for_everyone
entries.docstring:
"Neither is required": an open public link without a passphrase opens for every visitor,
whatever it presents.

entries.statement: ∀ (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (viewer : AgentWorkspace.PrincipalId) (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share), (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ownerOrAdmin role = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.listedFor role viewer s = true) ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ownerOrAdmin role = false → (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.listedFor role viewer s = true ↔ s.publisher = viewer))
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.list_is_mine_or_all_for_admins
entries.docstring:
"List (mine, or all as Admin/Owner)": an Owner or Admin lists every share of the workspace,
and a Builder or Viewer lists a share exactly when it published it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.live_public_share_always_opens
entries.docstring: A public share that is not revoked, suspended, stopped or expiring opens at every instant.

entries.statement: ∀ (t : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType) (m : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode) (i b tr d : Bool), t ≠ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.agent → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.optionsFit t m i b tr d = true → m = none ∧ b = false ∧ d = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.mode_budget_and_definition_are_agent_only
entries.docstring:
"`mode` and `budgetCapUsd` are for an agent share only": a command for any other subject that
fits carries no mode, no budget and no agent definition.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.one_table_for_every_shareable_object
entries.docstring:
"`shares` is one table for every shareable object, not one table per type": one `NOT NULL`
`subject_type` column whose check admits exactly the four subject types, and one `NOT NULL`
`subject_id` column that no foreign key of `shares` reads, so a single row shape carries every
type's subject.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share) (now : Nat), s.publiclyOpen now = true → s.visibility = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Visibility.public
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.only_a_public_share_opens
entries.docstring:
"Public: anyone with the link, unauthenticated": only a public share opens through
`/p/<token>`; a private or workspace share never does, at any instant.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.passphrase_gates_an_open_link
entries.docstring:
"Optional … passphrase" on opening: a public link that is open and has a passphrase opens
only for the right passphrase, and answers `invalid_passphrase` to a missing or wrong one.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRequest) (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (pse re : Bool) (now : Nat) (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Published), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role pse re now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.published p → p.hasPassphraseHash = Option.any (fun x => !x.isEmpty) r.passphrase
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.passphrase_is_stored_exactly_when_given
entries.docstring:
"Optional passphrase": a passphrase given at publish time is stored (as a hash), and none is
stored when none is given.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.passphrase_length_bounds
entries.docstring: A passphrase is 1 to 1024 code units long (`SHARE_PASSPHRASE_MAX_LENGTH`).

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRequest) (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (runnableEnabled : Bool) (now : Nat), r.visibility = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Visibility.public → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role false runnableEnabled now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRefusal.publicSharingOff ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRefusal.publicSharingOff.code = "invalid_share"
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.public_share_refused_while_public_sharing_is_off
entries.docstring:
"`400 invalid_share` (… public sharing disabled …)" and "it must be enforced server-side":
a `public` request while public sharing is off is refused with `invalid_share`, whatever the
subject, mode, role and release gate.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share), s.revokedAt.isSome = true → ∀ (now : Nat), s.stateAt now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ShareState.revoked ∧ s.publiclyOpen now = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.revoked_link_never_opens
entries.docstring:
"A published link is revocable. Revoking is immediate and permanent for that link": a revoked
share is in state `revoked` and does not open, at every instant.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRequest) (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (now : Nat), r.subjectType = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.agent → r.mode = some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode.runnable → r.visibility ≠ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Visibility.public → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ownerOrAdmin role = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role false true now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.published { mode := some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode.runnable, budgetCapUsd := some (r.budgetCapUsd.getD "20"), expiresAt := (r.expiry.getD AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Expiry.never).expiresAt? now, hasPassphraseHash := Option.any (fun x => !x.isEmpty) r.passphrase }
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.runnable_budget_defaults_to_twenty
entries.docstring:
"Budget cap $20 total": an admitted runnable share published without a cap gets
`defaultRunnableBudgetUsd`, and one published with a cap keeps it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.runnable_is_refused_in_this_release
entries.docstring:
"Runnable public links remain compiled off; … a typed request the server refuses (`400
invalid_share`)": with the release gate as it is today, an agent request for `runnable` mode that
public sharing does not already refuse is refused as unreleased, for every role.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRequest) (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (now : Nat), r.subjectType = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.agent → r.mode = some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode.runnable → (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ownerOrAdmin role = false → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role true true now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.refused AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRefusal.runnableNeedsOwnerOrAdmin) ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ownerOrAdmin role = true → ∃ p, AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role true true now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.published p)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.runnable_requires_owner_or_admin
entries.docstring:
"Publishing a **runnable** public link … requires Admin or Owner": were the release gate
open, a Builder's or Viewer's runnable request is still refused, and an Owner's or Admin's is
admitted.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.share_children_carry_no_principal
entries.docstring:
"The share view and run charge tables are public share-page accounting, out of scope for the
SDK": neither carries an owner or publisher column.

"share_views_share_workspace_fk") = some AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.OnDelete.cascade ∧ Option.map (fun x => x.onDelete) ((AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.shareRunCharges).foreignKey? entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.share_children_cascade
entries.docstring:
Deleting a share deletes its views and its charges (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), and deleting a run
deletes its charge; deleting the workspace deletes all three tables' rows.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.shareable_objects_are_exactly_four
entries.docstring:
"Shareable objects are exactly: agent, session, project, skill": the subject types are those
four, and each names the table of its kind.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.state_fields_are_always_rendered
entries.docstring:
"Suspended links stay listed with their state visible": every rendering carries the
revocation, suspension, stop and expiry fields.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share), s.revokedAt = none → s.suspendedAt = none → s.stopped = true → ∀ (now : Nat), s.stateAt now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ShareState.stopped ∧ s.publiclyOpen now = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.stopped_link_does_not_open
entries.docstring:
"A single 'Stop accepting messages' control, and an automatic stop on budget": a stopped
share that is neither revoked nor suspended is in state `stopped` and does not open.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share), s.revokedAt = none → s.suspendedAt.isSome = true → ∀ (now : Nat), s.stateAt now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.ShareState.suspended ∧ s.publiclyOpen now = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.suspended_link_does_not_open
entries.docstring:
"Existing public links are suspended, not deleted, when the policy is turned off": a
suspended, unrevoked share is in state `suspended` and does not open.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.three_visibilities
entries.docstring:
"Three visibilities, for every shareable object": private, workspace and public, stored in the
`NOT NULL` column `visibility`.

entries.statement: ∀ (v : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Visibility) (withViewCount : Bool), (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.persistenceOnlyKeys.all fun k => !(AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.resourceKeys v withViewCount).contains k) = true ∧ (v ≠ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Visibility.public → (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.resourceKeys v withViewCount).contains "url" = false)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.token_never_crosses_the_wire_as_a_field
entries.docstring:
"The token of a private or workspace share never crosses the wire": no rendered key is the
token or another persistence-only column, and a non-public share renders no `url`.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share), (s.url?.isSome = true ↔ s.visibility = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Visibility.public) ∧ (s.visibility = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Visibility.public → s.url? = some ("/p/" ++ s.token))
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.url_exactly_when_public
entries.docstring:
"`url` (`/p/<token>`) only when public": a share carries a URL exactly when it is public, and
that URL is `/p/` followed by its token.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.view_count_only_on_list_items
entries.docstring:
"`viewCount` is present on list items only": the key is rendered exactly when a count is
given.

entries.docstring: In every consistent state, every `audit_events` row references exactly one `workspaces` row through `audit_events_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.audit_row_invariants
entries.docstring:
In every consistent state an audit row has two non-blank labels, and a recorded subject id
has the canonical UUID shape (so its link can resolve).

entries.statement: ∀ (events : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.RunEvent) (run : AgentWorkspace.RunId), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.logContiguous events run = true → (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.sequencesOf events run).Nodup ∧ (∀ (n : Nat), n ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.sequencesOf events run → 1 ≤ n) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.logContiguous AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.interleaved✝ { val := "ra" } = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.logContiguous AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.interleaved✝ { val := "rb" } = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isWindow (List.map (fun x => x.key.sequence) AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.interleaved✝) = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.logContiguous (List.filter (fun x => x.key.sequence != 2) AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.interleaved✝) { val := "ra" } = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isWindow [3, 4, 5] = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isWindow [1, 3] = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isWindow [2, 2] = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isWindow [2, 1] = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isWindow [0, 1] = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.contiguous_log_has_distinct_positive_sequences
entries.docstring:
"Durable, ordered SSE events for one run. Sequence numbers are contiguous per run": when the
events a table stores for one run form a contiguous log, that run's sequences are distinct and
positive; contiguity is judged per run, so another run's events interleaved in the same table do
not break it, while a gap, a repeat, a reordering or a `0` in the run's own sequences does.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run) (s e : Nat), r.startedAt = some s → r.endedAt = some e → r.durationMs = some (e - s) ∧ (r.endedAfterStarted = true → s + (e - s) = e)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.duration_is_end_minus_start
entries.docstring:
Once both timestamps exist, `durationMs` is the end time minus the start time, so a
well-formed finished run's duration added to its start is its end.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.duration_needs_both_timestamps
entries.docstring: "`durationMs` is `null` until both `startedAt` and `endedAt` exist".

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName "a" = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName ("a" ++ String.ofList (List.replicate 63 '9')) = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName ("a" ++ String.ofList (List.replicate 64 '9')) = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName "Z.b_c-9" = true ∧ (["", "1abc", "_abc", "-abc", ".abc", "a b", "a:b", "é"].all fun x => !AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName x) = true ∧ ∀ (s : String), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName s = true → s.length ≤ 64
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.event_name_pattern_edges
entries.docstring:
`EVENT_NAME_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/` on its edges: a one-letter name and
a 64-character name pass, a 65-character name fails, and a name that is empty, starts with a
digit, `_`, `-` or `.`, or holds a space, `:` or a non-ASCII letter fails; every accepted name is
at most 64 characters.

entries.statement: (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.controlFrameNames.all fun n => AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.frameKind? n == some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.control) = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.frameKind? AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.runStatusEvent = some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.platform ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.relayedEventNames.all fun n => AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.frameKind? n == some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.relayed) = true ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.controlFrameNames ++ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.runStatusEvent :: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.relayedEventNames).Nodup ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.control.durable = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.platform.durable = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.relayed.durable = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.frame_kinds_are_disjoint_and_only_control_is_transient
entries.docstring:
Control frames "carry no `id:` and never move the resume cursor", while `run.status` and the
relayed runtime events are durable; the three name lists are disjoint, so every listed name has
exactly one kind.

entries.statement: ∀ (records : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord), (records = [] → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting records = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.pending) ∧ (records ≠ [] → (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting records).isPriced = records.any AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord.isPriced) ∧ (records ≠ [] → records.all AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord.isPriced = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting records = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.complete) ∧ (records ≠ [] → (records.all fun x => !x.isPriced) = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting records = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.unavailable)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.ledger_accounting_follows_the_priced_rows
entries.docstring:
The ledger's accounting state: no settlement is `pending`; after one, it is priced exactly
when some ledger row is priced, `complete` when every row is and `unavailable` when none is.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.listed_frame_names_are_well_formed
entries.docstring:
Every listed frame name satisfies `EVENT_NAME_PATTERN`, the grammar every `event:` name must
satisfy.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.main_transcript_has_no_wire_subpath
entries.docstring:
The main transcript is stored under the empty subpath, which the wire refuses as a subpath
("the empty string is refused rather than read as 'none'"), and every wire subpath is at most
128 characters.

entries.statement: ∀ (records : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord), records.any AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord.isPriced = true → (records.any fun x => !x.isPriced) = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting records = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.partial
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.mixed_ledger_is_partial
entries.docstring:
A ledger with at least one priced and at least one unpriced row is `partial`: the run's
cost is known for some of its responses but not all of them.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : String), s.toList.head? = some '-' → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.isZeroDecimal s = false → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.isNonNegDecimal s = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.negative_nonzero_decimal_is_refused
entries.docstring:
A leading `-` on a nonzero decimal is refused by the `≥ 0` half of the counter checks: the
only negative-signed amount a run or a ledger row may carry is a spelling of zero.

entries.statement: ∀ (id : AgentWorkspace.RunId) (ws : AgentWorkspace.WorkspaceId) (session : AgentWorkspace.SessionId) (now : Nat), have r := AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run.create id ws session now; r.status = AgentWorkspace.Contracts.RunStatus.queued ∧ r.accountingState = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.pending ∧ r.counters.totalTokens = 0 ∧ r.costUsd = "0.000000" ∧ r.priceTableVersion = none ∧ r.durationMs = none ∧ r.wellFormed = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.new_run_is_queued_unpriced_and_well_formed
entries.docstring:
A run exists as soon as it is started, as `queued` ("the run already exists, with
`status: 'queued'`"), with zero usage, the zero cost `'0.000000'` in USD, no price table version
and accounting `pending`, and it passes every check.

entries.statement: ∀ (a : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState), (a.isSettled = true ↔ a = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.complete) ∧ (a.isSettled = true → a.isPriced = true) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.partial.isPriced = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.partial.isSettled = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.only_complete_is_settled
entries.docstring:
Settlement is a separate question from pricing: only `'complete'` is "a settled answer",
every settled state is priced, and `'partial'` is priced without being settled.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.project_default_model_travels_with_its_connection
entries.docstring:
A well-formed project's default model travels with its default connection (the project rung
of the rule "no layer of the model-resolution ladder may mix a connection from one level with a
model from another").

entries.statement: ∀ (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.Project), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.Project.listedBy AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.ProjectListFilter.active p = !AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.Project.listedBy AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.ProjectListFilter.archived p ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.Project.listedBy AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.ProjectListFilter.all p = true ∧ (p.state = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Project.ProjectState.archived ↔ p.archivedAt.isSome = true)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.project_list_filters_partition
entries.docstring:
The `?archived=` filters partition projects: every project is listed by exactly one of
`active` and `archived`, and by `all`; its state is `archived` exactly when `archivedAt` is set.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.project_row_invariants
entries.docstring:
In every consistent state a project row's name has a character other than a space, and its
default model connection and default model are set together or not at all.

position is at most its sequence keeps that shape at every later sequence; a position after the

A session is resumable exactly when it is active and the SDK has reported its id; so an
archived session is never resumable, and a session the SDK never started launches fresh.

through `runs_session_workspace_fk` (the one reference `run_reaches_exactly_one_agent` and

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.run_join_refuses_another_workspace_or_session
entries.docstring:
The cross-tenant counterexamples: the witness run reaches the witness session's agent and
owner, but a session carrying the same session id in workspace `w2`, or another session of the
same workspace, reaches neither.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.run_reaches_agent_and_owner_only_through_its_own_session
entries.docstring:
A run reaches an agent through a session exactly when that session is the run's own session
in the run's own workspace, and the agent is then the session's; the owning principal likewise.
A session with the run's session id in another workspace yields nothing: the concept join is
the composite `(workspace_id, session_id)` key, never the bare id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.run_reaches_exactly_one_agent

A run reaches exactly one agent, through its session: `Run(… → Session, → Agent …)`, with no
`agent_id` of its own ("the run reaches its agent through `session_id`. One join, no way to be
wrong").

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.run_reaches_exactly_one_owner
entries.docstring:
A run reaches exactly one owning principal, through its session: `runs` carries no
`owner_principal_id`, and a run is "own" or "other" by its session's owner.

"A finished run has an end time and an unfinished one does not": in every consistent state a
run row has `ended_at` exactly when its status is terminal.

In every consistent state a run row carries a price table version exactly when its
accounting state is `complete` or `partial`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.session_user_is_a_member_of_its_workspace
entries.docstring:
"The person a session belongs to must hold a membership in the workspace the session is
in": a session row with a user has a membership row for that user in its own workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.tenant_scope_accepts_a_workspace_key
entries.docstring:
With a non-blank configuration directory, the tenant session scope keyed by a workspace id is
always accepted by `validateTenantSessionScope`.

entries.statement: (["con", "COM1", "lpt9", "", "a/b", "..", String.ofList (List.replicate 65 'k')].all fun k => !AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk k "/var/lib/aw") = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk "workspace-1" " \t\n" = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk "workspace-1" "" = false ∧ (["　", " ", " ", " ", "﻿", "   "].all fun d => !AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk "workspace-1" d) = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk "workspace-1" "​" = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk (String.ofList (List.replicate 64 'k')) "/var/lib/aw" = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.tenant_scope_refusals
entries.docstring:
The refusals, by case: a device-name key (`con`, `COM1`, `lpt9`), an empty or 65-character
key, a key with a `/` or `.`, and a blank configuration directory (ASCII blanks, or the Unicode
blanks `String.prototype.trim` also strips: U+3000, U+2028, U+205F, U+1680, U+FEFF) are all
refused, while a 64-character key under a real directory is accepted, and a directory holding a
zero-width space (U+200B, not whitespace to ECMAScript) is not blank.

entries.statement: ∀ (k d : String), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk k d = true → 1 ≤ k.length ∧ k.length ≤ 64 ∧ (∀ (c : Char), c ∈ k.toList → c ≠ '/' ∧ c ≠ '\\' ∧ c ≠ '.') ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.isWindowsDeviceName k = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.isBlank d = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.tenant_scope_refuses_unsafe_keys
entries.docstring:
`validateTenantSessionScope` accepts only a scope the SDK keeps apart from every other: the
key is one directory name of 1 to 64 characters with no path separator and no `.` (so no `..`
and no hidden or relative path), it is not a Windows device name, and the configuration directory
is not blank.

entries.statement: ∀ (c d : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.Counters), c.totalTokens = { inputTokens := c.inputTokens, outputTokens := c.outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens := c.cacheReadInputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens := c.cacheCreationInputTokens, toolCalls := 0 }.totalTokens ∧ (c.add d).totalTokens = c.totalTokens + d.totalTokens ∧ { inputTokens := 1, outputTokens := 2, cacheReadInputTokens := 4, cacheCreationInputTokens := 8, toolCalls := 16 }.totalTokens = 15
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.total_tokens_is_the_sum_of_four_counters
entries.docstring:
`totalTokens` is "the sum of the four" token counters: it never counts tool calls, and it
adds up across settlements (the total of a sum of counters is the sum of their totals).

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Run.Run), r.wellFormed = true → r.accountingState.isPriced = false → r.priceTableVersion = none ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.isZeroDecimal r.costUsd = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.unpriced_run_has_no_version_and_costs_zero
entries.docstring:
A well-formed run carries a price table version exactly when its usage is priced
(`priceTableVersion` "`null` until priced"), and a run whose usage is not priced costs zero.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.unpriced_run_row_costs_zero
entries.docstring: In every consistent state a run row whose usage is not priced costs exactly zero.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.well_formed_run_ends_iff_terminal
entries.docstring: A well-formed run has an end time exactly when its status is terminal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.work_row_counters_are_natural
entries.docstring:
In every consistent state every token counter of a run row or a ledger row is a
non-negative integer.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.work_rows_settle_in_usd
entries.docstring: In every consistent state every run row and every ledger row settles in USD.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : String), AgentWorkspace.Uuid.isCanonical s = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.isProjectKey s = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.isWindowsDeviceName s = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.workspace_id_is_a_safe_project_key
entries.docstring:
The transcript project key "is the caller's workspace id by construction", and that is always
safe: every canonical UUID matches `PROJECT_KEY_PATTERN` (the SDK's own validator) and is not a
Windows device name, so a workspace id never makes the SDK silently fall back to a key shared
across tenants.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : String), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.isZeroDecimal s = true → ∀ (c : Char), c ∈ s.toList → c.isDigit = true → c = '0'
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.zero_decimal_has_no_nonzero_digit
entries.docstring:
A decimal the model reads as zero has no digit other than `0`, which is what
`runs_unpriced_cost_zero`'s `cost_usd = 0` compares.

entries.statement: (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentCapabilities.all fun cap => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentDemands.all fun demand => match AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.unsupportedCapability cap demand with | some AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.mcp => demand.connectors && !cap.mcp | some AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.skills => demand.skills && !cap.skills | some AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.subagents => demand.subagents && !cap.subagents | none => true) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.a_capability_refusal_names_a_real_gap
entries.docstring:
When it refuses, the capability it names is one the engine really lacks **and** the agent really
demands. A refusal never names a capability that is beside the point.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.a_refusal_only_names_a_published_capability
entries.docstring:
Every capability a refusal can name is one the published capability set has a field for, so a
`details` entry always points at something an engine descriptor really states.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.a_registered_engine_reaches_the_union
entries.docstring:
The engine this deployment does register reaches the union, and the union's answer is the
parser's answer. Nothing above turns a well-formed Claude policy into a refusal.

entries.statement: (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentCapabilities.all fun cap => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentDemands.all fun demand => (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.saveAgent cap demand == AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.saved) == (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.compose (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.abstractAgent✝ demand) (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.abstractEngine✝ cap) == AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.ComposeResult.accepted)) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.capability_check_refines_compose
entries.docstring:
The save-time check refines ENG-01's `compose`: it saves exactly when `compose` accepts. So the
concrete refusal is the abstract rule instantiated, not a second rule that happens to resemble it.

entries.statement: (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentCapabilities.all fun cap => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentDemands.all fun demand => (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.unsupportedCapability cap demand).isNone == AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.honoursAssignments cap demand) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.capability_refusal_is_exact
entries.docstring:
The check refuses **exactly** the agents whose connectors, skills or subagents the engine cannot
honour: no refusal precisely when every demanded resource is supported, and a refusal in every
other case. Both directions, which is what rules out a check that is merely conservative.

entries.statement: (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentDemands.all fun demand => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.saveAgent AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.claudeAssignmentCapabilities demand == if demand.subagents = true then AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.unsupported AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.subagents else AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.saved) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.claude_agent_sdk_never_refuses_an_assignment
entries.docstring:
Nothing changes for `claude-agent-sdk`'s assignments. It honours both assignable resources, so
the check never fires for it on connectors or skills, whatever the agent is assigned — which is why
the refusal of an assignment needs a test-only descriptor to be reachable at all. A subagent is a
different matter: like every catalogue engine it declares `subagents: false`, so a demand for one is
refused naming `subagents`, whatever else the agent is assigned.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.default_registry_is_the_catalogue
entries.docstring: The registry a deployment installs by default is exactly the published catalogue.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.engine_capability_unsupported_is_a_four_twenty_two
entries.docstring:
The refusal travels as `422 engine_capability_unsupported`, and its `details` is exactly the
capability — one published wire string, never prose a client would have to parse.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.legacy_provider_discriminant_is_always_refused
entries.docstring:
A body carrying `provider` and no `engine` is refused as `invalid_body`, whatever the union
would have said about the rest of it. There is no silent acceptance of the old shape.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.legacy_refusal_names_the_rename
entries.docstring:
The refusal carries `invalid_body` at `400`, not the union's `invalid_policy`: a client on the
old shape is told about the rename rather than handed a list of complaints about a missing key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.naming_both_discriminants_is_refused
entries.docstring:
Naming **both** discriminants is refused too. The engine check passes — `claude-agent-sdk` is
registered — and the union refuses the extra key, so the body reaches `invalid_policy` rather than
being read as either shape.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.the_refusal_is_about_the_registry
entries.docstring:
`unsupported_engine` is a statement about the **registry**, not about the spelling: registering
acp moves the same body off that refusal and onto the union's own verdict.

entries.statement: (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.unregisteredBodies✝.all fun j => AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.unionVerdicts✝.all fun accept => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.defaultRegistered accept j == AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.unsupportedEngine) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.unregistered_engine_is_always_refused
entries.docstring:
An engine this deployment does not register is refused as `unsupported_engine`, whatever the
union would have said. A body whose `engine` is not even a string is refused here too: it names an
engine, and no registry contains it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.unsupported_engine_is_a_four_hundred
entries.docstring: The refusal carries `unsupported_engine` at `400`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.api_key_not_permitted_is_not_shared
entries.docstring:
`api_key_not_permitted` is not one of the shared codes: it belongs to the workspace and
invitation routes.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.bare_message_defaults_to_empty

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.common_code_statuses_are_documented

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.common_codes_match_errors_guide
entries.docstring: The shared codes and their statuses are, row for row, the errors guide's table.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.detail_becomes_message

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.envelopes_are_pairwise_disjoint
entries.docstring:
No JSON value is accepted by two of the three envelope schemas: the standard envelope needs
`message`, which the older RBAC envelope's strict `{ code, detail }` refuses (a standard body may
carry the deprecated `detail` beside `message`, never instead of it), and the bare envelope's
`error` is a string.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.foreign_bodies_are_unrecognised
entries.docstring:
A body that is none of the three envelopes (an HTML page, `null`, an empty object, a top-level
`code`) is not read as a problem: the SDK then reports `unrecognised_error_body`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.iso_date_time_is_utc
entries.docstring:
An instant `IsoDateTimeSchema` accepts is written in UTC: it ends in `Z`, and every character
is a digit or one of `- T : . Z`, so no `+hh:mm` or `-hh:mm` offset and no lower-case designator
can appear.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.normalise_is_order_free
entries.docstring:
The order in which `readProblem` tries the three envelopes never changes its answer: trying
them in the reverse order gives the same result on every body.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.standard_envelope_is_read_as_itself
entries.docstring: A standard envelope is read as its own body.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsRuns.archived_session_should_not_resume
entries.docstring: The wire schema accepts `resumable` as a boolean; derivation is a server obligation.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsRuns.list_envelope_refuses_empty_cursor
entries.docstring: A cursor is opaque to this response schema but must be nonempty when present.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsRuns.list_envelope_refuses_items_key
entries.docstring: The list envelope uses `runs`, with a nullable opaque cursor.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsRuns.start_202_contract
entries.docstring: SPEC §5.12: the 202 body is a run plus a nonempty stream path.

entries.docstring:
A run's billed usage is the sum of the gateway's ledger rows alone: two runs with the same
ledger bill the same, and changing what the engine reported about itself changes nothing.

entries.docstring:
Composing an agent with an engine either accepts with every portable requirement honoured, or
refuses naming at least one requirement the engine does not support; it never accepts while
dropping one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.EngineImages.catalogue_is_the_map
entries.docstring:
Every registered engine is listed, and a row reports `installed` exactly when the configured
map has an image for that engine.

The control plane never refuses a value for being unpinned, in production or out: the digest
rule belongs to the process that starts containers from the value (ADR-0073 D5). A refusal at the
control plane is only ever an unknown engine, a value that is not a reference, or a duplicate.

A configuration with an entry at fault — a key the catalogue does not publish, or a value the
parser does not accept — fails parsing as a whole, and the refusal names that entry's key.

The refusal is determined by the configured keys and the verdicts on their values: two
configurations that agree on those are refused identically, whatever their values are.

The runner manager, which starts sandboxes from the map, refuses in production any published
engine configured with a well-shaped reference that is not pinned by `sha256` digest, and names that
engine. This is where ADR-0073 D5's digest rule lives.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.EngineImages.startup_refusal_names_only_engine_ids

At the control plane the configuration is the environment, and a start-up refusal names only
engine ids the catalogue publishes — never a variable's value.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.EnginePort.claude_reaches_every_provider
entries.docstring:
The positive witness: today's only engine reaches today's every provider, because every
provider answers the gateway's own Anthropic Messages shape.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.EnginePort.no_overlap_is_refused
entries.docstring:
The refusal arm: no overlap, no run. `engine_model_protocol_unsupported` is the only answer,
because a run composed anyway would fail at its first model call with a provider error.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.EnginePort.resolved_protocol_is_served
entries.docstring:
A resolved protocol is one the **gateway** serves for that provider. The other half: together
the two say the answer lies in the intersection, which is what "servable" means.

entries.docstring:
A resolved protocol is one the **engine** declared. Not implied by the acceptance above: a
resolver that answered with the gateway's first dialect would satisfy it and would compose a run
on a protocol the engine cannot speak.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.EnginePort.responses_only_engine_cannot_reach_anthropic
entries.docstring:
The negative witness, which is the case the check exists for: a Responses-only engine pointed
at an Anthropic connection the gateway will not forward an OpenAI body to.

"`agent_grants` stores the membership's `user_id`": a grant row has a `user_id`, no principal
column, and its person is pinned to a membership of the grant's workspace.

ADR-0083: a CLI sign-in names its person through their Membership —
`cli_sessions_member_workspace_fk` is `(workspace_id, user_id) → memberships (workspace_id,
user_id)`, tenant-paired and `ON DELETE CASCADE` — so a sign-in exists only while its person is a

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ErCore.closed_set_check_admits_only_its_values

"A named `CHECK (<column> IN (...))` constraint over a closed set of string values": the
closed-set check `agent_files_access_valid` accepts rows whose `access` is `read` or
`read-write`, refuses a row with any other value (including a differently cased one), and, as
SQL's `NULL IN (…)` is not false, passes a row whose `access` is `NULL`.

`{id, workspace_id}`, the target of every tenant-paired reference into them.

The one partial unique key: at most one pending (neither accepted nor revoked) invitation per
workspace and address.

sessions and skills, and each references `workspace_principals` through a tenant-paired key.

entries.docstring:
The owner equivalents: `shares.publisher_principal_id` and
`browser_tokens.minted_by_principal_id` are `NOT NULL`, `audit_events.actor_principal_id` is
nullable, and all three reference `workspace_principals` through a tenant-paired key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ErCore.pending_invitations_are_unique_per_address
entries.docstring:
The partial unique key `invitations_workspace_email_pending_key`: two pending invitations to
one address in one workspace violate it, while an accepted or revoked invitation does not count,

"A principal has one source: a human Membership or a machine API key": the
`workspace_principals_source_xor` check accepts a membership principal with only a membership, and
an API-key principal with only a key, and refuses a principal with both sources, with none, or
with the source that does not match its kind.

"The source pair is tenant-paired" (the comment on `workspacePrincipals`): a principal's
membership and API-key sources are each referenced through a tenant-paired key, and the kind

`workspace_id` column, and no other table has one.

"A workspace is the tenant": `workspaces` is the tenant root, `users` and `user_identities`
are the only global tables, and every other table is tenant-scoped.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ErSynthesis.a_principal_of_another_kind_never_resolves
entries.docstring:
A principal whose kind is not `membership` never resolves a browser session, even when it names
the member's membership.

entries.docstring:
Revoking the owner's principal stops today's resolution of the owner's browser session, although
the user, the membership and the workspace are unchanged; the revoked state is itself a consistent
state of today's schema.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ErSynthesis.current_role_is_read_from_the_membership
entries.docstring:
Today, the role a browser session resolves to is the role stored on the membership of the user
the session's email names, in the workspace its slug selects; the token's role claim is not read.

and the resolved principal belongs to that workspace.

One identity holds different permissions in different workspaces: in the witness state the
user `u2` is a viewer of workspace `one` and the owner of workspace `two`, so no function of the
user alone decides a role.

member's own membership, never to an API-key principal.

the membership of the session's user in the selected workspace, never a value carried by the
token.

In the proposed target resolution, a workspace selection is honoured only through a membership in
that workspace: the resolved principal belongs to the workspace the slug selects.

proxy buffering.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.GatewayIngress.a_hosted_tool_field_is_refused_on_every_relayed_protocol
entries.docstring:
The other way a request can ask for vendor-hosted execution is refused with the same code: Chat
Completions turns on OpenAI's hosted web search through a top-level `web_search_options` rather than
a `tools` entry, so a request declaring no tool at all is still refused.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.GatewayIngress.a_self_contained_body_does_not_ask_for_vendor_state
entries.docstring:
Only a listed field asks: a body that keeps its context and instructions in the request — its
`input`, `instructions`, `tools` and even an explicit `store` — does not ask for vendor-held state.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.GatewayIngress.an_anthropic_sdk_request_keeps_its_envelope_on_every_family
entries.docstring:
The regression this rule exists to prevent, stated over every connection family: an Anthropic-SDK
request gets the Anthropic envelope whichever family serves the run, including the three OpenAI ones
that `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` also points at the gateway. The family is not an input to the decision.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.GatewayIngress.anthropic_messages_is_accepted_by_every_family
entries.docstring:
Anthropic Messages is accepted on every connection family: this unit adds ingress, it does not
narrow the ingress that existed.

entries.docstring:
And the `unavailable` outcome is that rule's alone: on `anthropic-messages` an unmetered response
settles `failed` whether or not it declared itself finished, which is what "Anthropic ingress
behaviour is unchanged" means for the accounting path (ADR-0068 D9).

Azure relays its deployment, not the client's model; every other family relays the client's
own choice (ADR-0068 D8).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Mastra.accepted_agent_offers_exactly_the_permitted_tools
entries.docstring:
An accepted agent offers exactly the workspace tools the four permission switches allow, with
the command tools withheld while a read-only grant exists, and is given network egress exactly when
`unrestrictedNetwork` allows it.

entries.statement: ∀ (c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Connector) (rest : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Connector), c.readable = true → c.asksApproval = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compileConnectors (c :: rest) = Except.error (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "approvals")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Mastra.an_approval_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
A connector tool whose policy asks for a human approval is refused naming `approvals`: the
engine runs no approvals (ADR-0065 D9), so the tool is never offered on other terms.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant} {b t w : String} {p : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.gateway = some (b, t, w) → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.ofWire? w = some p → r.environmentClean = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.databaseEnvClean r.envNames = true → r.budgetCap = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.priced (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.modelOf r p) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "maxBudget")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Mastra.an_unpriced_budget_cap_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
A per-run budget cap the provisional price table cannot price is refused naming `maxBudget`
(ADR-0074 D7, shared by ADR-0084).

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant} {b t w : String}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.gateway = some (b, t, w) → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.ofWire? w = none → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "wireProtocols")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Mastra.an_unspoken_protocol_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
A connection served over a dialect the adapter does not speak is refused naming
`wireProtocols`.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.ok c → c.memory.semanticRecall = false ∧ c.memory.workingMemory = false ∧ c.memory.generateTitle = false ∧ c.memory.resourceId = r.projectKey ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.threadOf r = some c.memory.threadId
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Mastra.semantic_recall_and_working_memory_are_off
entries.docstring:
Every accepted agent runs with semantic recall, working memory and title generation off, on
the platform's own thread and the tenant's namespace.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.Outcome.ok c → c.skillTools = !(AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.skillSet r.skills).isEmpty ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Mastra.compileConnectors r.connectors = Except.ok c.connectors
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Mastra.skills_and_connectors_are_honoured
entries.docstring:
An accepted agent is offered the skill tools exactly when it is granted a skill, and hands
`MCPClient` exactly the connectors the request carries.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills = [] → r.session = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.SessionMode.fork → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "fork")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.a_fork_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring: A fork is refused naming `fork`.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills ≠ [] → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "skills")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.a_granted_skill_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
A granted skill is refused `engine_capability_unsupported` naming `skills` (the engine
declares `skills: false`), never dropped.

entries.statement: ∀ (c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Connector) (rest : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Connector), c.asksApproval = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compileConnectors (c :: rest) = Except.map (fun x => c.name :: x) (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compileConnectors rest)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.a_remote_connector_needs_no_network_switch
entries.docstring:
Remote MCP parity with the Claude engine (Owner decision on #308, ADR-0074 D2): a connector
that asks for no approval is compiled whether it is remote or stdio, so `unrestrictedNetwork` off
never removes an assigned remote connector.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (t : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool), t ∈ c.tools ↔ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool.permitted r.permissions t = true ∧ ¬(t = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool.shell ∧ (c.grants.any fun x => x.readOnly) = true)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.accepted_agent_offers_exactly_the_permitted_tools
entries.docstring:
An accepted agent offers exactly the tools the four permission switches allow, with `shell`
withheld while a read-only grant exists.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → c.budgetCap = r.budgetCap ∧ (r.budgetCap = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.priced r.model = true)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.an_accepted_budget_cap_is_priced_and_compiled
entries.docstring:
Every accepted compile carries the request's cap into the configuration the boundary enforces
it from, and a cap is only ever accepted on a model the provisional table prices: the cap is
neither dropped nor accepted unenforceable (ADR-0074 D7).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.an_unhonourable_connector_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
A connector whose tool asks for a human approval is refused naming `approvals`; it is not
silently left out.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills = [] → r.session ≠ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.SessionMode.fork → r.budgetCap = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.priced r.model = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "maxBudget")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.an_unpriced_budget_cap_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
A per-run budget cap the provisional price table cannot price — an unlisted model, or none
named — is refused naming `maxBudget`: a cap that could never stop the run is not accepted
(ADR-0074 D7).

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant} {b t w : String}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills = [] → r.session ≠ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.SessionMode.fork → r.budgetCap = false → r.gateway = some (b, t, w) → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.ofWire? w = none → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "wireProtocols")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.an_unspoken_protocol_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring: A protocol the engine does not speak is refused naming `wireProtocols`.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant} {b t : String}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills = [] → r.session ≠ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.SessionMode.fork → r.budgetCap = false → r.gateway = some (b, t, "anthropic-messages") → r.model = none → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "model")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.anthropic_without_a_model_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
An Anthropic-family connection with no model named is refused naming `model`: the AI SDK
adapter has no default model, and the adapter does not invent one.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → ∃ b t w, r.gateway = some (b, t, w) ∧ c.connection.protocol.toWire = w ∧ c.connection.client = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.clientFor c.connection.protocol
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.compiled_protocol_is_the_gateway_protocol
entries.docstring:
An accepted compile speaks exactly the protocol the gateway connection names, through the
client that protocol selects.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (t : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool), t ∈ c.tools → t.wireType = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ToolType.function ∧ t.wireType.isRelayable = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.no_vendor_hosted_tool_is_compiled
entries.docstring:
No compiled tool is vendor-hosted: every one is sent as a function tool, which the gateway's
closed hosted-tool allowlist relays.

entries.statement: (["openai", "azure-openai", "openai-compatible"].all fun provider => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.resolveWireProtocol AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.engineProtocols provider == some "openai-responses") = true ∧ (["anthropic", "anthropic-compatible"].all fun provider => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.resolveWireProtocol AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.engineProtocols provider == some "anthropic-messages") = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.clientFor AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.openaiResponses = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Client.openai ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.clientFor AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.openaiChatCompletions = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Client.openai ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.clientFor AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.anthropicMessages = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Client.aisdkAnthropic
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.the_protocol_follows_the_connection
entries.docstring:
Compose resolves an OpenAI-family connection to the Responses dialect and an Anthropic-family
one to Messages for this engine, and the compiled client follows the protocol: `OpenAIProvider`
for the two OpenAI dialects, `aisdk()` for Messages.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.the_sdk_shell_tool_type_is_not_relayed
entries.docstring:
Why the tools are function tools: the SDK's own `shell` tool type is one the gateway refuses
as hosted, so an adapter that compiled it could not reach its model through the gateway.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.connectors ≠ [] → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "mcp")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Pi.a_connector_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
A connector is refused `engine_capability_unsupported` naming `mcp` on a request whose policy
and grants read, never dropped and never bridged.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (t : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Tool), t ∈ c.tools ↔ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Tool.permitted r.permissions t = true ∧ ¬(t = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Tool.bash ∧ (c.grants.any fun x => x.readOnly) = true)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Pi.accepted_agent_offers_exactly_the_permitted_tools
entries.docstring:
An accepted agent offers exactly the tools the four permission switches allow, with `bash`
withheld while a read-only grant exists.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.connectors = [] → r.budgetCap = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.priced (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.modelOf r) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "maxBudget")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Pi.an_unpriced_budget_cap_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
A per-run budget cap the provisional price table cannot price is refused naming `maxBudget`: a
cap that could never stop the run is not accepted (ADR-0074 D7, shared by ADR-0081).

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant} {b t w : String}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.connectors = [] → r.budgetCap = false → r.gateway = some (b, t, w) → w ≠ "anthropic-messages" → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "wireProtocols")
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Pi.an_unspoken_protocol_is_refused_by_name
entries.docstring:
A connection served over any dialect but Anthropic Messages is refused naming
`wireProtocols`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Pi.no_accepted_agent_has_a_connector
entries.docstring:
An accepted compile carries no connector: pi has no MCP client, so no agent with a connector is
ever run on it.

entries.statement: ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.ok c → r.permissions.runCommands = false → ∀ (path : Option String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.guard c "bash" path = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Pi.the_guard_blocks_bash_when_run_commands_is_off
entries.docstring:
Whenever the agent's `runCommands` switch is off, the compiled guard blocks every `bash` call,
whatever it asks for: pi is never told about the tool, and a call the model invents is blocked.

entries.statement: ∀ (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Config) (c : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Ceiling), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.violations e c = [] ↔ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.within e c = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.PolicyCeiling.policy_cannot_widen_iff_within
entries.docstring:
A write is refused exactly when it would widen: `policyWidenings` is empty if and only if every
field of the configuration is within the ceiling.

entries.statement: ∀ (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Config) (c : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Ceiling), (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.violations e c).Nodup ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.violations e c).Sublist (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.keyOrder e)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.PolicyCeiling.violations_name_each_field_once_in_key_order
entries.docstring:
The details name each field once, in C14's key order: the list has no repeats and is a
sublist of the canonical order (permissions in `AGENT_PERMISSION_KEYS` order, the two limits, the
engine, the model, then the distinct tools ascending).

entries.statement: ∀ (b : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score) (r r' : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release) (a : AgentWorkspace.AgentId) (src : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step (some b) r (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op.promote a src AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env.production) = Except.ok r' → ∃ v s, r.pointer a src = some v ∧ r.evals a v = some s ∧ b ≤ s
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Release.promote_requires_gate
entries.docstring:
With a bar set, `promote … production` succeeds only if the promoted version's score is at least
the bar; a version with no score is refused.

entries.statement: ∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release) (a : AgentWorkspace.AgentId) (src dst : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env) (v : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.VersionNo), r.pointer a src = some v → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step none r (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op.promote a src dst) = Except.ok (r.movePointer a dst v)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.Release.promote_without_a_bar_needs_no_evaluation
entries.docstring:
With no bar set, promotion needs no evaluation: whenever the source environment points at a
version, promoting it to any environment succeeds and moves the target's pointer to it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.environment_derives_scope_and_identity
entries.docstring: Compiled subprocess variables include the caller's values and four derived identity values.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.environment_refuses_master_key_in_any_case
entries.docstring: A mixed-case provider master-key variable prevents compilation.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.model_resolution_deployment_applies
entries.docstring:
With no other layer, a configured deployment default on a ready connection resolves at the
deployment layer.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { workspace := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝, deployment := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝ } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.ok AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.workspace AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝ ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { agent := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝, deployment := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝ } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.ok AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.agent AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝ ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { project := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝, deployment := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝ } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.ok AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.project AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.model_resolution_deployment_is_last
entries.docstring:
The deployment default is the last layer: a workspace default, or an agent selection, wins
over it.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { deployment := some (have __src := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝; { connection := __src.connection, defaultConfigured := false }) } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.rejected AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.deployment ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { deployment := some (have __src := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝; { connection := have __src := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝; { connectionId := __src.connectionId, model := __src.model, existsInWorkspace := __src.existsInWorkspace, ready := false, credentialReadable := __src.credentialReadable, discoverySucceeded := __src.discoverySucceeded, modelDiscovered := __src.modelDiscovered }, defaultConfigured := __src.defaultConfigured }) } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.rejected AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.deployment ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { deployment := some (have __src := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝; { connection := have __src := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝; { connectionId := __src.connectionId, model := __src.model, existsInWorkspace := false, ready := __src.ready, credentialReadable := __src.credentialReadable, discoverySucceeded := __src.discoverySucceeded, modelDiscovered := __src.modelDiscovered }, defaultConfigured := __src.defaultConfigured }) } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.rejected AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.deployment
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.model_resolution_deployment_unconfigured_refused
entries.docstring:
A deployment layer with no configured default, an unready connection, or no connection at all
(the agent names none and the workspace has none named `default`) is refused at the deployment
layer, never silently skipped.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { run := some (have __src := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝; { connectionId := __src.connectionId, model := __src.model, existsInWorkspace := __src.existsInWorkspace, ready := false, credentialReadable := __src.credentialReadable, discoverySucceeded := __src.discoverySucceeded, modelDiscovered := __src.modelDiscovered }), workspace := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝ } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.rejected AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.run
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.model_resolution_does_not_fallback
entries.docstring:
The first non-null selection wins; an unready run override is a refusal at run, with no
fallback to the ready workspace default.

data migration could not promise.

says its envelope could not be read.
