entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.patchAcceptsCurrent [("memoryMb", AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.PatchValue.null)] = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.patchAcceptsTarget [("memoryMb", AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.PatchValue.null)] = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.patchAcceptsTarget [("runtimeConnectionId", AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.PatchValue.null)] = true ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.requiredCreateFields.all fun k => !AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.patchAcceptsTarget [(k, AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.PatchValue.null)]) = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.s19ClearableFields.all AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RuntimeProfile.nullableFields.contains = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptConfiguration.s19_target_clears_sizing_but_not_required_fields
entries.docstring:
The S-19 target strictly extends today's `PATCH`: clearing `memoryMb` or `runtimeConnectionId`
is refused today and accepted by the target, while clearing a required field such as `driver` or
`name` stays refused.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptIdentity.me_rules_agree_on_well_formed_principals
entries.docstring:
On every well-formed authenticated principal the current and target `me` rules agree: the
divergence is reachable only by a body the server does not build.

entries.statement: (∀ (m : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.MeResponse), m.acceptedTarget = true → m.acceptedCurrent = true) ∧ ∃ m, m.acceptedCurrent = true ∧ m.acceptedTarget = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptIdentity.me_schema_target_refines_current
entries.docstring:
Every `GET /api/me` body the documented rule accepts, today's schema accepts; today's schema
also accepts an API-key principal with a user id, which the documented rule refuses.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptIdentity.principal_coverage_target_is_satisfiable
entries.docstring:
The target is satisfiable by a realistic state: the witness state of the invariants, where
every membership and every key has its principal.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptIdentity.principal_coverage_target_refines_current
entries.docstring:
Every state the RF-101 target admits, today's schema admits; today's schema also admits a
membership with no principal, which the target refuses.

entries.docstring:
A definition share with a budget cap is consistent today but refused by the Target: no check
ties `budget_cap_usd` to `mode = 'runnable'`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptPublication.current_admits_a_cross_workspace_subject
entries.docstring:
A share of workspace `w1` that names agent `a2` of workspace `w2` is consistent today but
refused by the Target: nothing ties `subject_id` to a subject of the share's own workspace, so the
Target's same-workspace conjunct is what refuses it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptPublication.current_admits_a_dangling_subject
entries.docstring:
A share whose subject id names no row is consistent today but refused by the Target:
`shares.subject_id` is polymorphic text with no foreign key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptPublication.current_admits_a_subject_of_the_wrong_type
entries.docstring:
A share that names an existing agent's id as a session is consistent today but refused by the
Target: nothing ties `subject_id` to the table `subject_type` names.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptPublication.current_admits_an_agent_share_without_mode
entries.docstring:
An agent share without a mode is consistent today but refused by the Target: the database
lets `mode` be `NULL` on an agent share, although the service always writes one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptPublication.target_refines_current
entries.docstring:
Every state the Target reading admits is a state today's schema admits: the Target only adds
constraints.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share), s.wellPublished = true → AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.Target.agentHasMode s.toRow = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.Target.budgetOnlyRunnable s.toRow = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptPublication.well_published_share_meets_the_target_checks
entries.docstring:
A share as the service publishes it meets the two row-local Target checks: it has a mode when
it is an agent share, and a budget only when it is runnable.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ConceptPublication.witness_state_meets_the_target
entries.docstring: The witness state (a runnable agent share of an existing agent) meets the Target.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migratePolicy { discriminant := some ("harness", AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migratedEngine), rest := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.rest✝ } = { discriminant := some ("harness", AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migratedEngine), rest := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.rest✝ }
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.policy_rewrite_invents_no_discriminant
entries.docstring:
A document naming neither key is left for a reader to find rather than given an invented
engine.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.policy_rewrite_is_idempotent
entries.docstring:
The rewrite is idempotent: a document that already states `engine` is left alone, which is what
makes re-running the migration set safe.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migratePolicy { discriminant := none, rest := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.rest✝ } = { discriminant := none, rest := AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.rest✝ }
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.policy_rewrite_leaves_a_null_column
entries.docstring:
A `NULL` policy column stays `NULL`. It means "compile from the permission checkboxes", and an
invented engine there would turn an absent policy into a stored one.

entries.statement: (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.policyCases✝.all fun p => Option.map Prod.fst (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migratePolicy p).discriminant != some "provider" && (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migratePolicy p).rest == p.rest) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.policy_rewrite_leaves_no_provider
entries.docstring:
No document comes out of the rewrite still naming `provider`, and none loses the rest of its
keys.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.policy_rewrite_renames_the_discriminant
entries.docstring:
A policy discriminated by `provider` comes out discriminated by `engine`, carrying the same
value, with every other key untouched.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.session_backfill_establishes_the_pairing
entries.docstring:
The release invariant, after the backfill: `engine IS NULL AND engine_session_id IS NOT NULL`
holds of no post-migration row. This is the acceptance criterion's `SELECT count(*) … = 0`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.session_backfill_is_idempotent
entries.docstring: The backfill is idempotent.

entries.statement: (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.sessionCases✝.all fun s => (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migrateSession s).engine == if (s.engine.isNone && s.engineSessionId.isSome) = true then some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migratedEngine else s.engine) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.session_backfill_pins_exactly_the_identified
entries.docstring:
Every session that already has an engine session id comes out naming the engine that reported
it; a session with no identity comes out unpinned.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.session_backfill_preserves_the_identity
entries.docstring: The backfill never touches the identity itself: it names the engine, it does not mint an id.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.enginePaired { engineSessionId := some "se1", engine := none } = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.enginePaired (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.migrateSession { engineSessionId := some "se1", engine := none }) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.the_backfill_has_something_to_do
entries.docstring:
The invariant did **not** hold before the migration: the third case is exactly the row the
backfill exists for. Without this, the theorem above would be satisfied by a migration that did
nothing at all.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsEngines.the_backfilled_engine_is_in_the_catalogue
entries.docstring: The engine the backfill writes is the one the contracts publish, not a loose string.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.normalise_current_differs_from_target_iff
entries.docstring:
Today's reader and the single-envelope target give different answers on exactly the bodies
that parse as the RBAC `detail` envelope or the bare-code envelope; on every other body, standard
envelopes and refused bodies alike, the two agree.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.normalise_current_diverges_on_legacy_spellings
entries.docstring:
Today's reader and the target diverge exactly on the two legacy spellings: the RBAC `detail`
envelope and the bare-code envelope are read today and refused by the target.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.normalise_target_refines_current
entries.docstring:
The target refines today's reader: every body the single-envelope target reads, today's
`readProblem` reads to the same problem.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.text_trim_is_the_agent_trim
entries.docstring: The shared `trim` is `Agent.jsTrim` on every string.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.text_utf16_length_is_the_agent_length
entries.docstring: The shared UTF-16 length is `Agent.utf16Length` on every string.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.text_whitespace_is_the_phase1_whitespace
entries.docstring:
The shared whitespace predicate is the one `ModelConnection` and `Connector` each define, on
every character.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.uuid_accepts_two_spellings_of_one_id
entries.docstring:
One id has two accepted spellings: the lower- and upper-case forms are both accepted, are
different strings, and name the same UUID.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.uuid_current_accepts_a_non_rfc_variant
entries.docstring:
The v4 target reads the variant nibble too: an id with version `4` but a variant nibble outside
`8`–`b` (here `c`, the reserved Microsoft variant) is accepted today and is not v4 text.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.uuid_current_diverges_from_v4_target
entries.docstring:
Today's rule and the documented v4 rule diverge: the nil UUID, a v7 id and a v1 id are
accepted today although none is v4, and an upper-case v4 id is accepted by both.

entries.statement: ∀ (s : String), AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Identifiers.isUuidV4Target s = true → AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Identifiers.uuidCodec.decode (AgentWorkspace.JValue.str s) = some s ∧ AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Identifiers.isUuid (AgentWorkspace.JValue.str s) = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsFoundation.uuid_v4_target_refines_current
entries.docstring:
Every id of the documented v4 form gets through today's two exported gates unchanged:
`UuidSchema` parses the JSON string to itself and `isUuid` accepts it.

entries.statement: AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Runs.runCost (AgentWorkspace.JValue.obj [("amount", AgentWorkspace.JValue.str "not-money"), ("currency", AgentWorkspace.JValue.str "X"), ("priceTableVersion", AgentWorkspace.JValue.null)]) = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsRuns.decimalCostTarget (AgentWorkspace.JValue.obj [("amount", AgentWorkspace.JValue.str "not-money"), ("currency", AgentWorkspace.JValue.str "X"), ("priceTableVersion", AgentWorkspace.JValue.null)]) = false
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsRuns.current_accepts_non_decimal
entries.docstring: The current cost schema accepts a concrete non-decimal amount.

entries.statement: ∀ (j : AgentWorkspace.JValue), AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsRuns.decimalCostTarget j = true → AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Runs.runCost j = true
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ContractsRuns.target_refines_current
entries.docstring: A decimal-only cost amount narrows the current permissive cost schema.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EngineImages.every_shipped_row_is_installed_exactly_when_the_map_configures_it
entries.docstring:
Under **every** map — the development default, and a production map that also configures
`AGENT_WORKSPACE_RUNTIME_IMAGE_OPENAI_AGENTS` — each shipped engine's catalogue row reports exactly
whether the map configures that engine's image, in registry order. This is the map-generic form of
the two theorems above: it covers the `openai-agents`, `pi` and `mastra` rows in both
configurations, which the development-map hypotheses above leave unstated.

entries.statement: ∀ (images : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.EngineImageMap), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.installed images "claude-agent-sdk" = true → List.find? (fun x => decide (x.fst = "claude-agent-sdk")) (List.map (fun row => (row.id, row.installed)) (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.catalogue (List.map (fun d => { id := d.id }) AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Engines.shippedRegistry) images)) = List.find? (fun x => decide (x.fst = "claude-agent-sdk")) (List.map (fun d => (d.id, d.installed)) AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Engines.shippedRegistry)
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EngineImages.shipped_claude_row_is_installed_through_the_map
entries.docstring:
Under any map that configures `claude-agent-sdk`, the derived catalogue's Claude row agrees with
the shipped registry's: the pre-ENG-09 statement, for the engine it was about, unchanged in
strength.

entries.statement: ∀ (images : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.EngineImageMap), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.installed images "claude-agent-sdk" = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.installed images "openai-agents" = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.installed images "pi" = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.installed images "mastra" = false → List.map (fun row => (row.id, row.installed)) (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EngineImages.catalogue (List.map (fun d => { id := d.id }) AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Engines.shippedRegistry) images) = List.map (fun d => (d.id, d.installed)) AgentWorkspace.Sdk.Engines.shippedRegistry
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EngineImages.shipped_registry_is_installed_through_the_map
entries.docstring:
Under any map that configures `claude-agent-sdk` and — as the development default does —
none of `openai-agents`, `pi` and `mastra`, the catalogue derived from the map agrees with the
shipped registry's ids and `installed` flags.

ENG-09 (#308) added `openai-agents`, ENG-08 (#307) `pi` and ENG-10 (#309) `mastra` to the shipped
registry as not installed, because the development default map configures no image for any of
them; the last three hypotheses are those facts, and the theorem below it keeps the pre-ENG-09
statement about the Claude row under the original single hypothesis.

A fork on an engine that declares `fork: false` is refused rather than narrowed to a fresh
session — which would be a different conversation under the same name.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EnginePortCompile.a_master_key_still_refuses_on_both
entries.docstring: A.11's own refusal is retained exactly: a master key still refuses, on both compiles.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EnginePortCompile.a_real_request_compiles_identically
entries.docstring: A worked witness: the environment every Claude run composes today, compiled both ways.

entries.statement: ∀ (capabilities : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Capabilities) (request : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Request) (projectKey configDir : String), request.policyReadable = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.compileTarget capabilities request projectKey configDir = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.CompileResult.refused AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Refusal.enginePolicyInvalid
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EnginePortCompile.an_unreadable_policy_is_refused
entries.docstring:
A policy arm the adapter cannot read is refused by name, never compiled with a default.

The intended difference, and the direction that matters: a run started with a *default* policy is
a run whose author believes it is narrower than it is.

entries.statement: ∀ (request : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Request) (projectKey configDir : String) (env : List (String × String)), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.compileCurrent request projectKey configDir = some env → env = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.assembledEnv request projectKey configDir
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EnginePortCompile.current_compile_yields_the_assembled_environment
entries.docstring:
The current compile's output, whenever it has one, is the assembled environment.

The assembly is the part that had to survive the move: the request's own entries with the four
derived ones appended last, so a caller cannot set a derived name for itself.

entries.statement: ∀ (capabilities : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Capabilities) (request : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.Request) (projectKey configDir : String) (envTarget envCurrent : List (String × String)), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.compileTarget capabilities request projectKey configDir = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.CompileResult.compiled envTarget → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.compileCurrent request projectKey configDir = some envCurrent → envTarget = envCurrent
entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EnginePortCompile.target_and_current_agree
entries.docstring:
**The refinement.** Wherever both compiles produce an environment, they produce the same one.

That is what "extracted without behaviour change" means for this unit, and it is an equality
rather than a simulation because the computation is the same function at a new address.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EnginePortCompile.target_compile_yields_the_assembled_environment
entries.docstring: The target compile's output, whenever it has one, is the same assembled environment.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EngineToolPolicy.a_stored_policy_with_a_grant_compiles_in_the_documented_order
entries.docstring:
A worked witness, written out rather than quantified: the stored arm first, then the permission
floor, then the read-only grant's denials. The order is the compatibility surface.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EngineToolPolicy.adapter_matches_compose_on_every_case
entries.docstring:
**The refinement.** For every input the platform can compose, the Claude adapter's compiled
tool policy is the policy compose produced before ENG-04b — the same lists, in the same order.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EngineToolPolicy.an_unrestricted_agent_compiles_the_empty_narrowing
entries.docstring:
The vacuity control: an unrestricted agent with no stored policy and no grant compiles to the
empty narrowing, so the theorems above are not satisfied by a model that denies everything.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EngineToolPolicy.the_compose_side_guard_changes_nothing
entries.docstring:
The compose-side legacy guard changes nothing: a request carrying `applyFileGrantPolicy`'s
denials and the same request without them compile to the same options.

That is what makes the guard removable rather than load-bearing, and it is the half of ENG-04b's
"byte-identical" claim that covers a control plane and a runner deployed at different versions.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EngineToolPolicy.the_meet_keeps_the_deny_byte_order
entries.docstring:
The ceiling's meet keeps the deny list's byte order (S2-04c). For every case and every one of
the sixteen permission caps, the met run still compiles in the adapter exactly as compose did, its
deny list still starts with the stored arm's own denials, and every tool the unmet permissions
denied is still denied: the meet only turns switches off.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EngineToolPolicy.the_permission_floor_survives_every_stored_policy
entries.docstring:
A stored policy narrows and never widens: every tool the permission switches deny is still
denied, whatever the stored arm says.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.added_keys_are_tenancy_constraints
entries.docstring:
Every key the target adds (no key of today's schema maps onto it) is itself a tenancy
constraint: the target only tightens tenancy.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.checks_diverge_exactly_at
entries.docstring:
The target adds and drops exactly these checks: the model pair on agents, the ledger's provider
set, the transcript key, the SDK session id, three share checks (subject, mode, budget) for the
blank-subject-id check, and the principal kind and source checks respelled with `api-key`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.columns_diverge_exactly_at
entries.docstring:
The target adds and drops exactly these columns: `principal_id` for `user_id` on grants,
`connector_id` for `mcp_server_id` on the two connector links, the inviter's principal, the model
connection's credential, and on shares the owner and the four typed subject columns for the
publisher and the untyped subject id.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.current_identity_breaks_on_an_email_change
entries.docstring:
Today, a browser session keyed by email stops resolving once the user's email changes, although
the user, the membership and the principal are unchanged.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.deleting_a_default_agent_diverges
entries.docstring:
Deleting an agent that is a project's default is refused today (the composite `SET NULL` nulls
`projects.workspace_id`), while the target clears the default and stays consistent.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_a_budget_on_a_definition_share
entries.docstring:
A budget on a definition share is consistent today; the target allows a budget only on a
runnable share.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_a_cross_workspace_subject
entries.docstring:
A share of one workspace whose subject is another workspace's agent is consistent today; in
the target the subject key is tenant-paired and refuses it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_a_dangling_subject
entries.docstring: A share whose subject does not exist is consistent today; in the target the subject is a key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_a_foreign_sdk_session_id
entries.docstring:
A session whose SDK session id is not its own id is consistent today although the launch path
never records one (it refuses any reported id other than the session id); the target makes that
rule a check.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_a_grant_without_principal
entries.docstring:
A grant held by a member who has no principal is a consistent state today (the grant stores the
user id); in the target the grant has no principal to name.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_a_model_without_connection
entries.docstring:
An agent with a model and no model connection is consistent today; the target enforces the
documented pair.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_a_source_without_principal
entries.docstring:
An API key with no principal is a consistent state today; the target requires one principal
per membership and per API key (RF-101).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_a_transcript_under_another_key
entries.docstring:
A transcript stored under a key other than its workspace id is consistent today; the target
checks that the key is the workspace.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_a_wrongly_typed_subject
entries.docstring:
A share whose subject id names a row of another type is consistent today; in the target each
subject type has its own key.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_an_agent_share_without_mode
entries.docstring: An agent share with no mode is consistent today; the target requires one.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_an_unknown_ledger_provider
entries.docstring:
A ledger row whose provider is outside `MODEL_PROVIDERS` is consistent today; the target closes
the set as `runs.provider` already is.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.diverges_at_an_untyped_runtime_connection
entries.docstring:
A runtime profile naming a plain secret as its runtime connection is consistent today; the
target types the reference (RF-204).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.every_divergence_cell_is_exact
entries.docstring:
Every one-cell divergence is admitted today and breaks exactly its named constraints in the
target.

Every foreign key of today's schema, tenancy constraint or reference to a global table, has
its image among the target's keys.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.every_run_provider_is_a_valid_ledger_provider
entries.docstring:
Every provider today's `runs.provider` accepts is accepted on a ledger row of the target: the
target witness with its ledger row's provider set to any of them breaks no constraint.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.every_tenancy_constraint_is_kept
entries.docstring:
Every tenancy constraint of today's schema has an image in the target with the same tenancy
class: no reference to the tenant root and no tenant-paired or sibling-paired reference is lost.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.keys_added_exactly_at
entries.docstring:
The target adds exactly nine keys: the inviter's principal (paired and sibling), the model
connection's credential, the two `SET NULL` siblings and one subject key per subject type.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.keys_diverge_exactly_at
entries.docstring:
The target changes exactly six keys of today's schema: the grant key (member → principal),
the two connector keys (column rename), the two composite `SET NULL` keys (now `NO ACTION`
beside a sibling) and the share owner key (publisher → owner).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.ledger_providers_are_the_run_providers
entries.docstring:
The target closes the ledger's provider column over exactly the value list today's schema
already enforces on `runs.provider` (`MODEL_PROVIDERS`), on the same column.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.owner_columns_diverge_exactly_at
entries.docstring:
Every owned resource names its owner `owner_principal_id` in the target; today exactly one
table, `shares`, names it otherwise.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.refinement_holds_on_the_witness
entries.docstring:
The witness state of today's schema is consistent, and so is its image: the refinement map
takes a well-formed database of today onto a well-formed target database.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.refinement_keeps_every_row_in_its_workspace
entries.docstring:
The refinement map keeps every row in its workspace: the tenant of each row of the target
state, in order, is the tenant of the row of today's state it comes from.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.resolution_by_id_refines_resolution_by_email
entries.docstring:
Wherever today's email lookup finds a user, today's resolution and the target's resolution by
that user's id give the same principal and role.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.role_claim_carries_no_information
entries.docstring:
Today's session verification accepts only the role claim `owner`, so the claim carries no
information and the target drops it without losing anything.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.set_null_diverges_exactly_at
entries.docstring:
Today exactly two keys carry an `ON DELETE SET NULL` that cannot execute (it would null the
`NOT NULL` `workspace_id` too); the target has none.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.table_names_diverge_exactly_at
entries.docstring:
The target renames exactly the three connector tables, so that "connector" is the concept's
one name.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.target_identity_survives_an_email_change
entries.docstring:
Resolving a browser session by user id never depends on any user's email: it survives an email
change, which today's resolution by email does not.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.target_keeps_the_tenancy_rules
entries.docstring:
The target has no unpaired reference and no undeclared `*_id` column, so today's tenancy test
rules 2 and 3 hold of it as they do of today's schema.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.target_refuses_a_subject_in_another_column
entries.docstring:
An agent share whose subject sits in the session column (the column does not match
`subject_type`) is refused by the target's subject check and by nothing else.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.target_refuses_two_subjects
entries.docstring:
An agent share that also names a skill (two subject columns set, both keys resolving in the
share's workspace) is refused by the target's subject check and by nothing else.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.tenancy_classes_are_unchanged
entries.docstring:
The target classifies every table as today's schema does: the same tenant root, the same two
global identity tables, the same 30 tenant-scoped tables.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.ErSynthesis.value_gate_diverges_exactly_at
entries.docstring:
Today exactly one closed set cannot be inlined into DDL by `oneOf` (the principal kind's
`api_key`); in the target every closed set can.

The server and SDK now agree on lone-CR frame separators once the following bytes resolve
the line ending.

the listed cursor has reached the log's latest id.

The repository's first list can see event 1, then a concurrent append and terminal transition
can produce event 2 before its separate run read. The final drain now delivers both events, so
the current and target exit decisions agree with the in-memory exit test.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.EventsSse.status_frame_sdk_roundtrip
entries.docstring: The server's durable status frame round-trips through the SDK parser with its cursor.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.GatewayIngress.an_anthropic_response_without_usage_still_fails
entries.docstring:
An Anthropic response carrying no usage at all still settles as a failure, exactly as it did
before the gateway spoke three dialects — **including** the shape every real one has, which ends in
`message_stop` (or is a non-streaming `type: "message"` body) and so reports itself complete. The
`unavailable` outcome is new behaviour for the two OpenAI dialects, not a change to this one.

On `/v1/messages` the target decision is the current one, for every request: adding two dialects

different rule: every name the closed list still admits the prefix admitted too, and the names the

reach the upstream than before; none that did not reach it now does.

entries.docstring:
**A migrated stream is resumable**: reading the stream the migration wrote answers exactly the
history the old `load()` answered, rather than `none`.

`none` and `some []` and `some history` are three different answers here and only the third is a
resume, so the refinement has to say which one a migrated session gets.

entries.docstring:
**A session the store has no stream for is served from the legacy tables**, folded the way the
old `load()` folded them — a pre-ENG-06 session keeps its history whether or not 0027 reached it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.SessionStateMigration.migration_preserves_the_history
entries.docstring:
**The migration preserves every entry, its order and its key.**

Stated as an equality of the two folds, which is exactly the three claims at once: the same list
means the same entries (payloads), in the same positions, carrying the same `Entry.key`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Refinement.SessionStateMigration.the_main_transcript_lands_under_the_project_key
entries.docstring:
**The stream a Claude transcript lands in is named by its own key.**

The other half of "the same history": a migration that preserved every entry and put it under a key
nothing looks up would satisfy the theorem above and lose the conversation. The Claude adapter reads
`projectKey + '/' + subpath`, and the main transcript's subpath is the empty string.

entries.docstring:
**The migration does not change what the public read answers.** Before 0027 the store is empty
and the read falls back to the legacy fold; after it, the store holds the migrated stream and the
read serves it — and the two answers are the same list.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.AgentFrames.decode_refuses_what_the_contract_refuses
entries.docstring:
The parser is exactly as strict as the contract on the closed fields: a `role`, a delta `block`, a
tool `status` outside their enums, a negative or non-numeric `engineCostUsd`, and an empty string
where the contract says `min(1)` are all refused. Without this, the round-trip above would hold over
payloads the real parser rejects and prove less than it reads as proving.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.AgentFrames.engine_message_fans_out_in_order
entries.docstring:
**One engine message fans out in order** (successor of `agent_event_fanout_order`).

The message frame comes first with its prose blocks in the model's order, then one call frame per
`tool_use` block in the order the blocks appeared; a block with no neutral meaning (the image) adds
no frame. Served from a stored row, the frames take sub-indices `0, 1, 2` in exactly that order, and
the ids are strictly increasing. `Invariants/AgentFrames.lean`'s
`served_frames_keep_emission_order` is the same statement for every row.

And for every message, not only that one: each frame it maps to carries the same capped message
as its `raw`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.AgentFrames.frame_codec_round_trips
entries.docstring:
The frame codec round-trips: a frame encoded with its engine and its engine-native payload
decodes back to exactly that engine, that payload and that frame.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.AgentFrames.frame_names_are_legal_sse_names
entries.docstring:
Every frame name is a legal SSE `event:` name, and none of them is `error`.

SSE has no escaping, so a name outside the grammar could terminate the field and inject a frame; and
HTML §9.2 dispatches `event: error` into `EventSource`'s own transport-error listener, where a
client's watchdog swallows it.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.AgentFrames.frames_cover_the_vocabulary
entries.docstring:
The model's frame names are the contract's, in the contract's order, and the witnesses cover
every one of them.

The neutral vocabulary and the pre-ENG-03 relayed vocabulary are disjoint.

This is what lets the event-read path decide, from a stored row's name alone, whether the row must be
upgraded — a positive membership test rather than a guess about the payload's shape.

`result_preserves_accounting_and_raw`).

entries.docstring:
**A `result` with no readable subtype never claims success** (successor of
`missing_result_subtype_is_provider`).

know is a result whose stop reason is `error`. `end_turn` is reachable from `success` alone.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.ConceptWork.decimal_text_edge_cases
entries.docstring:
The decimal reading of `numeric(14, 6)` text agrees with PostgreSQL on the cases the `runs`
and `run_usage_records` checks turn on: every spelling of zero is zero and `≥ 0`, a nonzero amount
is not zero, a negative nonzero amount is a decimal but not `≥ 0`, a positive amount is `≥ 0`, and
text that is not a rendered `numeric` (an exponent, a bare or doubled sign, a missing digit on
either side of the point, a `+`, a space) is not a decimal at all.

`SDK_WINDOWS_DEVICE_NAME` matches the reserved names in any case and nothing longer or
shorter: `con`, `PRN`, `Aux`, `nul`, `com0`…`COM9`, `lpt0`…`LPT9`, but not `con1`, `com10`,

The work constraints are jointly satisfiable, and not only by an empty database: the witness
state is consistent under every constraint of the catalogue and every refined check, has a row in
every work table, and uses every one of the cluster's 41 foreign keys.

The work tables declare 41 foreign keys: 29 whose every column is `NOT NULL` and 12 with a
nullable column.

The engine vocabulary and the **model** provider vocabulary share no spelling, so no field can
be read as either. This is the whole reason ADR-0065 gave the engine its own field name.

another order would satisfy every round-trip above and still break a consumer that reads
`ENGINE_IDS[0]`.

and `2⁵³` refused at the top, `-(2⁵³ − 1)` accepted and `-2⁵³` refused at the bottom;

integer `1`.

missing seconds field, a space for `T` and a trailing newline are refused.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.ErCore.safe_value_boundaries
entries.docstring:
`SAFE_VALUE` at its edges: a trailing hyphen, a double hyphen, a leading digit or hyphen, an
underscore and the empty string are refused; single hyphens between runs of letters and digits,
and a one-letter value, are accepted.

entries.docstring:
The decision is total over the protocol × family product: every one of the fifteen cells is
either a forward or a refusal, and never both.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.declared_refusal_codes_are_non_empty
entries.docstring: No declared refusal code is blank, so a client always has something to branch on.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.empty_frames_measure_zero
entries.docstring: Nothing observed measures nothing: three extractors, one zero.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.every_protocol_has_one_route
entries.docstring: Every wire protocol is reachable through exactly one route.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.every_refusal_carries_a_declared_code
entries.docstring:
Every refusal carries a non-empty code drawn from the declared list, whatever the request: a
request is either forwarded or refused with something a client can branch on.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.exactly_two_protocols_are_relayed
entries.docstring: Exactly the two OpenAI dialects are relayed; Anthropic Messages is translated.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.exactly_two_tool_types_are_relayable
entries.docstring: Exactly two of the ten tool types are relayed, so eight fail closed.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.ingressRefusalCodes
entries.docstring:
The stable codes the ingress decision can refuse with: the seven `authenticateGatewayRequest`
already publishes, plus the four this unit adds.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.metered_routes_name_distinct_protocols
entries.docstring: Exactly three routes carry a model turn, and each names a different dialect.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.refusal_carries_no_upstream_request
entries.docstring:
A forwarded request is the only shape that carries an upstream request; a refusal carries
none, so nothing can be read out of a refusal by mistake.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.route_paths_are_distinct
entries.docstring: The six routes of spec §9 have six distinct paths.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.GatewayIngress.route_table_is_the_spec_contract
entries.docstring: The route table is exactly §9's fenced block, in the order the specification prints it.

three dialects are reachable and named.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Theorems.WellFormed.RunCompose.no_permissions_deny_every_named_tool
entries.docstring:
Disabling every agent permission denies each named SDK tool group.

ENG-04b (#325) moved the table this cites. It was `apps/web/server/compose/run-request.ts`'s
`toolPolicyFor`; it is now `packages/contracts/src/agents.ts`' `claudeDeniedToolsFor`, which both the
Claude adapter's compile and `GET /api/agents/:id/policy` read — one spelling of one security
decision. The mapping itself is unchanged, which is what
`Theorems/Refinement/EngineToolPolicy.lean` states.

The triple is composed by two modules since ENG-04b (#325): `sandboxFor` answers the sandbox root
and the tenant namespace, and the engine's own adapter derives the configuration directory from the
first of them (`claudeSessionScope`). The string is the same one compose used to send.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.Sample.state
entries.docstring:
Two workspaces, two users; `u1` owns `w1` and `w2`, `u2` is a Viewer of `w1`; each membership
has its principal; in `w1` a secret, a model connection, a runtime profile, a project, an agent
that uses all three and has one version pointed at the `local` environment (one recorded move), two files (a folder and a file in it), a skill, a remote connector
authenticated by the secret and a `stdio` connector; the agent is assigned the file, the skill and
the remote connector, and granted to `u2`; the project links the file and the connector; `w2` has
an agent of its own.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.Target.agentHasMode
entries.docstring: Proposed `shares_agent_has_mode`: an agent share has a mode (the service always writes one).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.Target.budgetOnlyRunnable
entries.docstring:
Proposed `shares_budget_only_runnable`: only a runnable share has a budget cap (the contract
says `null` unless the share is a runnable agent).

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Publication.Target.subjectResolves
entries.docstring:
The subject a share names exists in the share's own workspace: a row of the subject type's
table with `id = subject_id` and the same `workspace_id`.

entries.name: AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Work.AuditEvent.wellFormed
entries.docstring:
The three checks of `audit_events` that are not closed sets: both labels non-blank, and a
recorded subject id has the canonical UUID shape.
